translation: Say, O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all — He in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words; and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Muhammad’s mission is universal—addressed to all humanity—and derives its authority from God’s sovereign control over life, death, and the cosmos. Calling him the “unlettered” prophet points to the authenticity of his revelation (not learned from previous scriptures or human training) while noting his firm belief in God and divine speech. The practical demand is clear: genuine guidance comes through faith in God together with acceptance of and obedience to the Prophet’s message; following him is presented as the means by which people are brought onto the right path.

translation: And among the people of Moses was a community who guided by the truth and by it established justice.
interpretation: The verse affirms that within the Israelites there remained a faithful group who actively transmitted and lived by divine guidance; their adherence to the truth did not remain theoretical but produced just, equitable action. It teaches that genuine guidance is measured by its capacity to correct wrongs and establish fairness, and that in every community a committed minority can preserve the prophetic way by embodying truth and enforcing justice.

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes as peoples. And We revealed to Moses, when his people asked him for water, "Strike the rock with your staff," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs; each people knew its drinking place. And We made the clouds a shade for them and sent down to them manna and quails: "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you." They did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s miraculous provisions and the social ordering of a community (here, the twelve tribes) are acts of divine care that distribute sustenance and identity fairly; the wonders (water from the rock, cloud-shade, manna and quails) are signs intended both to meet needs and to shape responsibility. The closing clause—'They did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves'—emphasizes human moral agency: divine favors do not negate accountability, and failure, ingratitude or rebellion turn blessings into opportunities wasted, making people culpable for the harm they bring upon their own souls and communal life.

translation: And when it was said to them, “Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you will, and say, ‘Ḥaṭṭa’ (an entreaty for pardon), and enter the gate prostrating,’ We will forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good [in reward].
interpretation: God is offering a conditional promise: sincere repentance expressed by invoking pardon (the terse formula “ḥaṭṭa”), combined with humble submission (entering the gate in prostration) and continued righteous conduct, opens the door to divine forgiveness and not merely cessation of penalty but an increase in favor for those who persist in goodness. The verse teaches that forgiveness is attained through inner contrition and outward acts of humility and obedience, and that true repentance is accompanied by ongoing virtuous behavior which attracts additional divine bounty.

translation: But those among them who did wrong changed the words that had been said to them for other words; so We sent upon them a scourge from the sky because of the wrongs they were committing.
interpretation: The verse condemns a people entrusted with divine guidance who, out of self‑interest or corruption, deliberately altered or substituted the revealed instructions. Their distortion of the truth broke the covenant and produced social injustice, and God’s response—described as a scourge from the heavens—serves as both punitive retribution and a corrective sign. The underlying lesson is that tampering with divine guidance and persisting in wrongdoing leads to collective consequences; preservation and honest transmission of the message, and just conduct in accordance with it, are morally and communally essential.

translation: Ask them about the town that lay by the sea — when they transgressed regarding the Sabbath: when their fish came to them on their Sabbath as an appointed provision, and on the day when they did not observe the Sabbath they did not come. Thus We tested them because of what they used to do of defiance.
interpretation: The verse recounts a historical episode used as a moral example: God set a communal test by arranging that fish would be easily available on the ritual Sabbath and absent on other days. The people, instead of accepting the law’s spirit, sought to evade it by contrivance (for example, catching fish before the Sabbath and claiming they had been provided on the Sabbath), thus observing only the letter while violating the law’s intent. Their behavior revealed hypocrisy and deliberate disobedience, so God made the pattern of provision itself into a trial and consequence. The underlying lesson is that divine guidance demands sincere obedience to both the substance and the spirit of commands; seeking loopholes or pretending compliance while acting contrary to God’s will renders one liable to test and reproof.

translation:
وَإِذْ قَالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْهُمْ أَلَا تَعْظُونَ قَوْمًا ۖ ٱللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا ۖ قَالُوا مَعْذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ
"And when a community among them said, ‘Why do you not admonish a people whom Allah will destroy or punish with a severe punishment?’ They said, ‘It is an excuse before your Lord; perhaps they will become conscious (of Him).’"
interpretation: The speakers object to merely warning the sinful people and expect decisive, visible punishment; the responders explain that admonition is intentionally offered as an ‘‘excuse’’ or record before God — they have fulfilled their duty to warn and will answer to God for it — and they continue to warn in the hope that those people may repent and develop taqwa. The verse emphasizes leaving ultimate judgment to God, carrying out the prophetic duty of admonition rather than taking matters into one’s own hands, and relying on sincere warning as the means that might awaken conscience and reform.

translation:
فَلَمَّا نَسُوا مَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ أَنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوءِ وَأَخَذْنَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ بِمَا كَانُوا يُفْسِقُونَ
"So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We delivered those who forbade evil, and We seized the wrongdoers with a wretched punishment for the wickedness they used to commit."
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine justice ultimately vindicates those who actively uphold moral order and admonition. When a community turns away and forgets the warnings and reminders given to them, God preserves and rescues the sincere people who oppose wrongdoing, while He punishes the persistent transgressors for their blatant disobedience. The contrast underscores that remembrance and action in line with guidance bring protection by God, whereas neglect and habitual sininevitably bring a severe retribution ordained by God.

translation: So when they persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them, “Be apes, despised.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that willful, repeated transgression of an explicit divine command leads to a pronounced degradation inflicted by God: those who obstinately rejected the prohibition were reduced to a humiliating state — described as “apes, despised” — which signifies both a punitive loss of honor and a loss of the moral reason and dignity that distinguish humans. It is a warning that persistent defiance brings spiritual and social degradation and the withdrawal of God’s favor.

translation: “And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send upon them — until the Day of Resurrection — those who would make them taste the worst of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment; and indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that God may enforce moral consequences by raising against a people worldly agents or recurring trials that inflict severe suffering as a reaction to persistent wrongdoing; such chastisement can continue across time (“until the Day of Resurrection”) as long as the cause remains. At the same time the passage balances deterrence and hope: God’s retribution is real and can be swift, yet it is not absolute—His nature also embraces forgiveness and mercy for those who return to Him. Thus the verse functions both as a warning that persistent injustice invites sustained consequences enacted through history, and as an encouragement that repentance can remove or avert those consequences because Divine mercy accompanies Divine justice.

translation: And We divided them upon the earth into nations; among them are the righteous and among them are less than that. And We tested them with good and evil so that perhaps they might return.
interpretation: God is explaining that human communities are dispersed across the earth with varying moral conditions not as arbitrary fate but as part of a purposeful arrangement: people are given differing circumstances and capacities, and through both blessings and hardships they are tested. These trials reveal true character and provide opportunities for moral correction — the contrasts among peoples are the result of their responses to tests, and the aim of sending ease and difficulty alike is to awaken conscience and prompt repentance and return to obedience to God.

translation: Then came after them a later generation who inherited the Book; they take the paltry gains of this world and say, “It will be forgiven us.” And if a similar gain were to come to them, they would take it. Was it not required of them by the covenant of the Book that they should say of God nothing but the truth? Yet they study what is in it (to suit their desires). And the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who are God‑fearing. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse censures communities who, though inheritors of divine scripture, sacrifice spiritual integrity for minor worldly advantage: they repeatedly seize small gains while placating themselves with the hope of divine forgiveness, and they manipulate the Book—selecting, studying, or twisting its contents—to justify their choices instead of upholding the covenant to speak truthfully about God. The passage contrasts transient worldly benefit with the superior, lasting reward of the Hereafter for the God‑fearing and calls on listeners to employ reason and conscience rather than excuse or rationalize behavior that betrays their religious responsibility.

translation: And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer — indeed, We will not allow the reward of the reformers to be lost.
interpretation: The verse assures that clinging to divine guidance (the Scripture) and maintaining regular prayer, coupled with sincere efforts to reform oneself and others, will not be wasted: God preserves, accepts, and ultimately rewards such righteous striving — protecting believers from misguidance and granting them their due recompense.

translation: “And (remember) when We drew the mountain over them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them — ‘Take firmly what We have given you, and remember what is in it so that you may be conscious (of Allah).’”
interpretation: The scene of the mountain held over the people conveys the gravity and solemnity of receiving God’s law: it was made overwhelmingly clear so they could not feign ignorance. The command “take it with firmness” therefore means not merely to acknowledge the revelation verbally but to accept and implement it decisively and responsibly. “Remember what is in it” directs continuous study, reflection, and internalization of the guidance so that it shapes conduct and produces taqwa (God‑consciousness). Implicitly this rebukes casual, selective, or superficial adherence to divine instruction and warns that the covenant requires wholehearted commitment and lived obedience.

translation: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam—from their loins—their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Yes, we bear witness.” [This was] so that you would not say on the Day of Resurrection, “Indeed, we were unaware of this.”
interpretation: The verse refers to the primordial covenant (al‑mithāq) in which God implanted an innate recognition of His lordship within human nature (the fitrah). It teaches that awareness of God is a fundamental part of the human condition, so that on the Day of Judgment a blanket plea of total ignorance is not acceptable; moral accountability is grounded in this original disposition, while ensuing guidance or error results from human choices and external influences rather than an absolute absence of awareness.

translation:
أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم ۖ أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون
“Or do you say, ‘Our fathers were polytheists before, and we are merely their descendants after them — will You destroy us for what the former wrongdoers did?’”
interpretation: This verse records a common objection: people appeal to ancestral precedent to evade responsibility for belief and conduct, implying that inherited error should excuse them from punishment. The Qur’anic response implied here is that moral and religious responsibility is individual and based on one’s own choices: God is just and does not doom people for their forefathers’ sins, yet those who knowingly persist in the same corrupt path after guidance has come become culpable. Thus invoking lineage as a defense neither absolves one nor nullifies the requirement to accept truth and reform; continuing in the way of the “former wrongdoers” brings the same consequences because of one’s present assent and conduct.

translation: And thus We make the signs clear, so that perhaps they may return.
interpretation: God deliberately presents His revelations and evidences in clear and varied ways so that those who were previously heedless or mistaken can, upon recognizing the unmistakable guidance, choose to repent and reorient their lives toward right belief and conduct; the clarity of the signs is meant to enable sincere return rather than compel it.

translation: And relate to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he withdrew himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who go astray.
interpretation: Divine favor or access to signs is not an automatic safeguard: when a person strips themselves of that guidance—by pride, negligence, selective obedience, or deliberate rejection—that spiritual vacancy is seized by Satan through temptation, deceit, and self‑justification, and the person is gradually led into persistent error. The passage warns that guidance must be actively preserved in belief and conduct; abandoning it becomes the pathway by which one falls into misguidance and incurs greater moral responsibility.

translation: Had We willed, We could have raised him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire. So his likeness is like that of a dog: if you drive it away it pants, and if you leave it it pants. That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s guidance (here represented by the revelation) can elevate a person, but elevation requires the person’s assent and turning away from low, worldly attachments. “He clung to the earth and followed his desire” describes a settled preference for base inclinations and worldly comforts that blocks inward movement toward God. The simile of the dog—panting whether driven off or left alone—illustrates spiritual stagnation and fruitless craving: the person remains restless and unchanged despite warnings or neglect, showing insensitivity to signs and no genuine response to guidance. By comparing such people to this useless, unresponsive condition, the passage warns that refusal of truth brings a kind of moral and spiritual debasement, and it urges the telling of prophetic stories as a means to awaken reflection in those who might yet turn.

translation:
سَاءَ مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَأَنفُسَهُمْ كَانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ
"Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and thereby wronged themselves."
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejecting God's revelations is self-destructive: those who deny the signs do not merely oppose truth outwardly but commit injustice against their own souls. Their denial corrupts their moral and spiritual state, makes them a bad precedent for others, and thus stands as a warning that turning away from guidance leads to ruin and self-inflicted loss.

translation: Whomever Allah guides — he is the rightly guided; and whomever He sends astray — those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true guidance is ultimately a gift from God: those who receive it are led to truth, upright conduct and success, while those whom God allows to go astray are the ones who suffer loss. This does not remove human responsibility; rather, divine guidance typically accompanies sincere seeking, humility and acceptance of truth, whereas persistent rejection, heedlessness and sinful choices render one liable to misguidance and its spiritual consequences.

translation: And We have certainly destined for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts by which they do not understand, and they have eyes by which they do not see, and they have ears by which they do not hear. They are like cattle; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse warns that many among people and jinn, by their persistent rejection of guidance, are headed for Hell. The reference to hearts, eyes, and ears is not merely physical but denotes faculties of understanding, perception and sincere attention: though these faculties exist, they are not used to comprehend signs, to see truth, or to listen to guidance. Calling them “like cattle” stresses their moral and intellectual failure to exercise reason and conscience; saying they are “more astray” underscores that deliberate heedlessness is worse than animal instinct because it involves squandering the higher gifts God gave. The passage therefore indicts willful neglect and hardness of heart—those who habitually close themselves to truth despite clear signs and opportunities, and so render themselves accountable for the consequences.

translation: To Allah belong the most beautiful names; so call upon Him by them. And leave those who pervert or take liberties with His names — they will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s names are perfect reflections of His attributes, and believers should address and call upon God using those names as a means of correct knowledge, devotion and supplication. It also instructs restraint toward people who ‘لحدوا’ in His names — i.e., those who twist, trivialize, deny, or attribute improper meanings to God’s attributes — advising to leave them rather than be drawn into fruitless argument, for accountability for such distortion rests with God and He will recompense them for their actions.

translation: And among those We have created is a community who guide by the truth and by it establish justice.
interpretation: This verse points to a segment of humanity specially endowed to lead others: they call people with what is true — divine guidance and sound moral discernment — and they use that same truth as the standard for judging and acting. The emphasis is that guidance and justice are inseparable: genuine leadership must be rooted in truth, and decisions must be measured against that truth rather than personal whims, tribal loyalties, or self-interest. Such people serve as exemplars who transmit guidance honestly and apply it impartially, showing that faithfulness to revealed truth necessarily leads to fair conduct and social equity.

translation:
والذين كذبوا بآياتنا سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون
"And those who denied Our signs — We will lead them on, little by little, from ways they do not know."
interpretation: The verse means that when people persistently reject God's revelations, He permits them a gradual slide into deeper error and self-deception — giving them respite and apparent ease while their misguidance increasingly isolates them — until their downfall arrives unexpectedly from directions they never perceived.

translation:
وَأَمْلِي لَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ
"Grant them respite; indeed, My plan is firm."
interpretation: The phrase teaches that apparent delays in divine justice are intentional and part of God's sovereign strategy: the respite given to wrongdoers is not impotence but a deliberate measure within a secure, unassailable plan. It reassures the patient and oppressed that ultimate vindication and the defeat of schemers are certain, timed according to divine wisdom rather than human expectation.

translation: Do they not reflect? There is no jinn with their companion; he is nothing but a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse challenges people to think: the messenger is not accompanied or inspired by a jinn, nor is he bewitched or deluded. Rather, his role is straightforward—to warn openly and plainly about divine truth and coming accountability. This rejects accusations that the message is supernatural trickery and directs attention to the content and purpose of the warning: a rational, observable summons to heed the signs, reform, and prepare for the consequences outlined by God.

translation: أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا فِي مُلْكِ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ وَأَنَّ عَسَى أَن يَكُونَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ أَجَلُهُمْ ۖ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ
interpretation: الآية توبيخ للتكذيب الناجم عن غفلة القلب: تدعو إلى تدبر ملك الله في السماوات والأرض كدليل واضح على قدرته وحكمته، وتذكر أن أجل الإنسان قد يكون قريبًا، فلو أن هذه البراهين الجلية والواقع المهيب لا تهدي المنكرين إلى الإيمان فلا دليل بعد ذلك سيقنعهم. المقصود تشديد على ضرورة التأمل والاعتبار والجاهزية للآخرة، وإظهار أن المكابرة ليست مسألة نقص دلائل بل نقص قبول القلب.

translation:
من يضلل الله فلا هادي له ۚ ويذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون
"Whoever Allah causes to stray—there is no guide for him; and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly."
interpretation: The verse indicates that when people persistently reject guidance and follow their own rebellious desires, Allah withdraws guidance from them as a consequence: no human or means will be able to lead them back to truth, and they are left to roam in error and excess. This 'leaving' is both a just response to their obstinacy and a divine decree that manifests as moral and intellectual bewilderment—they continue in wrongdoing and confusion because they have closed themselves off to the light of guidance.

translation: They ask you about the Hour: “When will it come to pass?” Say, “Knowledge of it is only with my Lord; none will disclose it at its time except Him. It is a burden upon the heavens and the earth. It will come to you only suddenly.” They ask you as if you were keeping careful watch over it. Say, “Knowledge of it is only with Allah, but most people do not know.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the exact timing of the Last Day is a divine secret reserved to God alone, and that the Prophet’s role is to convey God’s message, not to reveal the unseen. By describing the Hour as heavy upon the heavens and the earth and as coming unexpectedly, the text stresses both its absolute certainty and the wisdom of avoiding complacency or morbid obsession with when it will occur. Questioning the Prophet “as if” he had the knowledge is portrayed as presumptuous; the proper response is humility before God’s hidden wisdom and constant moral readiness, since most people lack true knowledge and must live in awareness of accountability rather than speculation about timings.

translation: Say, “I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm except what Allah wills. And if I knew the unseen, I would have amassed much good, and no evil would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of glad tidings to people who believe.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet’s human dependence on divine will and denies any claim to independent power or knowledge of the unseen. It teaches that control over benefit, harm, and hidden realities belongs to God alone, and that the Messenger’s role is limited to conveying revelation: warning the rejecters and giving glad tidings to those who believe. The passage therefore calls people to trust God’s sovereignty, to recognize the limits of human authority and foresight, and to place their hope and security in following God’s guidance rather than in any human’s ability to guarantee outcomes.

translation: He is the One who created you from a single soul and from it He made its mate so that he might find repose in her. When he covered her she conceived, carrying a light burden and passed through it; then when it grew heavy they both called upon Allah, their Lord, saying, “If You give us from it a righteous [child], we will surely be among the grateful.”
interpretation: The verse affirms human unity and the marital purpose of mutual tranquillity, then uses the couple’s shared turning to God in the difficulty of pregnancy to teach spiritual lessons: offspring, provision and the outcome of life’s trials are gifts from God, so humility and joint supplication are the proper responses. The prayer’s conditional request—not merely for a child, but for a righteous (salih) one and for the ability to be grateful—reorients human desire toward moral and spiritual quality rather than mere possession, and models reliance on divine mercy together as spouses rather than solitary striving.

translation: فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمَا صَالِحًا جَعَلَا لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ فِيمَا آتَاهُمَا ۚ فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
interpretation: The verse criticizes the human tendency to attribute blessings to others alongside God: when God grants good to people, some begin to regard those blessings as coming from or belonging to partners or intermediaries, thereby committing shirk in their gratitude. The final clause affirms God’s absolute transcendence above such false attributions, teaching that true thankfulness and correct belief recognize Allah alone as the sole source and owner of every gift.

translation: Do they ascribe partners to that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of shirk (associating partners with God) presented as a rational challenge: it is absurd to worship or assign divine status to beings or idols that lack the power to create or originate anything, because those very things are themselves contingent, produced creatures. The verse points out the logical and theological contradiction—only the One who brings things into existence has true sovereignty and authority, so devotion to powerless, created entities is mistaken and indefensible.

translation: And they are unable to provide them any aid, nor can they even help themselves.
interpretation: The verse affirms the complete impotence of those relied upon other than God (whether idols, false guardians, or powerless allies): they cannot confer benefit to their followers nor avert harm even from themselves, thereby exposing the futility of putting trust in anything but the One who alone has power to help.

translation: And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is the same for you whether you call them or remain silent.
interpretation: The verse indicates that some people are so settled in their way that no exhortation will alter their choice; the Prophet’s task is to convey the truth, not to compel acceptance, so the emotional and moral responsibility for their rejection lies with them (and ultimately with God’s judgment), not with the one who invites to guidance.

translation: Indeed, those whom you invoke besides God are servants like yourselves. So invoke them; let them respond to you, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse is a direct refutation of idolatry: it describes the deities people worship besides God as created, limited beings—'servants'—no different in essence from humans, and issues a rhetorical challenge to expose their impotence. By inviting the worshippers to call on these figures and demanding they prove their responsiveness, the verse emphasizes that true authority, power, and right to worship belong to God alone; the inability of other deities to answer reveals the emptiness of placing trust or devotion in anything besides Him and shows that such worship is inconsistent with sincere belief.

translation: Have they been given feet by which they walk? Or have they hands by which they seize? Or have they eyes by which they see? Or have they ears by which they hear? Say, “Call upon your partners, then devise your scheme; then do not look toward me.”
interpretation: The verse attacks shirk by pointing out that the alleged 'partners' of God have no real agency or power. By ordering the Prophet to tell the idolaters to invoke their partners and carry out their plots, God exposes the futility of relying on created things: such partners cannot affect outcomes, change divine will, or protect those who depend on them. The passage thus reassures the Prophet against threats and strengthens tawḥīd, affirming that ultimate control, help, and judgment rest only with God while trust in powerless idols is vain.

translation: Indeed, my Protector is Allah, He who has sent down the Book; and He is the Protector (or Ally) of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse affirms that ultimate guardianship and authority rest with God—the Source of revealed guidance—and not with worldly powers or false patrons. Because He is the One who revealed the Book, His protection is active: He guides, upholds, and cares for those who live rightly and submit to His guidance. The statement functions as both reassurance and injunction to place trust and dependence on Allah alone, since true help, preservation, and success for the believers come from His providential care.

translation: And those whom you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: The verse teaches that any beings, idols, or intermediaries that people turn to apart from God are utterly powerless: they have no ability to grant protection, benefit, or rescue to their supplicants, and they cannot even secure their own preservation. The practical implication is that reliance, hope and worship directed toward created things is misplaced; true assistance, sovereignty, and refuge belong solely to God, so believers must place their trust and seeking of help in Him alone rather than in impotent substitutes.

translation: And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you while they do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse points to people whose rejection of truth is internal and willful: although they appear to listen and look, their hearts and minds are sealed so the call to guidance cannot reach or move them. Their outward senses remain, but spiritual perception is absent—caused by arrogance, deliberate refusal, and the consequent sealing of their understanding—so evidence and exhortation fail to produce faith or insight.

translation: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين — Be forgiving, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse prescribes a balanced, wise stance for social conduct: respond to wrongs with pardon rather than revenge, actively promote what is morally good and customary in your community, and refrain from engaging with those whose ignorance leads only to provocation and conflict. It teaches patience and moral leadership—preserve dignity and unity by correcting through constructive guidance while avoiding needless disputes that escalate or corrupt the common good.

translation: And if an evil whisper from Satan should assail you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that whenever Satan plants a subtle prompting—doubt, temptation, anger, despair, or any urge toward wrongdoing—the proper response is an immediate turning to God for protection. Seeking refuge in Allah is not merely a formulaic phrase but an intentional act of reliance and remembrance that breaks the devil’s influence, because Allah truly hears the hidden whispers and knows the condition of the heart and is therefore the one who can guard and restore a believer to sound guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who are conscious of Allah — when a whisper from Satan touches them — remember [their Lord], and behold, they are made to see (clearly).
interpretation: When a fleeting temptation or whisper from Satan assails the God‑conscious, their immediate response is to turn to remembrance of Allah (seeking refuge, dhikr, repentance). That turning disperses the delusion and restores spiritual clarity and discernment, enabling them to recognize and reject the deception rather than remain misled.

translation: And their brothers extend to them support in error, and they do not relent.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in falsehood are not isolated: their companions actively sustain and deepen their misguidance—encouraging, justifying, and materially or morally supporting one another—so that the deviation becomes entrenched and they remain unwilling to desist.

translation: And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, “Why were you not given it?” Say, “I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.” These are clear proofs from your Lord and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who demand extraordinary, on‑demand miracles as a precondition for faith and clarifies the prophet’s role: he is a transmitter of divine revelation, not an inventor of spectacles to satisfy skepticism. The “signs” and the revealed message themselves are described as lucid inner evidences (basa’ir) that serve to guide and to show mercy to those who open their hearts and choose to believe; refusal to accept them is therefore shown to be a moral and spiritual obstinacy rather than a mere lack of visible proof.

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse commands a posture of respectful, attentive listening whenever the Qur'an is recited: silence is not merely outward stillness but an inner humility and readiness to let the divine words penetrate the heart and conscience. By suspending speech, distractions, and pride, listeners make room for understanding, repentance, guidance and spiritual transformation; such receptivity is the means by which God's mercy—in the form of guidance, forgiveness, comfort and communal harmony—is bestowed.

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with fear, and without being loud in speech, in the mornings and the evenings; and do not be among the heedless.
interpretation: The verse enjoins a sustained, inward devotion to God — a quiet, humble mindfulness of Him in the heart carried out regularly at the beginnings and ends of the day. It emphasizes sincerity over show: remembrance should not be ostentatious or merely vocal display but a reverent, self-checking awareness that shapes conduct. By warning against heedlessness, the verse urges believers to keep this inner consciousness active so it prevents negligence and guides ethical behavior.

translation: Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not show arrogance in His worship; they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.
interpretation: “Those who are near your Lord” denotes beings whose intimacy with God removes every trace of pride — classically understood as the angels and, by extension, the inwardly purified servants of God. Their nearness is expressed not in status or self‑importance but in continual humility and active devotion: they constantly sanctify (tasbih) God’s perfection and express total submission through prostration (sujood). The verse teaches that true closeness to God is manifested by the absence of arrogance and by unceasing worshipful recognition of His majesty; aspiring believers attain proximity not by asserting greatness but by humbling themselves, remembering God, and surrendering to His will.

translation:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. يسألونك عن الأنفال ۖ قل: الأنفالُ للهِ وللرسولِ ۖ فاتقوا اللهَ وأصلحوا ذاتَ بينِكم ۖ وأطيعوا اللهَ ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين.
“In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. They ask you about the spoils (al‑anfal). Say: ‘The spoils belong to Allah and to the Messenger.’ So fear Allah, and put your affairs right among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger if you are believers.”
interpretation: This verse affirms that gains obtained in collective struggle (especially spoils of war) are not private property but belong to the community under divine authority, with their use and distribution entrusted to the Messenger as God’s representative. By declaring this, the verse summons believers to two linked obligations: first, taqwa (God‑consciousness) which restrains selfish grabs and ensures justice; second, social rectification — settle disputes, restore harmony, and organize communal affairs according to principles revealed by God and implemented by the Prophet. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is presented as the test and expression of true faith, and the arrangement aims to preserve unity, equity, and the common good rather than individual enrichment.

translation: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble; and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they place their trust.
interpretation: The verse explains that true faith is primarily an inward, responsive condition: hearing God’s name provokes reverent awe and a shaken conscience (not mere ritual formality), the recitation of divine guidance actually nourishes and augments that faith rather than leaving it unchanged, and this inner orientation culminates in tawakkul—placing ultimate reliance on God. These three together mark a heart transformed by awareness of accountability and dependence on God, producing humility, steadfastness, moral restraint, and trust that orients one’s actions rather than passive resignation.

translation: Those who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This phrase characterizes true believers by two inseparable marks: a steadfast, sincere practice of worship (‘establishing prayer’—regular, attentive, and obedient performance of the prayers) and a God‑conscious use of their sustenance (‘spending from what We have provided’). By naming provisions as given by God, the verse frames charity and rightful spending as an expression of gratitude and trust, so that inner devotion is shown outwardly in social responsibility, generosity, and fulfillment of obligations.

translation: Those are the true believers. For them are ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness, and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse teaches that genuine faith is validated and rewarded by God in three complementary ways: spiritual elevation (degrees) indicating increasing nearness, honor, and responsibility before God earned through faith and righteous conduct; divine pardon (forgiveness) which removes guilt and restores the believer’s relational standing with God; and a dignified, generous provision that encompasses not only material sustenance but also inner well‑being, social support, and opportunities to live honorably and fulfill one’s purpose. Together these promised gifts redirect the believer’s hope away from transient worldly signs and toward God’s comprehensive, gracious dispensation of mercy and honor.

translation: Thus your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, and indeed a party of the believers were averse (to it).
interpretation: God is reminding the Prophet that the turning point—his being removed from his home—was a divinely willed and true act, even though some among the faithful disliked or resisted that change. The verse teaches that God’s guidance and decisions may require painful departures or unexpected courses that not everyone will welcome; obedience to the divine purpose and trust in its wisdom take precedence over the preferences of a faction of believers, for opposition by people does not undermine the rightness or necessity of what God ordains.

translation: They dispute with you about the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they look on.
interpretation: The verse likens those who contend with the clear message to people being led to their own destruction while watching it happen: they perceive the truth yet persist in argument and rejection. Their opposition is not earnest seeking but willful resistance that only accelerates their ruin; the image stresses both the futility of arguing against what is manifest and the moral responsibility borne by those who, despite awareness, choose defiance and thereby invite inevitable judgment.

translation: And when Allah promised you one of the two groups that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without the thorn (the weaker/unarmed group) would be yours; but Allah intended to make the truth prevail by His words and to cut off the root of the disbelievers.
interpretation: God fulfilled His promise in a way that served a greater purpose than the believers’ immediate hopes: they preferred an easier, less dangerous gain, but Allah willed a decisive, public confrontation so that the truth would be clearly established and the power and influence of the disbelievers would be uprooted. The verse teaches that divine wisdom may choose what seems harder to achieve a lasting, communal good—vindication of truth and elimination of corrupting power—so believers must trust God’s judgment even when it conflicts with their personal desires.

translation: لِيَحِقَّ الْحَقُّ وَيُبْطَلَ الْبَاطِلُ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ - "So that the truth may prevail and falsehood be abolished, even though the criminals dislike it."
interpretation: This phrase affirms a divine promise and moral certainty: by God's will the reality of guidance, justice and truth will be established and falsehood, corruption and error will be nullified despite the resistance or hatred of wrongdoers. It reassures the faithful that opposition and hostility cannot ultimately obstruct what is right, calling believers to trust in God’s decree and to remain steadfast in upholding truth rather than yielding to the pressures of those who persist in injustice or denial.

translation: When you sought help from your Lord and He answered you, “I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, successive (in ranks),”
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere, collective supplication can summon direct divine intervention: God responds by dispatching overwhelming, orderly support — described here as a thousand angels coming in ranks — which shifts the balance in favor of the believers. The phrase stresses both the magnitude and the disciplined, timely nature of God’s aid; its purpose is to strengthen the faithful, to unsettle their foes, and to show that real victory ultimately comes from God in response to true reliance and prayer, while still presupposing that believers fulfill their duties.

translation: And Allah has made it only as glad tidings and that your hearts might be reassured thereby; and there is no victory except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the divine message (and its promises) is given primarily to comfort and steady believers' hearts: ultimate success and deliverance are not products of human schemes but are granted only by God, whose power and wisdom govern events; therefore true confidence and patience come from trusting God’s support and wisdom rather than relying solely on worldly means.

translation: When He cast over you drowsiness — a security from Him — and sent down upon you from the sky rain to cleanse you thereby and to remove from you the filth of Satan and to bind your hearts and to steady your feet.
interpretation: This verse explains how God actively supported the believers by granting them a calming drowsiness (a divinely sent tranquillity and assurance) and sending rain that served both a physical and spiritual cleansing. The “filth of Satan” refers to fear, doubt, temptation, and demoralizing whisperings; the rain and God’s reassurance removed those corrupting influences, unified and steadied the believers’ hearts, and made their resolve and footsteps firm. In short, God provided inner peace, purification, protection from satanic undermining, cohesion among the faithful, and steadfastness in action.

translation: “When your Lord inspired to the angels: ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip.’”
interpretation: This verse speaks to a specific wartime moment: God promises divine support to the faithful and commands angelic reinforcement, producing fear in the enemy so that the believers can gain decisive advantage. The imperatives to “strike above the necks” and “strike from them every fingertip” are not a universal licence to harm innocents but an emphatic instruction for firm, decisive action against armed opponents in the context of legitimate combat, aimed at breaking the enemy’s capacity to fight. The deeper point is moral and strategic: victory is achieved through God’s assistance combined with resolute, targeted measures to neutralize a hostile fighting force.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger—indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that active opposition to God and His Messenger—manifested as deliberate rejection, public defiance, undermining of prophetic authority or sowing schism—is not a mere difference of opinion but a grave transgression. It emphasizes that such hostility toward divine guidance threatens communal and spiritual order and will be met with serious consequences from Allah; the phrase about God’s severity of punishment functions as both a moral diagnosis of the danger of sedition and a deterrent urging sincere submission and respect for the guidance brought by the Messenger.

translation:
ذلكم فذوقوه وأن للكافرين عذاب النار
"That is for you — so taste it; and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: The verse functions as a stern proclamation of inevitable divine justice: those who persist in denial and wrongdoing will ultimately have to ‘‘taste’’ the consequences they brought upon themselves. The imperative ‘‘taste it’’ stresses that the outcome will be an immediate, undeniable experience, while the explicit mention of the Fire underlines the certainty and seriousness of the punishment reserved for persistent rejection of guidance — serving both as a warning and as affirmation that moral choices carry real, inescapable accountability.

translation: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing in battle, do not turn your backs [in flight].
interpretation: This is a moral and military injunction against cowardice and betrayal: believers are required to maintain discipline, solidarity and resolve when confronted by hostile attack so that the community and its mission are not compromised. By forbidding ‘turning the back’ the verse seeks to preserve collective cohesion, obedience to legitimate command, and trust in God at critical moments; its broader lesson is to face trials and responsibilities steadfastly rather than abandoning them in fear.

translation: And whoever on that Day turns his back to them—except for turning aside to fight or to join a company—has certainly incurred the wrath of Allah, and his abode is Hell; and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: The verse condemns abandoning one’s duty or the community out of cowardice or rejection of the truth: on the Day of reckoning such deliberate turning away (unless for a legitimate tactical reason, like maneuvering in battle or regrouping) is considered a moral failure that earns God’s anger and leads to Hell. It emphasizes that faith and responsibility require standing with truth and collective obligation rather than fleeing from them for fear or selfishness; only bona fide, purposeful movement (not flight from conviction) is excused.

translation: You did not kill them; rather, Allah killed them. And you did not throw when you threw; rather, Allah threw — and that He might test the believers by a good test. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that in moments of apparent human achievement, ultimate agency and efficacy belong to God: the actions of people are real means, but the result — victory, the turning of hearts, the decisive event — is ordained and effected by Allah. The phrase “Allah killed” and “Allah threw” stresses divine sovereignty and support in battle, humbling believers so they attribute success to God, not to their own strength or skill. Calling the event a “good test” indicates that such manifestations of divine help serve to purify, strengthen, and distinguish true faith among believers rather than merely confer worldly advantage. The concluding reminder that Allah is “Hearing, Knowing” underscores that God is fully aware of intentions and inner states and that He judges and rewards accordingly.

translation:
ذلكم — وأن الله موهن كيد الكافرين
"That is so; and Allah undermines (renders weak) the scheming of the disbelievers."
interpretation: God actively frustrates and renders ineffective the plots and conspiracies of those who oppose truth; what may look like powerful, cunning plans are by divine decree nullified, so believers are to trust in God's protection and not be alarmed by the apparent strength of the enemy's machinations.

translation: If you request permission to go forth, then indeed the Victory has already come to you. And if you desist, that is better for you. And if you return (to hostility), We will prepare against you, and your party will not avail you anything, even if it be numerous. And Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: God addresses those who wished to hasten into combat and tells them that what they seek — a decisive triumph — has already been granted, not necessarily by immediate fighting but by the unfolding of events (so patience is appropriate). The verse commends restraint as the wiser course and warns that if people abandon right conduct or break covenant and revert to aggression, God will set consequences in motion; large numbers or alliances will not save them when they act unjustly. Ultimately success depends not on mere force or crowding but on God’s support for the sincere believers, so trust, discipline, and obedience to God’s guidance are decisive.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you are hearing.
interpretation: The verse enjoins immediate, sincere obedience: when God and His Messenger give guidance, believers must not merely appear to listen or let inward resistance and worldly interests turn them away. “Turning away while hearing” denotes hypocrisy, distraction, or refusal to submit; true faith is shown by attentive acceptance and acting on the command even when it is difficult or inconvenient.

translation:
وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ
"And do not be like those who said, 'We hear,' while they do not hear."
interpretation: A warning against hypocrisy and superficial conformity: people who outwardly claim to accept guidance or obey commands yet in fact do not truly listen, internalize, or act on it. The verse calls for sincere attention and wholehearted reception of truth — not mere verbal assent or pretense — so that hearing leads to understanding and practice rather than to self-deception or disobedience.

translation: Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the mute — those who do not use reason.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who, though capable of hearing, speaking and thinking, deliberately close themselves to guidance: they refuse to acknowledge truth, fail to employ intellect and conscience, and thus persist in error and injustice. By calling them the worst of creatures, God reproves the moral and spiritual obstinacy that makes a person harmful to themselves and to others — a condition judged more blameworthy than mere physical incapacity.

translation:
وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ لَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ
And if Allah had known any good in them He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.
interpretation: This affirms that God’s withholding of clearer guidance from certain people stems from His perfect knowledge of their inner disposition: because their hearts are closed, even being given an unmistakable call or evidence would not make them accept it but only cause them to turn away in stubbornness or hypocrisy. The statement removes any implication of Divine negligence—guidance is effective only when the soul is receptive, and persistent aversion places responsibility for rejection squarely on people’s corrupt interiority rather than on God’s providence.

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah interposes between a person and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse urges immediate, sincere obedience to God and the Prophet because their call leads to true spiritual and communal life — faith, moral rectitude and salvation. It also reminds believers that inner conviction is ultimately granted or withheld by God: outward action divorced from a heart directed by God may not attain the life the call promises. Finally, the reminder of being gathered to God grounds the command in accountability: one must seek both external compliance and inward guidance, relying on God to open the heart while answering the call with urgency and humility.

translation: And fear a trial that will not afflict those who have done wrong among you exclusively; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that a test, corruption, or divine chastisement, once it occurs, may spill over and harm the whole community rather than only the sinners. Therefore believers must proactively guard against causes of fitnah—by sincere repentance, upholding justice, correcting wrongdoing, and preserving communal faith and cohesion—because negligence or tacit permission of injustice can bring collective suffering. The reminder that God is “severe in punishment” stresses the seriousness and urgency of preventing and remedying moral and social faults so the community as a whole is not exposed to ruin.

translation: And remember when you were few and weak on the earth, fearing that people might seize you; He sheltered you, supported you with His help, and provided you with good things—perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: The verse is a moral and spiritual reminder: when God rescues a community from weakness by providing protection, victory and lawful sustenance, the fitting response is sincere gratitude — expressed not merely in words but in steadfast faithfulness: obedience to God, unity and discipline within the community, reliance on divine assistance rather than on transient human powers, and the righteous use of God’s blessings to uphold justice and strength. Recalling past vulnerability cultivates humility and dependence on God so believers do not relapse into fear, division, or ingratitude.

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, and do not betray your trusts while you know.
interpretation: The verse forbids treachery in both relation to God’s covenant and to human responsibilities: to “betray Allah and the Messenger” means acting in ways that violate God’s commands, undermine the Prophet’s mission, or subvert the communal covenant entrusted to believers; “betraying your trusts” covers breaking promises, misusing property or office, violating confidences, and breaking treaties. The clause “while you know” stresses moral culpability when such breaches are intentional. In short, true faith requires integrity — faithfully observing obligations to God, to prophetic guidance, and to people, even when it is difficult.

translation: Know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that possessions and family ties function as tests of the heart and conduct: they expose whether a person prioritizes God, fulfills obligations, shares with others, and resists passions, or instead becomes heedless, miserly, arrogant, or overly attached to this world. What is judged is not having wealth or children per se but how one uses them and whether they divert one from righteousness. The assurance of a ‘great reward’ from Allah urges believers to exercise responsible stewardship, moral discipline, and trust in God so that passing the trial yields eternal recompense rather than mere temporal gain.

translation: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah He will grant you a furqan (a clear criterion), and He will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the Lord of immense bounty.
interpretation: When believers cultivate taqwa — a sincere, continual God‑consciousness expressed in reverence, restraint, and obedience — God grants them furqan: the discerning light and guidance that distinguishes truth from falsehood and guides correct action. This inner clarity accompanies spiritual cleansing: God pardons and erases sins as part of His generous favor. The verse teaches that moral vigilance opens the way to divine guidance, ethical discernment, and the merciful removal of wrongs, all flowing from Allah’s great bounty.

translation: And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you. And they planned, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse teaches that apparent human schemes to harm the Prophet or the community are encompassed and overturned by Allah’s sovereign wisdom; God’s ‘planning’ is not deceit but the supreme, just, and all-knowing governance that can turn evil intentions into means of protection, testing, correction, or triumph for the believers. Thus believers are called to trust in God’s providence, remain patient and prudent, and recognise that hostile plots cannot frustrate the ultimate purpose of Divine wisdom.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, “We have heard; if we wished we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: The verse criticizes a dismissive and hypocritical response to divine guidance: people pretend to listen yet reject the message by arrogantly claiming they could produce similar words, while reducing revelation to mere old fables. It exposes both their insolence and self-deception — they refuse to engage with the truths presented, relying on prejudice and empty bravado instead of sincere inquiry or moral accountability.

translation: “And when they said, ‘O Allāh, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.’”
interpretation: The verse reports a scoffing challenge by opponents who, instead of humbly examining the claim, demand a spectacular punitive sign as proof. Their supplication is insincere and defiant—they call for stones from heaven or a visible torment not because they seek truth, but to test, ridicule, or evade sincere submission. Thus the verse exposes their hardness of heart, hypocrisy, and preference for theatrical proof over honest acceptance of guidance.

translation: And Allah would not punish them while you are among them; and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes divine mercy: Allah withholds immediate punishment for a community while the Prophet is present because his guidance, example and intercession restrain and give people the chance to reform; likewise, Allah refrains from chastising them while they are sincerely seeking forgiveness. The meaning conveys that punishment is postponed to allow repentance and change, and that both prophetic presence and genuine tawbah (seeking forgiveness) are effective wards against immediate divine retribution.

translation: And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) despite not being its guardians? The guardians of it are none but the God-fearing, yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who unlawfully claim control over sacred rites and places: blocking access to the Sacred Mosque is an act of injustice and a sign that those in charge lack true moral authority. True custodianship belongs only to the righteous (the muttaqūn), so claiming guardianship without piety and knowledge is illegitimate and deserving of divine accountability. The passage warns that worldly power or inherited privilege cannot substitute for God‑worship, moral integrity, and understanding; many who appear to lead are ignorant of these essentials, and thus their rule is corrupt and subject to God’s judgment.

translation: And their worship at the (Sacred) House was nothing but bleating and clapping. So taste the punishment for that which you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse condemns ritual practice that has lost all inner sincerity: when outward acts of devotion at the Sacred House deteriorate into meaningless sounds and gestures, they become empty imitation rather than true submission. Such formalism, combined with persistent denial of guidance, merits God’s retribution—an admonition that external rites without heartfelt faith are void and will not avert judgment.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [others] from the way of Allah. So they will spend it; then it will be for them a regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve — to Hell they will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when people use their resources to obstruct God’s cause — whether by bribery, propaganda, intimidation, or supporting injustice to keep others from following truth — that investment is ultimately self‑destructive. Their expenditure cannot change divine reality or secure success; it will turn into remorse and loss, bringing defeat in this life (moral and political failure) and final accountability in the Hereafter. The passage warns that material power used against the way of God only accelerates one’s ruin and inevitable gathering to punishment.

translation: ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا فيجعله في جهنم ۚ أولئك هم الخاسرون
interpretation: الآية تبيّن أن الحكم الإلهي في النهاية لا يَخدع بالمظاهر: الله يفرّق بين ما هو فاسد وما هو طاهر من القلوب والأعمال، ويترك الفاسدين متجمعين على حال فسادهم حتى تتجلى حقيقتُهم وتُحصى أعمالهم، فيُجازَوْن جزاءهم في النار. المقصود هو تحذير أن الخسارة الحقيقية على مستوى الآخرة هي لمن ظلّ باطنيًّا وفاسدًا رغم أي تزيين خارجي، وطمأنة بأن العدل الإلهي سيُميّز ويقضي بما يليق بكل حال.

translation:
قُل لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِن يَنتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ ۖ وَإِن يَعُودُوا فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّةُ الْأَوَّلِينَ
"Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, what has gone before will be forgiven them; but if they return [to hostility], then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed."
interpretation: The verse conveys a dual divine stance: mercy paired with warning. It emphasizes that God’s mercy is available — past misdeeds can be pardoned when people sincerely cease their disbelief and hostility — while also reminding that persistent, deliberate rejection carries real consequences, following the established pattern by which earlier communities who persisted in refusal were overtaken by the outcome of their stance. The purpose is to urge repentance through the assurance of pardon and to deter recidivism by pointing to the historical reality of accountability.

translation: And fight them until there is no more fitnah and the religion is wholly for Allah. But if they desist, then indeed Allah is, of what they do, Seeing.
interpretation: The verse authorizes fighting as a limited, purposive response aimed at ending persecution and securing freedom for the practice of religion; it does not endorse forcing belief. The goal is to remove the conditions (fitnah) that prevent people from freely living by and practicing their faith, and the command to fight is conditional and reversible—if the opponents cease their hostile persecution, hostilities must stop—because ultimate judgment of people’s inner states and deeds belongs to God, who observes all actions.

translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector; excellent is the Protector, and excellent is the Helper.
interpretation: When people withdraw their support or oppose you, take comfort and place your trust in God as your true wali — the supreme guardian, ally, and source of help; His protection and assistance surpass any human ally, so rely on Him rather than on those who abandon you.

translation: Know that whatever spoils you acquire — a fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives, and for the orphans, and for the needy, and for the wayfarer — if you have believed in Allah and in that which We revealed to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two forces met. And Allah is powerful over all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divinely sanctioned rule for the distribution of collective gain (historically war booty) so that a portion is reserved for public, religious, and social purposes rather than private enrichment. By assigning one-fifth “for Allah and for the Messenger” and naming vulnerable groups (relatives, orphans, the poor, travellers), the ordinance institutionalizes a mechanism for supporting the community, sustaining the messenger’s mission and leadership, and protecting dependents. The reference to the “Day of Criterion” (the decisive encounter) locates the ruling in the formative moment when the community’s faith and obedience were tested, underlining that such regulations derive from trust in God and in the revelation given to His Messenger. The closing clause (“Allah is able to do all things”) reaffirms divine authority and the moral imperative that collective resources be managed in accordance with God’s justice and wisdom rather than purely personal interest.

translation: (Remember) when you were on the near ridge and they were on the far ridge, and the caravan was lower than you. And had you made an appointment, you would have differed about the time. But that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed — that He might cause to perish whom He was to cause to perish by clear evidence and to give life to whom He was to give life by clear evidence. And indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that what appear as unexpected reversals or coordination failures in human affairs can be instruments of divine wisdom: God allows events to unfold to make manifest people’s true states, separating those whose fate is sealed from those who remain, by clear evidence — so outcomes depend on God’s decree and knowledge rather than on human plotting.

translation: When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have been dismayed and would have disputed about the matter; but Allah preserved you. Indeed He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: God sometimes controls what people perceive—here by limiting the appearance of the enemy in a dream—to shape their communal response and protect unity and morale. If He had revealed a more frightening image, believers would have been overcome by fear and internal disagreement; by moderating the vision He spared them from collapse. The verse thus teaches that divine wisdom governs the information and tests we receive according to what is best for the community, because God alone truly knows the hidden states of hearts and how they will react.

translation: And when He made them appear to you as few in your sight when you met, and made you appear small in their sight—that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed. And to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: The verse indicates that God sometimes alters the perception of parties in a confrontation so that each sees the other in a particular light, not by chance but to bring about a divinely ordained purpose. This perceptual shifting serves to test and purify faith, to curb both arrogance and despair, to expose the true disposition of hearts, and to set the conditions for the fulfillment of God’s predetermined decree. It reminds believers that what appears on the surface is arranged within a wisdom beyond immediate comprehension, and that ultimately every affair is returned to Allah for final judgment and resolution.

translation: O you who have believed, when you meet a group (of the enemy), remain firm and remember Allah often, that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse directs believers that in moments of confrontation or collective trial they must not give way to fear or disorder but hold their ground with resolve; pairing that steadiness with abundant remembrance of God (prayer, reliance, and invocation) steadies the heart, preserves unity and moral clarity, and thereby increases the likelihood of true success — whether in the literal battlefield or in any testing struggle.

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose heart and your strength depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse warns that communal obedience to divine guidance and prophetic leadership is essential for effectiveness and survival: internal disputes—especially at critical moments—sap morale, scatter effort, and lead to practical failure. Instead of arguing and allowing discord to weaken a group, believers are called to exercise restraint and perseverance; patience preserves unity and preparedness, and through such steadfast endurance one attains God’s support and presence.

translation: “And do not be like those who went forth from their homes boastfully and to be seen by people, and who hinder [others] from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.”
interpretation: The verse warns against ostentation and hypocrisy: performing outward acts (leaving home, going into public) for pride or to win people's admiration strips those actions of spiritual worth, and such showy behavior often goes together with obstructing others from Allah’s path (by seeking status, creating division, or distorting guidance for personal gain). The closing phrase reminds that God fully knows and encompasses both inner motives and outward deeds, so true faith requires sincerity, humility, and constructive conduct rather than spectacle and obstruction.

translation: And when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, 'No one will overcome you today among the people, and indeed I am a protector for you.' But when the two parties appeared to each other, he turned back on his heels and said, 'Indeed I am clear of you; indeed I see what you do not see; indeed I fear Allah.' And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse exposes Satan’s method of deception: he glamorizes sinful plans to instill overconfidence, pretending to be an ally and protector so people will act boldly. When the real test comes he abandons them, disclaims responsibility and even feigns piety to avoid blame—revealing his mendacity and cowardice. The warning is that apparent strength or assurance given by Satan is illusory; true support and victory are from Allah alone, and those who follow Satan’s counsel will be deserted at the critical moment and face Allah’s severe punishment.

translation: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, “What is this religion of ours?” — and whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights that open rejection or mockery of the faith often comes from inner spiritual sickness (hypocrisy, doubt, envy) rather than honest inquiry; such objections aim to unsettle the community. The corrective offered is not debate alone but firm reliance on God: true trust in Allah is an active stance of confidence that God’s power and wisdom will protect, judge and guide, so the slanders of the hypocrites cannot overturn the truth or the destiny of the sincere.

translation: If you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve — they strike their faces and their backs, saying, "Taste the punishment of the Blaze!"
interpretation: The verse conveys that at the moment of death the disbeliever experiences humiliation and immediate chastisement: the striking of faces and backs symbolizes forceful, degrading removal of the soul and the loss of dignity, while the command to “taste the punishment of the Blaze” shows that death is the threshold to the just and certain torment reserved for persistent rejection. The vivid imagery emphasizes both the reality and severity of divine consequences that begin with the soul’s departure and manifest the moral outcome of one’s choices.

translation: That is for what your hands have sent before [you]; and Allah is not at all unjust to the servants.
interpretation: The verse affirms divine justice: the harms, losses, or punishments that befall people are consequences of their own actions and choices, and Allah does not wrong His servants—He recompenses each according to what they have earned, even if the timing or manner of that recompense is not immediately apparent.

translation:
كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ: كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
“As with the conduct of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they rejected the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in punishment.”
interpretation: The verse functions as a warning and theological principle: persistent rejection of God’s clear guidance—especially when combined with arrogance, oppression or reliance on worldly power—follows a recurring historical pattern that leads to certain divine accountability. By citing Pharaoh’s example the text emphasizes that no temporal strength can avert God’s justice; the attributes “Powerful” and “Severe in punishment” affirm both Allah’s ability to enforce consequences and the seriousness and inevitability of those consequences for unrepentant disbelief, thereby urging humility, moral responsibility, and timely repentance.

translation: That is because Allah does not change a favour which He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves; and indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches a general moral principle: divine blessings persist so long as a community’s inner condition—its beliefs, intentions and conduct—remains sound. When people corrupt their hearts and actions, the outward benefits they enjoyed are allowed to be altered or removed as a natural consequence of that inner change. This is not arbitrary punishment but the operation of God’s wise governance: He is fully aware of inner states (All‑Knowing) and responsive to causes and appeals (All‑Hearing). Thus responsibility rests with people to reform their intentions and behaviour if they seek the continuance or restoration of God’s favour.

translation: كَذَابٌ كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ وَكَانُوا ظَالِمِينَ
interpretation: The verse functions as a moral and theological warning: the history of Pharaoh and earlier peoples is presented to show that persistent denial of divine guidance combined with injustice and moral corruption brings about divinely permitted consequences. It emphasizes that worldly power and oppression do not exempt a community from accountability; rather, such examples are meant to prompt reflection, repentance, and reform so people abandon arrogance and wrongdoing before similar ruin befalls them.

translation: “Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve; they will not believe.”
interpretation: الآية تستخدم تشبيهًا قويًا ليبيّن أن الكفر، حين يستمر بالعناد والظلم ورفض الهداية، يهبط بصاحبه إلى أدنى المراتب الأخلاقية والروحية؛ وصفهم بـ«شر الدواب» مجازي يبيّن فقدان الكرامة الأخلاقية والقدرة على الانفتاح على الحقيقة، و«فهم لا يؤمنون» تصف حالة قلوبهم المصلّبة وإصرارهم على الجحود وما يترتب على ذلك من عواقب معنوية وآخرية.

translation: Those among them with whom you made a covenant, yet they break their covenant each time and they do not fear (God).
interpretation: The verse warns that formal pledges or treaties are of no moral value when the heart lacks taqwa: people who do not fear God will habitually betray commitments, so true trustworthiness is measured by inner God‑consciousness and not merely by words, with such hypocrisy warranting communal caution and divine accountability.

translation: فَإِنْ أَدْرَكْتُمُوهُمْ فِي الْقِتَالِ فَاشْرُدُوا بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
interpretation: الآية تقدم مبدأ توجيهيًا في سياق القتال: حين يتحقق للمؤمنين التفوق، يُطلب منهم تحطيم تماسك العدو وإفراغ ما وراء الصفوف من قوة ومقاومة بحيث يُفقد العدو قدرته على الاستمرار. الغاية ليست الإبادة العمياء بل إحداث رادع ووجدان يفضي إلى تذكّر العدو وتراجع عدوانه—أي استعمال القوة بصورة تهدف إلى حفظ المجتمع ووقف العدوان وإتاحة فرصة للتوبة والتفكّر بدلاً من الإصرار على العنف.

translation: And if you fear treachery from a people, then cast [the covenant] back to them on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous.
interpretation: The verse lays down a rule of defensive reciprocity: when there are credible signs that a party intends to violate a treaty or commit betrayal, it is permissible to suspend or return obligations proportionately—matching their stance rather than responding with hidden deceit or excessive aggression. It is a safeguard for the community that allows measured, equal responses to anticipated perfidy while making clear that treachery itself is condemned by God.

translation:
وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا ۚ إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ
"And let not those who disbelieve imagine that they have gone ahead; indeed, they will not be able to frustrate [God's decree]."
