translation: And [remember, O Prophet], when you said to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, “Keep your wife and fear Allah,” while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. But when Zayd had concluded from her [i.e., divorced her], We married her to you so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have ceased to be part of them; and ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: The verse reproves yielding to human opinion and explains that Allah’s revelations and commands can purposefully overturn entrenched social assumptions. By making the Prophet’s situation a public legal precedent, God taught that adoptive ties do not create the same legal barriers as blood relations, removed social stigma attached to such marriages, and emphasized that fearing and obeying Allah outweighs concern about people’s perceptions; ultimately it shows that divine wisdom and ordinance supersede private hesitation and are duly carried out.

translation: It was not for the Prophet to be in distress over that which Allah had prescribed for him. That is the way of Allah with those who passed away before. And the command of Allah is a decree determined.
interpretation: The verse affirms that a prophet is required to carry out God’s injunctions without personal hesitation or reproach; when a prophet implements what God commands—even if it appears hard or surprising to people—he is following Allah’s established practice with His messengers, and such actions are expressions of God’s fixed, measured decree. Therefore criticisms of prophetic conduct that ignore the divine mandate are misplaced, and believers are called to trust the wisdom and finality of Allah’s rulings.

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and do not fear anyone except Allah — and Allah is sufficient as an Accountant.
interpretation: The verse commends those who faithfully transmit God’s guidance without seeking approval or fearing reproach from people, maintaining reverent fear and accountability before Allah alone. It teaches that true integrity in conveying truth requires courage to resist human pressure and complete reliance on God as the ultimate judge and disposer, so that one’s motive remains sincere and one’s trust rests in Allah’s reckoning rather than in worldly opinion.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men; rather he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Muhammad’s authority is not derived from biological descent or to establish a hereditary spiritual dynasty among the people; his unique status is that of Allah’s Messenger and the final prophet, signaling the end of prophetic succession by divine decree, and it reminds believers that this determination rests in God’s complete knowledge and wisdom.

translation: O you who believe, remember Allah often and abundantly.
interpretation: A direct command to make remembrance of God a constant, lived practice: not merely occasional ritual but a steady inner and outward attention that keeps the heart aware of God, cultivates gratitude and reliance, restrains heedlessness and sin, and shapes speech and action. The qualification “much” points to regularity, sincerity, and variety of remembrance (silent reflection, tasbih, istighfar, supplication, and mindful awareness in daily deeds) so that a believer’s life is continually oriented toward God and morally strengthened.

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This is an injunction to maintain regular remembrance and praise of God at the two pivotal times of the day—dawn and evening—so that worship, gratitude and recognition of His sovereignty become a continual rhythm in a believer’s life; by sanctifying the start and close of the day one cultivates mindfulness, moral vigilance and reliance on God amid life’s changing circumstances.

translation: He is the One who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [also send blessings], that He may bring you forth from darkness into light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s “salāt” (blessing, grace, and honoring) upon the Prophet and the angels’ invocation are expressions of divine care that secure guidance and support for the community. This heavenly favor operates by confirming the prophetic mission, sending revelation and protection, and by prompting inner transformation so that people are led out of ignorance, moral error, despair or spiritual trial (the ‘darkness’) into faith, understanding, righteous conduct and spiritual clarity (the ‘light’). The concluding phrase emphasizes that this movement is rooted in God’s mercy toward believers: His attention both uplifts and forgives, sustaining their growth and salvation.

translation: Their greeting, when they meet Him, will be: “Peace.” And He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: The word “Peace” as their salutation from God conveys more than a polite greeting: it signifies absolute safety, the removal of fear, regret, and punishment, and divine approval at the moment of meeting the Creator. The “noble reward” is the dignified, enduring recompense prepared by God—an honourable, generous grace (both the pleasures of the Garden and the status of being accepted) that matches their faith and righteous conduct.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet’s mission in a single holistic role: he is appointed to testify to God’s truth—both by proclaiming the revelation and by embodying it—while simultaneously offering hope to those who accept the guidance (glad tidings of God’s mercy and reward) and warning those who reject it of the consequences; through testimony, encouragement, and admonition he aims to guide people to a responsible moral choice for which they will be accountable.

translation: and a caller to Allah by His permission and a shining lamp.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the Prophet as one commissioned by God to invite people to Him (his mission has divine authorization), and as a 'shining lamp'—a guiding, illuminating presence whose message and example dispel spiritual darkness, clarify truth, and lead hearts toward faith and upright conduct.

translation: And give glad tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty.
interpretation: The verse affirms that sincere faith will be met by Allah’s abundant and overflowing grace — not merely limited material gains but a comprehensive favor including forgiveness, spiritual elevation, support in trials, and the ultimate reward in the Hereafter — intended to cultivate hope, patience, and steadfastness by showing that God’s generosity far outweighs any worldly cost.

translation: Do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Leave their harm alone and put your trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse admonishes the Prophet—and by extension sincere believers—not to be guided or swayed by the hostile unbelievers or the inwardly treacherous, and not to be consumed by responding to their insults or schemes. Instead of seeking approval, revenge, or validation from those who oppose the message, one is to entrust the outcome to God: rely on His wisdom, protection and justice. Allah is called the sufficient wali/agent—He alone will manage affairs rightly and vindicate the truth—so believers should preserve their principles, refrain from futile entanglement with malice, and maintain confident reliance on God.

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, there is no waiting period for them that you must observe; so give them a gift and release them graciously.
interpretation: The verse establishes a specific legal and ethical rule: if a marriage contract is ended by divorce before sexual relations occur, the woman is not required to observe an ’iddah (waiting) period, yet the husband remains obliged to provide a fair settlement or gift and to part with her honorably. This both recognizes the binding nature of the marriage contract (so rights and obligations arise) and protects the woman from unnecessary hardship and stigma by removing the waiting restriction when consummation has not taken place, while insisting on dignified, equitable treatment to prevent exploitation.

translation: O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their due and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and maternal aunts who migrated with you, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to contract her marriage — exclusively for you, not for the (other) believing men. We already know what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty upon you. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse grants the Prophet specific marital dispensations that are exceptions to the general rules set for the Muslim community, and it explains the reason and wisdom behind them. Because the Prophet stood in a unique public and representative role — with social, political and communal responsibilities — God allowed for special permissions (including certain relatives who accompanied him and the right to accept a believing woman’s offering of herself exclusively to him) so that the burdens and constraints that apply to ordinary believers would not create hardship for him in carrying out his mission. The clause “We already know what We have enjoined upon them…” signals that these dispensations do not overturn the general law for others but are measured exceptions made with full divine knowledge. The closing reminder that God is Forgiving and Merciful underscores that this specific allowance was given out of divine compassion and wise governance, not arbitrariness, and that God’s law can accommodate particular needs of prophetic responsibility while maintaining justice for the community.

translation: You may keep (as your wife) whom you wish of them and admit to your home whom you wish, and whoever you choose to take back from among those you had set aside, there is no blame on you. That is nearer to calming their eyes so that they do not grieve and are pleased with what you give them of the wealth. And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse allows practical, conciliatory arrangements within a strained marital situation—permitting a husband to retain one spouse, bring another into the household, or reconcile with a previously separated wife—because such flexibility can reduce hurt and restore tranquility. The guidance prioritizes preventing grief and securing the wives’ reasonable material provision, while reminding that outward actions cannot conceal inner motives: only God truly knows hearts and is both fully aware and patient. Thus the command balances pragmatic mercy and social stability with the ethical demand for sincere intention and restraint.

translation: It is not permissible for you (to marry) women after (their husbands), nor to replace them with other wives, even if their beauty pleases you — except those whom your right hands possess. And Allah is, over all things, Watchful.
interpretation: The verse sets a clear legal and moral boundary: one must not take as a spouse a woman who is already bound by marriage to another, nor treat one’s existing wives as disposable by swapping them for others merely because of attraction; the only exception mentioned — “what your right hands possess” — refers to women in the specific historical circumstance of captivity and was a limited allowance within that context. By concluding that Allah is ever Watchful, the verse emphasizes that these rules are divinely ordained to protect marital bonds, preserve women’s rights and family integrity, and that human conduct in these matters will be observed and held accountable by God.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, not waiting for its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse and do not linger for conversation — indeed that used to harm the Prophet, and he felt shy with you; but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask them (his wives) for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed that would be a grave matter with Allah.
interpretation: This verse establishes social and moral boundaries to protect the Prophet’s personal dignity, the privacy of his household, and the emotional integrity of the community. It forbids casual entry into the Prophet’s home except by invitation for a meal (and not to loiter waiting for food), requires guests to leave once they have eaten so as not to burden or distress him, and instructs that requests to his wives be made through a barrier — a measure that preserves modesty and prevents situations that might unsettle hearts or invite scandal. The phrase “Allah is not shy of the truth” underscores that these practical rules, though they touch on intimate matters, are divinely mandated and to be stated plainly for the public good. Finally, the prohibition against harming the Messenger or marrying his wives after him serves to protect his unique status and the sanctity of his household, making clear that certain personal relations and liberties are restricted to uphold communal honor, prevent jealousy or slander, and set a lasting precedent for respectful boundaries between leaders, their households, and the wider community.

translation: If you disclose anything or conceal it, then indeed Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse reminds believers that God’s knowledge encompasses both outward deeds and inner intentions; nothing hidden in the heart or revealed by the tongue is beyond His awareness. This truth nullifies any refuge in hypocrisy or secret wrongdoing and urges inward sincerity and moral responsibility: private good deeds are seen and rewarded, private sins are observed and will be addressed, so one must cultivate purity of intention, reliance on God’s justice, and mindfulness that ultimate judgment rests with Him.

translation: There is no sin upon them concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or the sons of their brothers or the sons of their sisters or their women or those whom their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: The verse indicates that certain close familial and legal relationships entail legitimate relaxations of ordinary restrictions, but it immediately qualifies those allowances with a moral injunction: permissibility does not equal licence. Believers must exercise such permitted interactions with God‑consciousness, restraint and responsibility, because Allah observes all actions and will hold people to account.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and salute him with peace.
interpretation: The prescribed invocation of blessing (salawāt) functions not merely as praise but as a spiritual instrument: by asking God to confer mercy and honor on the Prophet, believers join in the divine act of elevating his rank, express their attachment to his guidance, and thereby align themselves with God's will. The mention of angels shows this is a cosmic reality, not a private sentiment, and the believer’s participation both confirms communal fidelity to the prophetic message and opens a channel for receiving divine mercy and spiritual benefit for the supplicant.

translation: Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger—Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The phrase refers to deliberate attacks—verbal or practical—against God’s authority and the Prophet’s mission (mockery, slander, incitement, or actions that seek to undermine the faith and its community). The verse announces divine rejection and consequent disgrace both socially/psychologically in this life and as retribution in the hereafter; it functions as a stern deterrent to protect the honor, unity, and moral order of the believing community by warning that malicious hostility toward God and His Messenger brings humiliation and punishment.

translation:
وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ بِغَيْرِ مَا اكْتَسَبُوا فَقَدِ احْتَمَلُوا بُهْتَانًا وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا
"As for those who harm believing men and women without any right, they have certainly borne a calumny and a clear sin."
interpretation: The verse condemns any unjust harm toward believers—especially false accusations, slander, malicious gossip, or persecution—by defining such behavior as twofold wrongdoing: an invented charge (baḥtān) that attacks a person’s honor and an evident moral sin. It affirms that reputation and dignity are sacred in the community, that blame must not be laid without just cause and evidence, and that those who fabricate or inflict unjust harm are morally culpable and subject to divine accountability; the passage therefore calls for restraint, verification before accusation, protection of the innocent, and repair (repentance and restitution) where harm has been done.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should draw their jilbābs over themselves. That is more conducive that they will be recognized and not molested. And Allah is Oft‑Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse enjoins a visible outer covering for the Prophet’s wives, his daughters, and believing women as a social safeguard: by adopting a modest external dress they are to be publicly identified as respectable members of the Muslim community, which reduces exposure to harassment and social harm. The command thus serves a protective, communal purpose, and the closing phrase reminds that God’s disposition toward believers is forgiving and merciful.

translation: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and the agitators in the City do not cease, We will surely urge you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors there except for a little.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and reassurance: God promises to curtail the influence of persistent hypocrites, the spiritually diseased, and trouble‑makers within the Muslim community by bringing about circumstances that remove or marginalize them from the city. It affirms divine protection of the community and the Prophet’s authority, and signals that continued subversion of communal unity and faith will lead to loss of standing, exclusion, or expulsion so their harmful presence becomes minimal.

translation:
ملعونين — أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلاً
"Accursed — wherever they are found they are seized and put to death utterly."
interpretation: The verse declares divine condemnation and the inevitable downfall of those who persist in violent rebellion and spreading corruption; it communicates that such entrenched, destructive hostility is met by decisive retribution—both as a manifestation of God’s justice and as a scriptural basis for strong communal measures to remove persistent, violent threats to social order.

translation: This is the way (sunnah) of Allah concerning those who passed away before; and you will not find for the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: The verse declares that Allah’s established pattern—how He deals with peoples who accept or reject His guidance—is constant and unalterable: when communities persist in disbelief and corruption despite clear warning, they face the consequences seen in past nations, and when people respond with faith and perseverance they receive His mercy. It is a warning and reassurance that divine justice and decree follow a fixed, consistent law across history and will not be arbitrarily altered by human desire.

translation: Men ask you about the Hour. Say, “Its knowledge is with Allah alone.” And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the exact time of the Last Hour is known only to God and that humans — even the Prophet — must acknowledge that ignorance. The rhetorical question “What will make you know?” stresses our limited perspective; we should not speculate, predict, or become preoccupied with dating the end. At the same time the warning “Perhaps the Hour is near” imposes urgent moral responsibility: because the Hour could come at any time, believers must live in constant God‑consciousness, prioritize righteous action and repentance, and remain ready rather than distracted by conjecture about signs or timetables.

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse communicates that deliberate, persistent rejection of God’s clear guidance is met with divine disapproval that has real consequences: those who close themselves to truth thereby forfeit God’s favor and are held accountable, facing a just and certain recompense in the Hereafter. The wording stresses both the seriousness of willful disbelief and the certainty and proportionality of divine justice, functioning as a stern warning to reject arrogance and as reassurance that ultimate injustice will not go unaddressed.

translation: They will abide therein forever; they will find neither protector nor helper.
interpretation: This verse affirms the permanence of the recompense for those who persist in rejection and wrongdoing: once the judgment is enacted they will be left utterly without support. Neither human allies, patrons, nor any attempted intercession will be able to shield them from divine justice. The passage thus underscores the finality of consequence and warns against trusting in worldly protections instead of turning to God’s guidance and mercy.

translation: يوم تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ يَقُولُونَ: «يَا لَيْتَنَا أَطَعْنَا اللَّهَ وَأَطَعْنَا الرَّسُولَ»
interpretation: الآية تبرز درسًا أخلاقيًا وتربويًا: لا تفيق النفس إلا عند وقوع الجزاء، فندم المحكوم عليهم في لحظة العذاب يبيّن أن الإيمان والطاعة لا تُقَدَّران بالكلام أو بالتأجيل، بل بالفعل والالتزام في الدنيا. لذلك تحذر الآية من المماطلة وتؤكد أن طاعة الله ورسوله هي سبب النجاة، وأن الندم بعد فوات الأوان لا يغير حكم العدل الإلهي.

translation: And they will say, 'Our Lord, we obeyed our chiefs and our great ones, and they led us astray from the way.'
interpretation: The verse records the futile excuse of those who shift blame to influential leaders for their own wrongdoing. It teaches that following powerful or respected people who deviate from God's guidance does not remove individual moral responsibility; reliance on such leaders can lead one away from the right path, and each person will be held accountable for choosing to obey them rather than obeying divine guidance.

translation: Our Lord, give them twice the punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: A prayer invoking God’s decisive and intensified retribution upon those whose repeated, grave wrongdoing has harmed the community; the plea for “double” punishment and a “great curse” expresses that severe, aggravated transgression warrants an escalated, unmistakable divine response, and it places ultimate justice in God’s hands rather than relying on human vengeance.

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses; Allah cleared him of what they alleged, and he was esteemed in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against participating in slander, malicious opposition, or collective hostility toward the innocent and the righteous. It teaches that spite, envy, and bandwagon cruelty toward a person of truth are disgraceful behavior — God ultimately vindicates the wronged and honors them — so believers must discipline themselves to uphold justice, refrain from spreading false accusations, and trust God’s judgment rather than joining a hostile mob.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words that are upright.
interpretation: The verse ties God-consciousness to moral integrity in speech: true faith must show itself in how one talks — being truthful, clear, just, and beneficial rather than deceitful, abusive, slanderous, ambiguous, or manipulative. "Qawlan sadeedan" means speech that is straight and right in both content and manner — sincere, measured, timely, and aimed at good — because words shape trust, social harmony, and a believer’s standing before God.

translation: He will set right for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger has indeed attained a great success.
interpretation: The verse indicates that sincere submission to God and adherence to the Prophet’s guidance become the means of real moral and spiritual rehabilitation: God transforms intentions and conduct, grants steadiness to perform genuinely righteous actions, and pardons past failings. ‘Great success’ therefore signifies comprehensive deliverance — inner reform, sustained upright behavior, forgiveness, and ultimate well‑being in the sight of God — rather than mere worldly advantage.

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and were apprehensive of it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: The “Trust” (al‑amanah) refers to the moral responsibility God bestowed on human beings — the capacity for free will, knowledge of right and wrong, accountability, and the duty to uphold justice and covenantal obligations. Unlike inert creation, humans were given the power to choose and thus the burden of moral agency; accepting that burden does not guarantee right conduct. The phrase “he was unjust and ignorant” diagnoses the recurring human failure: though entrusted with faculties and duties, people often misuse them through selfishness, oppression, forgetfulness, or heedlessness. The verse therefore explains both why humanity carries immense responsibility and why moral failure occurs — a call to recognize the seriousness of our charge and to strive to fulfill it with humility and justice.

translation:
ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات ۗ وكان الله غفورا رحيما
"[This is] so that Allah may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, and that Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: The verse draws a clear moral distinction based on inner conviction and response to guidance: those who persist in hypocrisy or in associating others with God, having rejected truth and betrayed communal trust, face divine punishment as a just consequence of their choices; by contrast, sincere believers who turn back to God are the recipients of His forgiveness and acceptance. The statement underscores that God’s administration balances justice and mercy — wrongdoers are held accountable, yet God remains forgiving and merciful toward those who truly repent, and forgiveness is granted by His will to those whose hearts genuinely return to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the All‑Aware.
interpretation: The verse asserts God’s absolute ownership of all realms and, by naming Him al‑Hakim (the Wise) and al‑Khabir (the All‑Aware), teaches that every happening and decree has purpose and is fully known to Him; therefore true response is continual praise and trust — in this life and the next — because what may appear puzzling or unjust to us is encompassed by divine wisdom and awareness.

translation: He knows what enters the earth and what comes forth from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute, intimate knowledge and governance of both hidden and apparent movements in the cosmos—what goes into and out of the earth (e.g., seeds, treasures, the dead) and what comes down from the heavens and rises within them (e.g., rain, angels, revelation, souls, prayers). This comprehensive awareness underscores that nothing escapes Him, so human affairs and cosmic processes are within His supervision. Coupling that omniscience with the names “the Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving” teaches that God’s encompassing knowledge is exercised with compassion and readiness to pardon: He observes and judges with full insight, yet treats creation with mercy, inviting trust, repentance, and reliance on His forgiving nature.

translation: وقال الذين كفروا: "لا تَأتِينا الساعة". قل: "بلى وربي لتأتينكم، عالم الغيب؛ لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض، ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين".
interpretation: الآية تردّ على إنكار الكافرين ليوم القيامة وتؤكد حتمية وقوعه بعهد من النبي («بلى وربي»)، وتربط ذلك بعلم الله الكامل بالغيب: لا يخفى عنه أدق وزنٍ أو أعظم قدرٍ في السماوات والأرض. المقصود أن لا شيء صغيرًا كان أم كبيرًا يقع خارج نطاق علمه ولا عنونَ لتركه دون حساب — كل عملٍ وجزءٍ من الكون مُسجَّل في كتابٍ واضح. المعنى العملي: على الناس أن يعيشوا مع وعي دائم بأن ما يفعلونه محسوب ومعلوم لله، وأن إنكار الساعة لا يغيّر حقيقة المحاسبة والقدرة الإلهية.

translation: That He may recompense those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse affirms that God’s just recompense for sincere faith combined with moral action is twofold: the removal of sin (forgiveness) and the granting of dignified sustenance (rizq karīm). “Forgiveness” signifies God’s pardon and spiritual restoration, while “noble provision” denotes not only material means but honour, tranquillity, and lawful, respectful support in life and standing before God. The promise underscores that true reward is both moral/spiritual and practical, encouraging believers to unite inner conviction with outward righteous conduct.

translation: And those who strove against Our signs while they were helpless — for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse means that people who persistently oppose, deny, mock, or try to nullify God’s revelations will ultimately be powerless to avert divine judgment; their efforts are futile and will bring upon them a severe and humiliating chastisement, because persistent rejection of guidance leads not to triumph but to grievous retribution.

translation: And those who are given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and that it guides to the path of the Exalted, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Those endowed with sincere, sound knowledge perceive with certainty that the Qur’anic revelation is divinely true; this is not an abstract intellectual assent but recognition that its teaching actually leads people onto the straight way established by God — a path that secures real strength, honour and rightful praise. In other words, true knowledge confirms the Qur’an’s origin and shows that following it brings moral guidance, upright conduct and ultimate success under the authority of the Almighty, Praiseworthy Lord.

translation: وقال الذين كفروا: «هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق أنكم لفي خلق جديد؟»
interpretation: الآية تصوّر سخرية الكافرين الذين يقلّلون رسالة النبي إلى كلام رجل عادي يحدّث عن أمرٍ مستحيل، فجملتهم تكشف اعتقادهم بأن الموت هو تفكك نهائي لا إمكانية بعده لعودة أو وجود جديد. وصفهم للمسألة بهذه الصورة يعكس عدم إدراكهم لقدرة الله على الخلق ثانية، كما أن عبارة «خلق جديد» تشير إلى نوع من الوجود المختلف كليةً عن الحالة الدنيا، فالسخرية هنا تكشف الجهل والإنكار الأخلاقي اللذين يدفعانهم إلى رفض مسؤولية الآخرة باختزالها إلى خرافة.

translation:
أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة ۗ بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد
"Have you fabricated a lie against God, or is there some profit in it? Nay—those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far astray."
interpretation: The verse condemns the making of false claims about God (or His messenger) as either a deliberate fabrication for personal advantage or a delusion, and it defines the true consequence of denying the afterlife: such denial is not a harmless error but a condition that leads to real, enduring punishment and profound misguidance away from divine truth.

translation: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماوات والأرض؟ إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفًا من السماء. إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب.
interpretation: الآية توبخ الغفلة البشرية وتظهر أن الكون كله شاهد على ملكوت الله وسلطانه؛ الله قادر بإرادته أن يقتلع الناس من مساكنهم أو يرسل عليهم عقابًا فاجعًا، لكن عدم إعمال هذا الجزاء الفوري ليس إلغاءً للقدرة بل رحمةً واختبارًا. لذا، الغاية من تذكيرهم بما أمامهم وما خلفهم هو أن تكون دليلاً واضحًا يدفع كل عبد واعٍ راجع إلى التوبة والخضوع قبل أن يأتي التغيير الحاسم — فالآيات الكونية مقرونة بإنذارٍ ودعوةٍ إلى الرجوع إلى الله.

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty: “O mountains, repeat [the praise] with him,” and [so do] the birds; and We made iron pliable for him.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God’s favor on a rightly guided leader embraces both spiritual confirmation and concrete enabling: creation itself (mountains and birds) is summoned to acknowledge and harmonize with the prophetic mission, while the “softening” of iron signifies God-given mastery of material means — skills, technology, and authority — so the leader can secure, build, and administer justice for the community. Thus divine support unites sacred legitimacy with practical capacity to fulfill a just governance and communal protection.

translation: لأعمل أشياء واسعة الشمول وقدرها في التسلسل؛ واعملوا صالحًا؛ إني بما تعملون بصير
interpretation: الآية تذكّر بأن الله يسنّ الأمور ويقدّرها شمولًا وبترتيب محكم، وبأن الإنسان مدعو لعمل الأعمال الصالحة مع علمه أن الله مطلع على أفعاله. لذلك يجب أن تكون أعمال الإنسان مخلصة وصادقة ومتماسكة مع المقصد الإلهي، لأن ما يظهر وما يخفى مرصود أمام البصيرة الإلهية وسيؤخذ بعين الاعتبار.

translation: And for Solomon (We made) the wind subservient — its outward journey was a month and its return was a month. And We caused for him a spring of molten copper to flow. And among the jinn were those who worked for him by permission of his Lord. And whoever among them turned away from Our command, We made him taste the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Solomon’s extraordinary powers — control over the wind, access to molten metal, and the service of certain jinn — were not innate but granted by God to fulfill a divinely sanctioned role. These gifts are presented as instruments for governance and construction under God’s will, and those supernatural agents who served him remained morally accountable: obedience to divine command is required regardless of one’s strength or capability, and deviation brings punishment. The passage therefore affirms God’s sovereignty in bestowing authority, the purposive use of power for God’s ends, and the moral limits and responsibilities that accompany such gifts.

translation: They made for him what he wished of sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs, and cauldrons firmly set. “Work, O family of David, in gratitude.” And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights God’s gift to David: authority, skilled craftsmen and the means to produce both sacred and utilitarian works. By commanding the family of David to “work… in gratitude,” the Qur’an teaches that gratitude is not merely feeling but active, obedient service—using bestowed gifts for God’s purpose, building rightly, and worshiping. The final clause, that few servants are grateful, is an admonition: blessings are trusts that call for humility and responsible use, and human beings often fail to respond with the thankful conduct God requires.

translation: And when We decreed his death, not a sign of it did they perceive except a creature of the earth that gnawed his staff. And when it fell, the jinn realized that had they known the unseen they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that knowledge of the unseen—such as the exact time of death—belongs to God alone. Even powerful or privileged beings (like the jinn) can be utterly ignorant of what is hidden and therefore vulnerable to error and disgrace; the passage warns against arrogance in claiming hidden knowledge, affirms reliance on God’s decree, and calls for humility before realities beyond our perception.

translation: Indeed, for the people of Sabaʾ there was a sign in their dwelling: two gardens on the right and on the left. “Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him.” A good land and a forgiving Lord.
interpretation: The verse teaches that material blessings are intended as visible signs that call for moral response: provision should awaken gratitude, humility and obedience rather than pride or entitlement. God couples outward prosperity with an ethical demand and with mercy—true well‑being consists of both just use of resources and gratefulness, and ingratitude or misuse turns a blessing into a test whose failure can bring loss.

translation: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل
interpretation: Their turning away — a rejection of guidance and ingratitude for blessings — brought about a decisive divine response: a destructive flood and the transformation of luxuriant gardens into meager, bitter growths. This shows a moral and theological principle: worldly favor depends on God’s mercy and moral conduct; arrogance and refusal to heed God’s signs can lead to the swift removal or degradation of blessings, so humility, gratitude, and obedience are necessary to preserve God’s gifts.

translation:
ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا ۖ وهل نجازي إلا الكفور
"Thus We requited them for their disbelief. And is there any recompense from Us except the recompense due to the disbelieving?"
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine justice responds proportionally to human response: persistent denial or ingratitude toward God's guidance brings upon people the only fitting outcome — a recompense corresponding to their disbelief. The rhetorical question underscores inevitability and moral symmetry: gratitude and faith merit mercy, while persistent rejection merits just consequence; God’s punishments are not arbitrary but the appropriate consequence of rejecting clear signs.

translation: And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed neighboring villages, and We appointed travel in them; they journeyed through them by nights and days, secure.
interpretation: الآية تشير إلى أن الله قد نظّم مساحات السكن والطرق بين القرى والبلدات ووفّر السهولة والأمن في التنقّل ليلاً ونهاراً باعتبار ذلك نعمةٍ إلهية عملية تُيسّر التجارة والاجتماع والحياة الاجتماعية. وهي تبيّن أن الراحة والأمن في المرور والمساكن من تدبير الله ومِن فضله على الناس، فتستلزم الشكر، وهي أيضاً تذكير بأن استمرار هذه النعم مرتبط بطاعة الله واستقامَة المجتمع، وقد تزول عند الجحود والكفر.

translation:
قَالُوا رَبَّنَا بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا ۖ وَظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقْنَاهُمْ كُلَّ مَمْزَقٍ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ
“They said, ‘Our Lord, put distance between our journeys.’ They wronged themselves, so We made them mere tales and scattered them into fragments. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a community’s decline often begins with spiritual complacency and ingratitude: by asking to lengthen their journeys (seeking ease, delay, or separation from obligations) they effectively abandoned responsibility and thereby harmed themselves. God’s response — reducing them to stories and scattering them — signals that moral failure breeds social dissolution; the passage is presented as a lesson for those who combine patience in hardship with gratefulness in ease, reminding believers that endurance plus gratitude preserves a people, while neglect and self‑wronging lead to disappearance and public disgrace.

translation: And indeed Satan's conjecture concerning them proved true, so they followed him — except a party of the believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Satan’s expectation that many would submit to his whisperings came to pass because people, by giving in to desire, heedlessness, or weakness of will, choose to follow temptation; this underscores human responsibility (Satan only tempts, he does not compel). The exception — a group of believers — shows that steadfast faith, remembrance of God, sincere repentance, and adherence to guidance can repel Satan’s influence, so guidance and resistance to temptation remain attainable through true belief and moral vigilance.

translation: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك ۗ وربك على كل شيء حفيظ
interpretation: The verse teaches that no human, however respected, truly possesses coercive power to make people believers; apparent authority and trials serve God's purpose of distinguishing those whose faith in the Hereafter is genuine from those who remain doubtful. Ultimately God watches over, preserves, and oversees all affairs, so the true state of hearts and the just outcome belong to Him alone.

translation: قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ۖ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ وَمَا لَهُمْ فِيهِمَا مِن شَرِيكٍ وَمَا لَهُ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ
interpretation: الآية تردّ على عبادة الأصنام والشك في توحيد الربوبية: ما يُدعى من دون الله لا يملك أدنى مقدار من القدرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض، ولا له نصيب أو شريك في تصريف خلْقِ الله، ولا أحد منهم يُعِين أو يساند الله أو الناس. المقصود أن هؤلاء المزاعم عاجزون تمامًا عن النفع أو الضرّ، فعبادتهم وطلب المدد منهم باطل، والتشديد على «مثقال ذرة» يظهر منتهى العجز والمعنى التوحيدي أن الإلهية والسلطة المطلقة لله وحده دون شريك.

translation: And intercession will not avail with Him except for those whom He permits. Until when fear is removed from their hearts, they will say, “What did your Lord say?” They will say, “The truth.” And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: The verse affirms that all intercession on the Day of Reckoning is subject to Allah’s exclusive will: no mediator can benefit anyone unless God grants permission. This underscores divine sovereignty and justice—intercession is not an automatic right or a human entitlement but a mercy conferred by Allah alone. When the terror of the Hour subsides and people face the clear reality of judgment, they will acknowledge that God’s declarations were true; the closing phrase (‘the Most High, the Most Great’) emphasizes that this permission and the final ordering of affairs belong to the utterly exalted, all-powerful Lord, so trust must be placed in His judgment rather than in presumed intermediaries.

translation: Say, “Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?” Say, “God.” And indeed, either we or you are on guidance, or in clear error.
interpretation: The verse strips away polytheistic pretenses by locating ultimate provision solely in God and then frames a decisive test: recognizing God as the Sustainer is the mark of true guidance, while persisting in attributing provision to other beings exposes one to manifest error. Thus it invites people to examine the observable reality of their dependence on God — that realization determines whether they stand in guidance or in clear misguidance.

translation: قل: «لا تُسأَلون عما أجرمنا، ولا نُسأَل عما تَعملون».
interpretation: الأمر هنا يُخاطب الرسول ليُعلِن أن المساءلة أمام الله قائمة على مسؤولية كل نفس عن عملها؛ لا يُحمّل الناس ذنوب غيرهم ولا يُطلب من المؤمنين أن يجيبوا عن أعمال الكافرين. مجمل المعنى: الحساب فردي والذنب لا ينتقل من إنسان إلى آخر.

translation: Say, “Our Lord will gather us together; then He will decide between us in truth, and He is the Opener, the All‑Knowing.”
interpretation: This statement directs the believer to relinquish the need for immediate vindication and to trust God’s final adjudication. “He will gather us” points to the ultimate reunion on the Day of Reckoning when all disputes are confronted; “He will decide between us in truth” means Allah will disclose reality, reward and punish justly, and make plain what was hidden. Calling Him al‑Fattah (the Opener) emphasizes that He alone unfolds outcomes, opens hearts and affairs, and grants decisive victory or exposure, while al‑Alim (the All‑Knowing) guarantees that His judgment is based on full and perfect knowledge of intentions and circumstances. The verse therefore counsels patience, reliance on divine justice, and restraint from seeking worldly retribution, since ultimate justice and clarification belong to God alone.

translation: Say, ‘Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners.’ No! Rather, He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This command to challenge idolaters is a method of exposing the emptiness of polytheism: demand that they produce any real partners or evidence, and their failure reveals that claims of sharing God’s lordship are baseless. The verse affirms that God’s sovereignty is absolute—His might and wisdom are complete and indivisible—so attributing partners is both logically impossible and theologically illegitimate; purported partners cannot share in His attributes, authority, or providence, and therefore such claims rest on illusion, not reality.

translation: And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all people; but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the prophet’s mission is universal and twofold: to announce God’s mercy and to warn of the consequences of rejection. Its purpose is not limited to one community, and the responsibility it creates rests on each person’s reception of the message. The phrase about most people not knowing highlights human heedlessness or willful disregard—so the verse teaches that guidance has been offered plainly and broadly, and failure to respond stems from one’s own ignorance or negligence, for which one will be held accountable; the prophet’s duty is conveyance, not coercion.

translation: وَيَقُولُونَ: «مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا الْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ»
interpretation: الآية تجسّد موقف المشكّكين الذين يردّون بتهكّم على وعود الآخرة، فيمسكون عن قبولها عبر طلب تأجيلها أو طلب زمان محدد كدليل. هذا السؤال ليس بحثاً عن حقيقة بل وسيلة للتسويف والتكذيب: يريدون أن يجعلوا المساءلة أمراً بعيداً ليبرروا استمرار غيّهم وظلمهم، ويظنون أن المطالبة بموعد ستحملهم عن الإيمان. من ذلك نفهم درساً أخلاقياً وروحياً أن إنكار الحق يتخذ صوراً عقلانية زائفة، وأن وعد الله بالبعث والحساب حتميّ رغم سخرية المنكرين.

translation: قل: «لكم ميعاد يومٍ لا تُستأخرون عنه ساعةً ولا تُستقدمون.»
interpretation: الآية تؤكد أن يوم الحساب موكول إلى حكم الله وحده وله موعد ثابت لا تخضعه أهواء الناس: لا يستطيع أحد أن يؤخره ولا أن يقدّمه. هذا المقصد يقوّي قَبول المسؤولية الفردية ويُحطّم مطامع المتكبرين الذين يظنون أنهم بقدرتهم أو بزعمهم سيفلتون من الجزاء، ويواسي المؤمنين بأن العدل الإلهي سيحصل بالتمام في الوقت الذي يقرره الله وحده.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in that which was before it." And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, they will turn to one another in speech; those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant, "If it had not been for you, we would have been believers."
interpretation: The verse depicts a common human pattern: under pressure from powerful or arrogant figures the timid may outwardly reject guidance and later try to shift blame for their unbelief. At the Resurrection this excuse will be exposed — social coercion and conformity cannot remove personal moral responsibility. The scene condemns both the arrogant who suppress the truth and the weak who failed to uphold it, reminding that accountability before God is individual and that blaming others will not avert judgment.

translation:
قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم ۖ بل كنتم مجرمين
"Those who were arrogant said to those whom they deemed weak, 'Are we the ones who have turned you away from guidance after it has come to you?' — No; you yourselves were sinners."
interpretation: The verse exposes a pattern of arrogant people deflecting responsibility: when a community rejects divine guidance, the powerful blame the marginalized to absolve themselves. By asking rhetorically whether they 'turned others away' from guidance, the proud pretend innocence while accusing the weak; in truth the sin lies with those who, through arrogance, wilful denial, or injustice, refuse guidance and persecute others. The passage condemns scapegoating and insists that accountability rests on those who knowingly reject or obstruct the truth, not on the oppressed they blame.

translation: And those who were made weak will say to those who were arrogant, “Rather, it was the plotting of night and day when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and to set up equals to Him.” They will hide the remorse within themselves when they see the punishment, and We have put chains on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: The verse exposes how entrenched power and persistent worldly influence can lead vulnerable people into error by normalizing disbelief; when divine retribution arrives, the deceit and pressure of the powerful are exposed but remorse comes too late and is inward and concealed. The chains and punishment symbolize the irreversible consequence of choices made under that influence, while the closing question affirms moral responsibility and divine justice — each person will receive the due for their own deeds despite the social dynamics that led them astray.

translation:
وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَا إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ كَافِرُونَ
“And We did not send a warner to any town but its affluent ones said, ‘Indeed we are, regarding that with which you have been sent, disbelievers.’”
interpretation: The verse points to a recurring social dynamic: those who enjoy luxury, privilege, or power in a community often reject prophetic guidance because it threatens their comforts, status, or interests. Their denial is rooted in arrogance, attachment to worldly gain, and fear of losing authority or livelihood, so they dismiss the warning rather than reform.

translation: And they say, "We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished."
interpretation: This statement reflects an arrogant, self‑deceptive logic that equates worldly abundance—many children and riches—with protection from divine accountability. The verse criticizes that false criterion for security, reminding that moral standing, not numbers or material prosperity, determines one’s standing before God; relying on wealth or progeny as a shield is a dangerous illusion that leads to complacency and eventual ruin.

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]; but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: The verse affirms that sustenance is ultimately apportioned by God's wise will in ways beyond human sight; apparent riches or poverty are not definitive signs of divine favor or rejection but serve purposes—tests, trials, means of spiritual growth, social balance, or wisdom known only to God. The practical demand is humility and trust: work lawfully, be generous when able, be patient and maintain faith when provision is limited, and refrain from judging others or arrogantly claiming that wealth equals God's special approval.

translation: Neither your wealth nor your children will bring you nearer to Us in nearness, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them there will be a double reward for what they did, and they will be in lofty chambers, safe.
interpretation: The verse teaches that rank before God is not secured by lineage, offspring, or material possessions; true nearness to Him is attained only through sincere faith and righteous action. Those who combine belief with good deeds will receive multiplied recompense and be granted elevated, secure places in the Hereafter, emphasizing that moral and spiritual responsibility—not worldly ties—determine one’s standing before God.

translation: And those who strive to render Our signs ineffective—they are the ones who will be brought to punishment.
interpretation: The verse indicts anyone who, out of arrogance, envy, or self‑interest, works to nullify, disparage, obstruct, or explain away God’s signs (the revelations, proofs, or manifestations of divine truth). Their efforts are ultimately powerless (معاجزين) against divine reality, and because they oppose and mislead others away from guidance they will be held accountable and presented for punishment.

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts (it) for whom He wills; and whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it; and He is the best of providers."
interpretation: The verse teaches that provision is ultimately determined by God's sovereign wisdom: He may expand or constrict sustenance for people according to purposes known to Him. Believers are therefore urged to trust God's governance of provision and not hoard out of fear, because charitable spending is not a literal permanent loss — God promises to recompense and supply what is given. Calling Him 'the best of providers' reassures the faithful that true sustenance comes from Divine mercy and that generosity, dependence on God, and acceptance of His decree are the proper responses to the distribution of wealth.

translation: And on the Day He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels, “Are these the ones you used to worship?”
interpretation: The verse teaches that on Resurrection the pretended divinity of anyone other than God will be publicly exposed: God will confront the angels with those beings people revered, and by asking this rhetorically He highlights their impotence and the absurdity of worship directed at created things. The question brings shame and accountability upon false objects of worship and their adherents, affirming the exclusive right of God to be worshipped.

translation: They will say, “Glory be to You; You are our protector instead of them.” Rather, they used to worship the jinn — most of them believed in them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of invoking or trusting created beings as protectors: at the moment of reckoning people will acknowledge God’s sole sovereignty, but previously many had been misled into worshipping invisible creatures (jinn) and placing faith in them. It teaches that such misplaced reliance stems from ignorance or deception and will not avail on the Day of judgment, for true protection and authority belong to God alone.

translation: So today none of you will have power over another, nor will you be able to benefit or harm one another. And We will say to those who wronged, “Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.”
interpretation: On Resurrection Day all human relationships and worldly means of influence are rendered powerless: kinship, wealth, rank, and alliances can neither help nor protect anyone; each person stands alone before divine justice. The command “taste the punishment” signals that the wrongdoers will immediately and experientially receive the torment they once denied or mocked, showing the certainty of the warnings they rejected. The verse therefore emphasizes individual responsibility, the finality of God’s judgment, and the folly of denying the reality and consequences of the Hereafter.

translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, they say, “This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.” And they say, “This is nothing but a fabricated lie.” And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, “This is nothing but clear magic.”
interpretation: The verse diagnoses a common human reaction to divine truth: instead of engaging with the evidence, opponents dismiss it by ascribing bad motives to the messenger (accusing him of corrupting ancestral practices), by charging fabrication, or by labeling the revelation as sorcery. This response reveals that rejection often springs from attachment to inherited beliefs, fear of social or personal loss, and moral obstinacy rather than from an objective assessment of the signs; the verse therefore indicts the psychological defenses and social interests that prevent people from accepting clear guidance.

translation: And We did not give them any books to study, nor did We send to them before you any warner.
interpretation: The verse indicates that those peoples lacked the means of transmitted guidance — no revealed scripture available for them to learn from and no prior messenger to warn them — and thus their situation should be understood in light of that absence: divine guidance normally comes through books and warners, so responsibility and accountability are tied to whether such clear, accessible instruction was provided to a community.

translation: And those before them denied [the messengers], and they did not attain a tenth of what We had given them; yet they denied My messengers — so how severe was My punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that past communities rejected divine messengers despite having only a small share of God’s blessings, and that their rejection brought overwhelming disgrace and punishment (نكير). The underlying moral is that greater provision and guidance increase responsibility: if those who had little were destroyed for denying the truth, then those who receive more favors or clearer evidence but still reject the message should expect an even graver reckoning.

translation: Say: I only admonish you to one thing — that you stand for Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect. There is nothing of madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse narrows the Prophet’s mission to a single, urgent demand: sincere orientation toward God expressed both collectively and individually, accompanied by deliberate reflection. That method—standing before God and thinking—enables people to recognize truth for themselves rather than following emotion or social pressure. By stating that the Messenger is not mad, the verse defends his integrity and clarifies his role as a clear, sober warner whose message must be taken seriously because it comes as a warning prior to an imminent, grave accountability.

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only with Allah, and He is, over all things, a Witness."
interpretation: The speaker affirms that his preaching is not for worldly profit or personal gain; he seeks no payment from the people because the true recompense for his efforts rests with God alone. By declaring that Allah is witness over everything, the statement both vindicates the sincerity of the mission—God knows the inner motives—and promises ultimate accountability and recompense beyond human judgment, so acceptance or rejection by people does not affect the moral and eternal value of the message.

translation: Say: Indeed, my Lord casts forth the truth — the Knower of the unseen.
interpretation: The phrase portrays revelation and truth as coming directly from God: He 'casts' or imparts the true reality decisively into hearts, speech, and events, not as a product of human conjecture. Calling Him 'the Knower of the unseen' underscores that what He sends is rooted in complete knowledge of hidden realities (future matters, inner truths, unseen wisdom), so the message’s authority and trustworthiness rest on God’s perfect, all-encompassing knowledge rather than on human opinion.

translation: Say, “The Truth has come, and falsehood neither originates anything nor can it restore (what it has destroyed).”
interpretation: The verse affirms that divine truth is established and self-sufficient, while falsehood is essentially powerless: it cannot create reality or perpetuate itself and therefore is transient and destined to fail when confronted by truth.

translation: قُلْ: «إِن ضَللتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي، وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي؛ إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ.»
interpretation: The speaker (the Prophet) declares that his guidance is not self-originated but comes by divine revelation; if he errs, the fault is his alone, and he bears its personal consequence, while any true guidance he manifests is due to what God discloses to him. By affirming that God is “Hearing, Near,” the verse both vindicates the prophet against charges of deceit or whim and directs responsibility for accepting or rejecting the message onto the people, stressing that ultimate guidance and accountability rest with God and that the prophet is a sincere, receptive bearer of what God communicates.

translation: And if you could see when they are seized with terror — “There is no escape!” — and they are taken from a nearby place.
interpretation: The verse portrays the sudden, inescapable onset of divine judgment: those who denied truth will be overwhelmed by panic and find that every perceived refuge vanishes. The phrase “taken from a nearby place” stresses the immediacy and inevitability of accountability — what seemed distant or safe is swiftly brought upon them, showing that worldly measures cannot avert the consequences ordained by God.

translation: وقالوا: «آمنا به» — فأين الصدق في ذلك، إذ أن تناوشهم وخصوماتهم نابعة من مكان بعيد؟
interpretation: الآية تصف من يعلنون إيمانهم باللسان حين تُتلى عليهم الآيات ولكن باطنهم لا يوافقه؛ كلامهم بالإيمان مجرد شعار، بينما أفعالهم ونزاعاتهم ومواقفهم تكشف بُعد قلوبهم عن الحق. المعنى أن الإيمان الحقيقي يظهر بالصدق والطمأنينة والامتثال، أما الأقوال الفارغة فتبقى مجرد ادعاء لا يغير حالة القلب ولا يقرب صاحبه من هدى الله.

translation: And they had already disbelieved in it before, and they fling about regarding the unseen from a distant place.
interpretation: The verse points to people who, having already closed themselves to the message, continue to speak and spread assertions about matters beyond human knowledge—claims about the unseen—yet do so from a place of ignorance and remoteness. Their rejection is not the result of fair inquiry but of prejudice and conjecture: they hurl unfounded accusations and rumors at the truth while remaining distant from evidence and sincere seeking.

translation: وُوضِعَ حَاجِزٌ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ كَمَا فَعَلَ بِأَشْيَاعِهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا فِي شَكٍّ مُّرِيبٍ.
interpretation: الآية تُفسِّر وجود الحاجز بين الناس وبين ما يطلبون بأنه نتيجة لإعراضهم وتماديهم عن الحق: يَمنَعُ اللهُ عنهم الوسائل أو يُغشي قلوبهم أو يهيئ لهم وسائل خداع، كما جرى على أقوام سلف، فتبقى أرواحهم معلقة في شكّ مريب — لا يصلون إلى الحقيقة التي ينوونها لأن حالتهم النفسية والربانية تحول دون إدراكها.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. All praise is due to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers—those having wings, two, three, and four. He increases in creation whatever He wills. Indeed, God is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute sovereignty and creative power: He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth and appoints angels as His messengers and agents, fashioned with varying numbers of wings to indicate diversity and order in the created realm. By stating that He “increases in creation whatever He wills,” the verse emphasizes God’s freedom to originate, multiply, transform, and sustain life and phenomena according to His will; therefore all plurality, change, and the capacity for renewal in the universe point back to His omnipotence and authority, calling believers to acknowledge reliance on and submission to that divine power.

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, there is none who can release it thereafter. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute sovereignty over all blessings and provisions: ultimate giving and withholding rest with Him alone, so human beings and created causes have no true power to grant or deny what He decrees. This teaches reliance on divine wisdom and power, warns against attributing independent agency to other forces, and reminds believers that apparent gains or losses are under God’s wise, purposeful governance.

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you: is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? There is no deity except Him—so how then are you being led astray?
interpretation: The verse confronts human ingratitude and misplaced allegiance by pointing to the single, observable reality that God alone creates and sustains life. Its rhetorical questions are meant to dissolve the pretence of other gods or forces deserving trust: if all provision and existence come from Allah, then denying or ignoring His lordship is irrational and morally culpable. The passage therefore urges a conscious turning to gratitude, recognition, and dependence on God rather than following vain beliefs, desires, or traditions that divert people from the clear evidence of divine sovereignty.

translation: And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied. And to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: The verse consoles and counsels: rejection of the Messenger is not a new phenomenon—previous prophets were also denied—and therefore such denial does not overturn the truth of the mission. Ultimately every affair, judgment and outcome rests with God, so one should remain patient, steadfast and trust in God’s final adjudication rather than be unsettled by temporary opposition.

translation: O people, the promise of Allah is true. So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver (al‑ghurūr) deceive you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute certainty of God’s promise — especially of resurrection, judgment and ultimate recompense — and warns against two complementary forms of spiritual error. First is being consumed by the temporary attractions and successes of this world so that one becomes complacent, morally lax, or postpones sincere preparation for the Hereafter. Second is being misled by the subtle deceit called al‑ghurūr: satanic suggestions, vain pride, or false reasoning that distorts one’s view of God (making Him seem distant, unconcerned, or unlikely to hold us accountable). The practical thrust is ethical and existential: cultivate awareness of life’s transience, resist self‑deception and pride, ground hope and fear properly in God’s promises, and let that certainty shape choices and priorities now rather than allowing worldly glitter or sly temptation to derail you from what will matter eternally.

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Satan is a real, hostile force whose purpose is to draw people into ruin; therefore believers must adopt an active, defensive stance—recognizing and resisting his whisperings, avoiding influences and companions that encourage disobedience, and relying on remembrance of God, prayer, and righteous action to thwart his attempts—because following his calls ultimately leads to the fire.

translation: Those who disbelieve — for them is a severe punishment; and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse affirms a moral and eschatological principle: people's ultimate outcomes are tied to both their inner stance toward divine guidance and their outward conduct. Persistent rejection of truth leads to just, severe consequences, while genuine faith accompanied by righteous action attracts God's mercy — the wiping away of sins — and an elevated, abundant recompense. It teaches that salvation requires sincerity of belief manifested in ethical behavior, reflecting God’s balance of justice toward wrong and generosity toward those who accept guidance and act upon it.

translation:
أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا ۖ فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ۖ فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات ۚ إن الله عليم بما يصنعون
“Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he regards it as good? Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let your soul grieve over them; indeed Allah is Knowing of what they do.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that when people persist in wrongdoing it is often because their faults have been made to look appealing to them—whether through their own desires, blind habits, or subtle deceits—so they come to accept vice as if it were virtue. Divine guidance and misguidance are described here not as arbitrary caprice but as the outworking of God’s wise knowledge in response to people’s hearts and choices: those who harden themselves and embrace self‑deception are left to that condition, while those who turn sincerely are guided. The command not to be overcome with grief reminds the believer (and the Messenger) to entrust the ultimate judgment and outcomes to God’s perfect knowledge and justice, rather than agonize over people who, by their own inclinations, have chosen the path away from guidance.

translation:
وَاللَّهُ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّيَاحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا فَسَقْنَاهُ إِلَى بَلَدٍ مَيْتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ النُّشُورُ
“And Allah is He Who sends the winds, which stir up the clouds; then We drive them to a dead land and cause rain to descend upon it, and by it We bring the earth back to life after its death. Thus is the Resurrection.”
interpretation: The verse uses the observable revival of barren land by God’s will as a sign demonstrating the certainty and plausibility of the final Resurrection: the same divine sovereignty and power that orders winds, clouds and rain to restore life to the earth suffices to raise human beings for judgment. It therefore affirms God’s control, wisdom and mercy, and intends to awaken reflection and moral seriousness about resurrection and accountability.

translation: Whoever seeks honor — to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends the pure word, and the righteous deed He raises. But those who scheme evil — for them is a severe punishment; and the scheming of those is ruined.
interpretation: True honor and exaltation belong solely to God; any dignity a person attains is by being aligned with what pleases Him. Sincere, truthful speech and righteous action are what ascend and are elevated before God — not worldly plots, force, or pride. Those who pursue prestige through deceit, oppression, or secret scheming will be repelled and punished, for their plans are ultimately futile and destroyed. The passage thus teaches that lasting honor comes through faithfulness, good conduct, and God’s acceptance, while immoral striving for status leads to ruin.

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop (of sperm), then made you into pairs. And no female conceives nor gives birth except by His knowledge. And no one’s life is extended nor is any portion of it diminished except in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that origin, conception, birth and the span of life are entirely under God’s sovereign knowledge and decree: human beginnings return to God’s creative act, every pregnancy and delivery unfold within His awareness, and the length of each life is noted in a Divine Record. The intended effect is to remind people of their dependence on God, to foster trust and acceptance of life’s events (including death and hardship) as part of His wise ordinance, while also calling them to act responsibly within the sphere of human agency knowing that ultimate outcomes rest with Him.

translation:
وما يستوي البحران: هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج، ومن كلٍّ تأكلون لحماً طرياً وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها، وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون.
"And the two seas are not alike: this one is fresh, pleasant to drink, and this one is salt and bitter. From each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments to wear. And you see the ships ploughing through them to seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful."
interpretation: The verse points to a theological and ethical lesson: the created differences and resources of the world are intentional signs of God’s wisdom and providence meant to move people from mere observation to recognition and gratitude. The contrast and variety in nature—paired with human ability to benefit from them (food, material wealth, trade, travel)—shows that provision is not accidental but part of a purposeful order that invites responsible use, dependence on God, and moral response. The visible benefits (such as navigation and extraction of goods) are presented not as ends in themselves but as stimuli for gratefulness and acknowledgment of divine sovereignty; gratitude and thankfulness are the proper human reaction to God’s generous arrangement, while ingratitude would be a moral failure despite obvious blessings.

translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon—each runs toward an appointed term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those whom you invoke besides Him do not possess so much as the membrane of a date-stone.
interpretation: The verse is calling attention to the ordered, purposeful governance of the universe as decisive evidence of one sovereign Lord. The regular, law‑governed movements of celestial things manifest God’s authority, wisdom and control, so reliance, worship and submission properly belong to Him alone; whatever people set up as deities or aids besides God have no real power or ownership—even the smallest claim—and thus trusting or venerating them is futile and misplaced.

translation: If you call upon them, they will not hear your invocation; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your associating them (with Allah). And none can inform you like the All‑Aware.
interpretation: The verse declares the impotence and futility of worshipping created things: idols or false deities neither hear nor answer supplication, and even if they could, they would not help; ultimately they will repudiate being worshipped on the Day of Reckoning, exposing the lie of shirk. The warning serves to redirect trust and worship exclusively to God, and to remind that only God—Al‑Khabeer, the All‑Aware—truly knows the reality and consequences of those claims.

translation: O people, you are the ones in need of Allah; and Allah is the Self‑Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse confronts human self‑sufficiency by making dependence on God the defining reality of human existence: our lives, provision, knowledge and outcomes are contingent, not autonomous. Describing God as Self‑Sufficient stresses His absolute independence—He neither needs creation nor is affected by it—while calling Him Praiseworthy explains that every true reason for praise ultimately returns to Him because He is the source of all good. The intended moral and spiritual lesson is humility and grateful reliance: to abandon arrogance in worldly means, to turn to God in worship and supplication, and to orient action and trust toward the One whose independence and worthiness of praise are absolute.

translation: If He wills, He will remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: The statement emphasizes God’s absolute sovereignty and the contingency of human status: no community’s existence is guaranteed — if a people persist in disobedience or fail to fulfill God’s purpose, God can replace them with others more fitting to carry out His plan. It is a warning to avoid complacency and a call to humility, obedience, and trust in divine authority.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: A concise affirmation of divine omnipotence: matters which appear impossible, burdensome, or beyond human capacity—whether creation, resurrection, judgement, change of states, or fulfilment of promises—are effortless for God; nothing is too hard or beyond His will, so reliance on His power and decrees is justified.

translation: And no bearer of burden will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden one calls another to help carry his load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a near relative. You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and who establish prayer; and whoever purifies himself does so for the benefit of his own soul; and to Allah is the return.
interpretation: The verse affirms that moral and spiritual responsibility is ultimately individual: each person will answer for their own deeds and cannot shift their accountability onto others, not even onto close kin. The Prophet’s warnings and guidance reach and transform those whose inward reverence for God (expressed in unseen fear and regular prayer) makes them receptive; spiritual purification (tazkiyah) is an inward investment whose benefit accrues to the one who undertakes it. All outcomes are settled by God in the final return, so ethical conduct and self-purification are matters of personal duty with eternal consequences.

translation: And the blind and the one who sees are not alike.
interpretation: A moral and existential distinction is being drawn: “the blind” refers to those deprived of inner insight or who reject divine guidance, while “the one who sees” denotes those granted understanding and acceptance. This difference is decisive for one’s direction, responsibility, and outcome before God—spiritual sight brings guidance, action, and reward, whereas spiritual blindness leads to error and loss.

translation: Neither darkness nor light.
interpretation: A negation that underscores God’s transcendence and all‑encompassing sovereignty: nothing, whether hidden (darkness) or manifest (light), lies outside His knowledge and dominion.

translation: Neither shade nor scorching heat.
interpretation: A terse declaration of total deprivation: all means of relief and protection are removed—there will be no shelter to cool nor any respite from burning—so the suffering is comprehensive, unavoidable, and complete.

translation: And the living and the dead are not equal. Indeed, Allah makes to hear whom He wills; and you are not (able to) make those in the graves hear.
