The verse thus exposes hypocrisy and reminds that genuine belief is internal and ultimately known to God.

translation: We had no authority over you; rather, you were a people given to transgression.
interpretation: The statement denies any legitimate power or right of domination by the speakers over those addressed and turns the charge back onto the addressees, portraying them as the real wrongdoers. It teaches that blame and responsibility belong to those who exceed bounds and act oppressively, not to those who lacked authority to compel them.

translation: So the word of our Lord proved true against us: indeed, we shall surely taste [the punishment].
interpretation: This is the confession of the condemned acknowledging that God’s warning was accurate and unavoidable: their earlier doubt or denial cannot avert the decree, and they must now face the consequences. The verse underscores the certainty of divine promise and human accountability — when God’s judgment comes, people will experience exactly what they were warned of, revealing the reality of moral responsibility and the inevitability of recompense.

translation: So We led you astray — indeed, We were astrayers.
interpretation: This is the confession of the deceivers (the devils) admitting that those who followed them were led into error by their deliberate misleading. It emphasizes that misguidance was not accidental or ordained by God but the result of following beings whose nature is to divert people; their repeated description of themselves as “astrayers” underscores the persistent, intentional character of their deception and serves as a warning that following such guidance brings accountability and punishment, so people must reject their whisperings and turn back to true guidance and repentance.

translation:
فَإِنَّهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
"For indeed, on that Day they will share together in the punishment."
interpretation: The verse warns that on the Day of Judgment those who embraced falsehood, followed misleading leaders, or allied themselves with wrongdoing will not escape individually but will bear the consequences collectively — showing that worldly ties and pretenses will be nullified and divine justice will hold all parties to their shared responsibility.

translation: Indeed, thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: The verse declares a principle of divine justice: God, in response to those who persist in transgression and rejection, brings about their undoing—exposing their deeds, thwarting their plans, and imposing punishment or humiliation in this world or the hereafter—as a measured consequence of their wrongdoing and a deterrent for others.

translation: Indeed, whenever it was said to them, 'There is no god but Allah,' they would be arrogant.
interpretation: The verse points to a habitual, pride‑born rejection: certain people are so attached to their status, traditions, or self‑esteem that when confronted with the clear truth of God’s oneness they respond with disdain rather than humility. Their arrogance acts as a barrier to guidance, preventing sincere submission; the passage therefore indicts pride as the spiritual obstacle that keeps the heart closed to faith and calls attention to humility as a prerequisite for accepting divine guidance.

translation: And they say, “Shall we abandon our gods for a poet, a madman?”
interpretation: The verse calls attention to a common defensive reaction: when confronted with inconvenient truth, people often reject it not on evidence but by attacking the messenger’s character—dismissing the claim as mere poetry or madness. This reflects stubborn attachment to familiar beliefs and the use of ridicule and ad hominem dismissal to avoid examining the message on its merits; the passage therefore condemns relying on social prejudice and emotional resistance instead of judging truth by reason and signs.

translation: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين — "But he has come with the truth and has confirmed the messengers."
interpretation: The statement affirms that what was brought is authentic divine truth that corroborates and validates the missions of the earlier prophets; it asserts continuity of God’s guidance, showing that this revelation confirms, completes and vindicates the message delivered by the messengers before him.

translation: Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment.
interpretation: A stern warning that those who persist in rebellion or denial of God's guidance will inevitably experience the consequences of their choices; the verb “taste” stresses immediate, unavoidable personal experience, and “painful punishment” denotes the severity of divine retribution (whether manifest in this life or the Hereafter), serving both as justice for wrongdoing and as a deterrent to further transgression.

translation: And you will be recompensed only for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse affirms personal moral accountability: ultimate reward or punishment is determined by one’s own actions and intentional conduct. It underscores divine justice — no one will be credited or debited for another’s deeds, and outcomes correspond to what a person actually did and intended, thus urging sincere, responsible behavior in this life.

translation: Except the sincere (devoted) servants of Allah.
interpretation: It designates a distinct group who are exempted from the general fate mentioned contextually: those whose faith and actions are purely for God alone — free from hypocrisy, ostentation, or partnership — so their inner sincerity makes their worship accepted and secures them God’s special protection or deliverance.

translation: For them is a known (appointed) provision.
interpretation: It means that God has set aside for those people a definite, predetermined provision — an assured, measured portion (of sustenance or reward) reserved for them — emphasizing the certainty and divine guarantee of what they will receive.

translation: Fruits — and they will be honoured.
interpretation: This brief statement points to the dual nature of the reward for the righteous: they are granted abundant, pleasant sustenance (fruits) and, beyond material provision, are raised to a state of honour — dignity, respect, and privileged standing before God. The word “honoured” signals not merely comfort but the removal of shame and the bestowal of nearness to divine favour, showing that Paradise’s blessing combines bodily delights with spiritual elevation.

translation: In the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: A designation of the paradisal abode Allah promises the righteous: an enduring realm of perfect comfort, peace, and fulfillment where physical delights and spiritual nearness to God consummate the reward and mercy granted for faith and righteous conduct.

translation: Reclining on couches facing one another.
interpretation: A depiction of the honoured repose and social ease of the righteous in Paradise: they rest in dignity on beautifully prepared couches set opposite each other, allowing unobstructed fellowship, recognition and tranquil conversation. The image conveys honour, comfort, mutual respect and the absence of fatigue or discord — an expression of perfected communal life and serene reward.

translation: A cup of clear, flowing spring-water will be passed around among them.
interpretation: The phrase promises that the righteous in Paradise will receive an inexhaustible, pure, life‑giving drink — both a literal refreshment and a symbol of spiritual renewal and satisfaction. The word “معين” (a running spring) conveys continuous, unpolluted bounty, while “يطاف عليهم” (is passed around among them) emphasizes that this blessing is freely given and communally enjoyed, removing all deficiency and fully quenching bodily and spiritual thirst by God’s generous mercy.

translation: بيضاء — لذةٌ للشاربين
interpretation: تشير إلى مشروبٍ من نعيم الجنة، نقيٌّ ومشعّ بلونه الأبيض، رمزٌ للطهارة والصفاء، يزوَّد به السعداء ليكون لذّةً كاملةً وخاليةً من كل ضارة أو مرارة.

translation: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون — "Therein is no ghul (no monstrous, predatory being), nor do they bleed from it.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the place (understood as Paradise) as entirely free from harm and terror: no frightening, devouring creatures threaten the dwellers, and they suffer no injury, bleeding, or physical hurt. It underscores the complete safety, purity, and absence of pain or loss experienced by its inhabitants, emphasizing the tranquil and unassailable nature of that abode.

translation: And with them will be maidens of restrained gaze and beautiful eyes.
interpretation: The phrase describes the companions promised to the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing their chastity, dignity and refined demeanor. “قاصرات الطرف” conveys modesty and purity of gaze rather than lasciviousness, while “عين” highlights their radiant beauty; together the words portray a relationship in the Hereafter that is honorable, free from worldly corruption and based on serene, respectful companionship as part of God’s gracious reward.

translation: كأنهن بيض مكنون — "As if they were preserved (white) eggs."
interpretation: The phrase likens the women's luminous, unspoiled beauty and seclusion to white eggs kept enclosed and guarded: their fairness and attractiveness appear pristine because they are protected from public exposure, so their beauty is both preserved and striking precisely because it is concealed.

translation: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون — Then some of them turned toward one another, questioning.
interpretation: This depicts the human response when reality and accountability arrive: people become bewildered, seek answers from one another, and instinctively search for causes, explanations, or someone to blame — revealing confusion, regret, and the failure of prior certainties in the face of the truth.

translation:
قال قائلٌ منهم: إِنِّي كان لي قَرِينٌ
"One of them said, ‘Indeed, I had a companion.’"
interpretation: The phrase expresses a culpable person's attempt to locate the source of his misguidance in another who accompanied and influenced him. It points to two lessons: companionship strongly shapes moral choice—bad company can incline a person toward error—and yet on the Day of Reckoning such an explanation becomes an admission, not an excuse. Responsibility remains with the individual even if a companion misled him; the verse warns to choose companions carefully and reminds that blaming others will not remove one’s own accountability.

translation: He says, “Are you indeed one of those who affirm (the truth)?”
interpretation: A derisive challenge from a skeptic — an expression of incredulity and contempt intended to undermine the messenger’s credibility by treating his claim to confirm the divine message as absurd, revealing the questioner’s stubborn refusal to accept the truth.

translation: “When we die and have become dust and bones, will we indeed be brought back (to life)?”
interpretation: The verse records a skeptical objection that treats bodily decomposition as proof that resurrection is impossible; its meaning is to expose that narrow, materialist reasoning and to remind listeners that God’s creative power is not limited by physical decay—He who gave life can reassemble and restore it—so using burial and decay as an argument against accountability and resurrection is logically and theologically untenable.

translation: He said, “Are you fully aware?”
interpretation: A rhetorical challenge to those who presume knowledge or authority over hidden matters—it exposes the inadequacy of their claim and reminds listeners that true, comprehensive knowledge belongs to God, calling for humility and caution before asserting what one does not know.

translation: Then he looked — and saw it in the midst of Hell.
interpretation: The verse depicts the moment of realization for one who denied or rejected divine warning: when the truth is unveiled he sees his own doom placed at the very heart of Hell. It conveys the sudden, inescapable exposure of the consequences of his choices and serves as a warning that heedlessness and persistent wrongdoing will culminate in clear, unavoidable punishment.

translation: قالت: «تالله إن كدت لتردين» — “By Allah, you almost made me turn back.”
interpretation: An emphatic oath of reproach: the speaker invokes God to stress that the addressee’s words or actions very nearly caused her to abandon her chosen course, resolve, or safe position. It expresses shock and blame, highlighting how close she came to a harmful reversal and underlining the seriousness of the other person’s effect on her state.

translation: And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought to punishment.
interpretation: The speaker acknowledges that their safety or exaltation is not by personal merit but by God’s mercy; without that divine favor they would have been counted among the condemned, a reminder to be humble, grateful, and aware that deliverance and honor are gifts from God rather than human achievements.

translation: Are we then not to die?
interpretation: A rhetorical rebuke aimed at those who deny resurrection: it stresses the inevitability of death and uses that inevitability to expose the inconsistency of rejecting God’s power to bring the dead back to life — if our present mortality is real, then divine revivification is equally possible, and thus moral accountability before God is unavoidable.

translation: Except that We had caused them to die before, and We are not ones who are punished.
interpretation: The phrase ‘the first death’ refers to the temporal, worldly death that God has already brought upon those people; it is contrasted with the ultimate resurrection and Reckoning. The clause ‘We are not ones who are punished’ affirms God’s absolute sovereignty and that He does not suffer harm or injustice—He does not endure retribution as creatures do. Together the words deny any suggestion that God is weak, unjust, or subject to punishment, and they remind the listener that life and death are entirely under God’s control and that final recompense will come from Him alone.

translation: Indeed, this is the great success.
interpretation: It declares that the highest triumph is spiritual and eternal: to follow God’s guidance, win His pleasure, and be saved into Paradise is the supreme, lasting victory far surpassing any temporal worldly achievement.

translation: For the like of this let those who work, work.
interpretation: A divine exhortation: having presented an example of divine reward, God calls on those who seek the same outcome to persist in earnest, sincere righteous action — to continue laboring in faith and good deeds so as to attain that described recompense.

translation: Is that a better provision, or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: A rhetorical contrast intended to correct priorities: the verse warns that fleeting, outward comforts of this life are not the true good, and one must not be deceived by immediate provision—what truly matters is one’s relation to God; disobedience and rejection lead to the dreadful, humiliating sustenance of Hell (symbolized by the tree of Zaqqum), whereas true lasting good lies in obedience, faith, and the rewards of the hereafter.

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: God is saying that the thing mentioned (the event, punishment, or warning in context) was allowed or ordained as a test specifically for the unjust so that their corruption and rejection become manifest, so they are separated from the righteous and receive the consequences of their wrongdoing rather than it being an arbitrary act of cruelty.

translation: It is indeed a tree that springs up from the bottom (root) of Hell.
interpretation: This verse describes the tree of Zaqqūm — a real, divinely created means of torment in the deepest part of Hell. Its presence and bitter, repulsive fruit symbolize how the very things by which people pursued sinful gratification will be transformed into their punishment: what was sought for pleasure becomes their degrading sustenance. The image emphasizes the extremity and appropriateness of divine justice — that the origins of corruption (a tree growing from the lowest, most base place) yield the vilest consequences for those who chose evil, leaving no refuge from the moral reversal and humiliation of the damned.

translation: Its shoots appeared as if they were the heads of devils.
interpretation: The verse uses a stark visual metaphor: the plant’s growth is described as grotesque and menacing, its shoots like devils’ heads, to convey that what is produced is repulsive and harmful. It warns that outward growth or fruit can be corrupt and dangerous, symbolizing the ugly, ominous consequences of wickedness rather than any life‑giving or good outcome.

translation: For indeed they will eat of it and will fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: The verse is a rebuke of heedless, greedy consumption: people will gorge themselves on what is offered (in context, the tempting provision or forbidden fare) and sates their appetites, showing their preoccupation with worldly satisfaction and insensitivity to moral and spiritual accountability — their filling of the belly symbolizes excess, ingratitude, and neglect of the obligations and warnings that should restrain them.

translation: Then indeed, for them upon it is a scalding, boiling (pouring).
interpretation: The verse signifies that the disbelievers will be overwhelmed by a searing, boiling flood as part of their punishment: the word شوبَة (shobā) conveys a mixing and intense heat that penetrates and burns, turning what might seem like a resource into agonizing torment; it stresses the reality, severity and inevitability of retribution for those who rejected guidance.

translation: Then indeed their return is to Hell.
interpretation: الآية تؤكد حتمية المآل الأخروي للمتمردين: كلمة «مرجعهم» لا تشير إلى عودة مادية فحسب بل إلى المقام النهائي بعد الموت والقيامة، و«ثم» تدل على تسلسل الأسباب والنتائج بحيث يكون العذاب لاحقاً لواقعهم وحالهم الدنيوي، بينما «إن» تضع الأمر في إطار اليقين الإلهي. المقصود بيان ثبوت الجزاء العادل وأن النعيم الدنيوي أو التهاون لا ينجّي من حتمية المحاسبة، فدعوة الآية تذكير بالتوبة والالتزام قبل أن يكون الرجوع إلى ذلك المقام المحتوم.

translation: Indeed, they have made their forefathers go astray.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who perpetuate false beliefs or corrupted practices and thus either lead their ancestors into error or claim their ancestors were misguided; it points to a moral and intellectual failing in which people normalize innovation and deviation, thereby validating and transmitting misguidance across generations instead of adhering to true guidance.

translation:
وَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
"And they hasten along their tracks."
interpretation: It depicts people who, without pausing to examine right or wrong, rush to follow the footsteps of those before them—imitating their practices and errors in haste and thereby speeding themselves toward the same outcome; a warning against unreflective conformity to predecessors' ways.

translation: And indeed many of the earlier peoples went astray before them.
interpretation: This statement serves as a warning grounded in historical pattern: most past communities abandoned divine guidance—by following desires, leaders, or invented doctrines—and suffered the consequences. Its purpose is to urge the present listeners to learn from those failures, turn away from imitation of error, submit to revealed guidance, and avoid the same fate.

translation: And indeed We sent among them warners.
interpretation: God is describing His just and merciful method of guidance: before any judgment reaches a people He dispatches warners—prophets, messengers, or sincere admonishers—to make the truth known and the consequences of rejection clear. The presence of these warners means responsibility lies with those who persist in denial; punishment follows only after a fair opportunity to repent and embrace guidance, so Divine recompense is based on prior admonition and human choice.

translation:
فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُنذَرِينَ
"So observe how was the end of those who were warned."
interpretation: The verse urges reflection on the fates of past peoples who rejected divine warning: their destruction confirms the seriousness and truth of the message and serves as a moral lesson to heed guidance, abandon stubborn denial, and prepare for the final reckoning.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: It indicates that those whose faith and worship are purely for God — free from hypocrisy, ostentation, or association of partners — are set apart and spared from condemnation; sincerity (ikhlāṣ) is presented as the decisive quality that gains God’s protection and acceptance.

translation: And indeed Nūḥ (Noah) called upon Us; and excellent were We as the Responders.
interpretation: The verse affirms an attribute of God—He is the perfect, decisive responder to sincere invocation. By recalling that Noah’s plea was met by God’s intervention, it teaches that turning wholly to God in distress invites His effective help and mercy; the assurance is not merely that God hears, but that He answers in the way and time that serve divine wisdom, making prophetic supplication a model of trust in God’s dependable response.

translation: And We saved him and his household from the great distress.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God, by His mercy and sovereign power, intervened to rescue a righteous person and his believing family from an overwhelming calamity; the phrase “the great distress” stresses that such deliverance was impossible without divine help, teaching that faith, obedience and reliance on God can bring decisive rescue in situations beyond human capacity.

translation: And We made his offspring those who remain.
interpretation: God preserved and sustained that man's progeny so they would endure after him — ensuring his lineage and its continuity, demonstrating Divine power to maintain and perpetuate what He wills.

translation: And We left him among the later generations.
interpretation: The phrase indicates that God preserved this person’s fate — whether punishment or the moral example of his life — so that it remains for subsequent generations as a clear sign and warning: his outcome is kept as a lesson and testimony about the consequences of arrogance, wrongdoing, or disbelief.

translation: Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.
interpretation: A divine commendation that affirms Noah’s vindication and exalted status: God grants him peace and honor as an exemplar whose steadfast faith, patience, and trust transcend his own people, giving his mission universal significance and offering a model for all communities and ages.

translation: Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah, in His justice and mercy, grants fitting recompense to those who practice ihsān—sincere excellence and righteousness; their good deeds are recognized and rewarded appropriately, sometimes through tangible blessings in this life and ultimately through perfected reward in the Hereafter, so genuine moral goodness is never overlooked.

translation: Indeed, he is one of Our believing servants.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that the person belongs to God’s community of true believers: his identity is defined by sincere faith and servitude to God, marking him as divinely recognized, protected, and honored—assured of God’s guidance, mercy, and a place among the faithful.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: تفهم الآية أن الله سبحانه وتعالى أتمّ عقابه الحاسم بالغرق على بقية القوم الذين أصرّوا على الكفر والظلم بعد التذكير والتحذير؛ ولفظة «الآخرين» تشير إلى الذين لم يستجيبوا للدعوة فحلّ بهم الهلاك كقضاء إلهي لا تراجع فيه.

translation: And indeed among his followers is Abraham.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that Abraham belonged to the ranks of those who followed the cause or message just mentioned; his inclusion is offered as authoritative support, linking Abraham’s obedience and monotheistic witness to that same truth and thereby validating and dignifying the party or way being described.

translation: When he comes to his Lord with a sound (pure) heart.
interpretation: The verse means that ultimate acceptance by God rests on the inward condition: to ‘come with a sound heart’ is to stand before God with sincerity, purity of intention and freedom from spiritual corruption (hypocrisy, idolatry, rancor, or undue attachment to worldly gains). It affirms that inner integrity and genuine faith, not wealth, lineage, or mere outward acts, determine one’s standing before the Lord.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: The phrase is a pointed, rhetorical challenge meant to break the complacency of inherited practice: by asking "What do you worship?" the speaker forces his father and community to examine the object and purpose of their devotion, exposing the emptiness of mere tradition or idolatry and inviting them to adopt a conscious, reasoned commitment to the one true God.

translation: Do you desire gods other than Allah?
interpretation: The words confront the spiritual error of giving ultimate trust, love and obedience to transient, powerless substitutes instead of the Creator. It calls for self-examination: to prefer anything other than Allah as the goal of one’s devotion is to invert the proper ordering of allegiance and leads to moral and existential ruin, so one must return to sincere tawḥīd (recognition of God’s exclusive sovereignty and worthiness of worship).

translation: فما ظنكم برب العالمين — "So what do you think of the Lord of the Worlds?"
interpretation: A rhetorical challenge urging inward reckoning: it confronts people with their true conception of God’s lordship and demands that this belief be reflected in their deeds — reminding that how one regards the Sovereign, All‑Knowing, and Just Creator will determine one’s response to guidance and one’s ultimate accountability.

translation: So he cast his gaze upon the stars.
interpretation: The phrase depicts a person turning to the stars in search of help, guidance or authority; symbolically it criticizes the human tendency to place hope and trust in created celestial objects instead of in God, showing that looking to the stars here represents misplaced reliance on signs of creation rather than submission to the Creator.

translation:
فقال: إني سقيمُ
He said, "Indeed, I am ill."
interpretation: He declares a state of physical illness—signaling that bodily weakness or sickness is affecting his condition and accounting for his inability or altered behavior.

translation: So they turned away from him, retreating.
interpretation: An image of willful rejection: the physical act of turning one’s back symbolizes an inward, deliberate refusal to receive guidance. It denotes avoidance and obstinacy — choosing to withdraw from truth and fellowship rather than to listen, accept correction, or engage humbly, thereby separating oneself morally and spiritually from what is right.

translation: فرغ إلى آلهتهم فقال: "ألا تأكلون؟"
interpretation: A rhetorical challenge that exposes the impotence of idols: by asking why the offered provision is not consumed, the speaker underscores that these objects of worship have no life, power, or ability to respond or benefit from what is given, thereby condemning the folly of directing devotion to lifeless things and pointing toward worship of the One who truly hears and acts.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: A rebuke directed at those who remain silent when confronted with clear truth or accusation; their silence is portrayed not as innocence but as evidence of impotence, fear, or obstinate denial—silence itself becomes a tacit confession that exposes their inability or unwillingness to answer and thus heightens their moral and legal responsibility before God.

translation: He unleashed upon them a crushing blow by (His) right hand.
interpretation: It depicts God executing a swift, decisive punishment on those who rejected the truth; the “blow” signifies an overwhelming, chastening torment, and “the right” emphasizes the act’s sovereign authority, firmness and certainty rather than weakness or hesitation.

translation: فأقبلوا إليه يزفون — So they approached him, coming to him in a joyous procession.
interpretation: The verb 'يزفون' frames their approach as a public, celebratory advance rather than a casual visit; it signifies communal approval and honor, a ceremonious reception that conveys joy, triumph, or the bringing of glad tidings to the person they come to.

translation: He said, "Do you worship what you carve?"
interpretation: A rhetorical challenge that exposes the absurdity of directing worship to lifeless objects fashioned by human hands: it points out the inconsistency of attributing divine power or worth to things that are created and dependent, and thereby calls people to recognize the exclusive right of the Creator to receive reverence and obedience rather than his creatures.

translation: And Allah created you and what you do.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute creative sovereignty: He is the source not only of your existence but also of the actions you perform. It therefore denies any true autonomy or divinity in human deeds, calling people to humility and acknowledgment that their lives and acts are ultimately within God’s creative power and subject to His judgment.

translation: They said, "Build for him a high structure, then cast him into the blazing Fire."
interpretation: The verse exposes how tyrants institutionalize cruelty by creating a public spectacle of punishment to intimidate and extinguish conviction; the ordered construction and theatrical execution symbolize organized efforts to suppress truth through fear, condemning both the planners and enablers of such oppression and implying that apparent power used to terrorize does not make injustice legitimate and will be held accountable.

translation: So they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest (of the low).
interpretation: God is saying that those who schemed to harm His servant were not victorious; their plans were overturned and they were publicly humbled and reduced in status — their apparent strength proved empty, and divine justice exposed and degraded them both in worldly standing and ultimately before God.

translation: And he said, “Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.”
interpretation: A concise declaration of surrender and trust: the speaker resolves to place his affairs before God and expects God’s direction. It expresses confident reliance (tawakkul) that when one consciously turns to the Lord, He will show the correct path, ordain what is best, and bring relief or guidance beyond what human planning alone can achieve.

translation: My Lord, grant me from among the righteous.
interpretation: A heartfelt supplication asking that whatever blessing God grants—most directly a child but by extension any gift or companion—be of upright character and faith; it expresses the believer’s priority for moral and spiritual quality in their legacy and relationships, preferring righteousness over mere worldly gain.

translation: So We gave him glad tidings of a forbearing (gentle, patient) son.
interpretation: The word “حليم” emphasizes that God’s gift was not merely a child but one endowed with forbearance and noble character—patience, self‑control, gentleness and wisdom—qualities that make him fit to uphold faith and righteous conduct; the verse thus highlights the importance of moral excellence in the blessing granted.

translation: So when the boy reached the age of exertion, he said, “O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice you; so tell me what you think.” He said, “O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.”
interpretation: The passage illustrates a supreme test of faith in which true submission to God (taslim) and steadfast patience (sabr) are shown as higher obligations than natural attachments. It teaches that sincere belief manifests not merely in outward ritual but in the readiness to surrender one’s dearest possessions and even one’s own life to divine will, trusting that God’s wisdom and mercy transcend apparent hardship; the episode thus elevates trust in God, obedience to His command, and patient acceptance as the core ethical responses in moments of existential trial.

translation:
فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَهَا لِلْجَبِينِ
"So when they submitted and lowered their foreheads (in prostration)."
interpretation: The phrase points to sincere, total submission to God: faith is not merely a verbal claim but a humble inner surrender made manifest by bowing the forehead in prostration — an outward sign that one’s ego, pride and personal will have been humbled before divine authority, marking genuine inward transformation rather than mere lip-service.

translation: And We called to him, “O Abraham.”
interpretation: The divine address by name signals intimate, authoritative selection: when God calls “O Abraham” He singles him out for personal commissioning, guidance, reassurance or test. The form of the call emphasizes both honor and responsibility — Abraham is chosen to receive a message and to embody submission — and it teaches that God’s speech to His servants is direct in purpose, reaching the heart and binding the addressee to the duty or promise that follows.

translation: The vision has come true; indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: God affirms that the prophesied vision has been fulfilled and uses this fulfillment to teach a general moral principle: Allah brings about just outcomes and elevates those who act with goodness, patience, and integrity. The verse indicates that apparent setbacks and trials can be part of a divine process that ultimately recompenses the righteous, showing both God’s wisdom in unfolding events and His faithful reward for moral excellence.

translation: Indeed, this is a manifest trial.
interpretation: The phrase teaches that the events described are an unmistakable test from God, designed to expose people’s true dispositions; its being “manifest” means the trial’s purpose and reality are clear, so the proper response is steadfastness, trust in God, and moral resolve rather than being deceived or derailed by appearances.

translation: And We ransomed him with a mighty sacrifice.
interpretation: The phrase teaches that sincere submission to God is met by Divine deliverance and honor: rather than endorsing human loss, God replaces the threatened trial with a generous, significant provisioning. “Ransomed” emphasizes that rescue comes from God’s mercy, and “a mighty sacrifice” points to the greatness of that mercy and the sanctified, symbolic nature of what is given in place of the trial—affirming that obedience is valued and rewarded by God.

translation: And We left it for him among later generations.
interpretation: The verse indicates that Allah caused a lasting legacy or blessing associated with that person to endure among those who came after him — God preserved his honor, benefit, or progeny so that its effects, recognition, or covenant would continue in subsequent generations by divine decree.

translation: Peace be upon Abraham.
interpretation: A divine pronouncement granting Abraham God’s tranquility and honor, signifying his acceptance and exalted station as a model of faith; it implies that steadfast submission to God brings divine peace and commendation.

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The phrase affirms a consistent divine principle: those who act with moral excellence and sincere benevolence will receive appropriate recompense from God. It reassures the faithful that acts of genuine goodness — rooted in sincerity, patience and righteousness — are not overlooked; God’s justice and mercy respond to them, sometimes by visible blessings in this life and ultimately by reward in the hereafter, even when immediate results are not apparent.

translation: Indeed, he is of Our believing servants.
interpretation: A divine affirmation that the person spoken of is counted among God’s faithful servants — a status earned by sincere belief and upright conduct. It expresses God’s recognition and ownership of that person as part of the community of true believers, conferring honor, protection, and the promise of divine favor; it also points to the criterion for spiritual distinction being inner faith and trustworthiness rather than worldly rank.

translation: And We gave him the glad tidings of Isaac — a prophet, one of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse indicates that God’s promise to Abraham was not merely a personal consolation but the establishment of a divinely guided lineage: the coming of Isaac as a prophet and a man of righteousness confirms that God’s favor produces both continuity of guidance and moral exemplars. It affirms that God answers the faithful in ways that sustain prophetic mission and communal virtue, showing that blessings granted to the patriarchs are part of a larger plan to preserve and transmit divine guidance.

translation: وَبَارَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰ إِسْحَاقَ ۚ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ
interpretation: God affirms that He blessed both Abraham and Isaac, yet their progeny did not all follow the same path: among them were those who acted righteously and at least one who committed clear injustice against his own soul. The phrase “ظالم لنفسه مبين” emphasizes that the wrongdoing was manifest and ultimately self‑destructive, teaching that divine favor on a lineage does not override individual moral responsibility and free choice.

translation: And We certainly bestowed Our favor upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that God specially chose and honored Moses and Aaron by granting them prophetic authority, revelation, clear signs, and assistance against their opponents; saying “We bestowed” (minna) stresses that their status and success were divine gifts, not merely human achievement, so the verse underscores God’s sovereign selection and support as the foundation of their leadership and a model for recognizing true, God‑given guidance.

translation: And We delivered them and their people from the great distress.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God, by His mercy and intervention, can rescue the guided and even their communities from overwhelming calamity or impending punishment; “الكرب العظيم” denotes a severe trial or divine retribution, and the deliverance underscores that salvation comes through God’s mercy—often connected with guidance, repentance, and turning away from wrongdoing—rather than by human means alone.

translation: And We helped them, so they became the ones who prevailed.
interpretation: The phrase teaches that real and lasting triumph is not merely a product of human power but of Divine support: when God grants His assistance to a people who remain faithful, steadfast and obedient to His guidance, He lifts them from weakness to dominance. Their prevailing is thus a sign of God’s favor and a reminder that success and permanence depend ultimately on reliance upon, and alignment with, God’s will rather than on mere numbers or worldly strength.

translation: And We gave them both the clear Book.
interpretation: God bestowed upon the two (those referred to in context) a revealed scripture that is manifest and decisive: a guidance that makes matters clear, distinguishes truth from falsehood, provides authoritative law and proof, and removes ambiguity so people can rightly believe and act.

translation: And We guided them both to the straight path.
interpretation: This states that Allah actively bestowed guidance upon the two referenced individuals (or parties), turning their hearts and faculties toward the path of truth — the way of sincere monotheism, right belief and righteous conduct. “Guided” here implies divine facilitation: opening understanding, removing doubts, and granting the inclination and means to follow the Qur’anic and prophetic way so they remain rightly directed in faith and action.

translation: And We left [it] upon them among the later generations.
interpretation: The phrase indicates that God caused the outcome or mark of those two to endure in the memory and records of subsequent peoples: their case was preserved as a continuing lesson and sign so that later generations would inherit its consequences and learn from it (whether as a warning, an admonition, or an example).

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: A divine salutation affirming God’s favor and vindication of Moses and Aaron—declaring their elevated, righteous status as prophets and the tranquility and reward bestowed upon them, serving as reassurance of God’s approval for those who faithfully fulfill prophetic mission.

translation: Indeed, thus do We recompense the doers of good.
interpretation: God affirms that He appropriately rewards those who act with excellence and righteousness; their good deeds are not overlooked but met with fitting recompense—whether through blessings in this life, inner peace and moral refinement, or the multiplied, everlasting reward in the Hereafter—reflecting divine justice and mercy rather than random favor.

translation: Indeed, they are among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This statement is a divine affirmation that those referred to belong to God’s community of true believers; it signifies not merely an external label but God’s own recognition of their inner faith and allegiance. Being named “from Our believing servants” denotes acceptance, honor, and nearness to God, implying divine protection, guidance, and promise of reward that flow from sincere faith rather than mere outward profession.

translation: And indeed, Ilyās (Elijah) was of the messengers.
interpretation: The verse affirms Ilyās’s status as a divinely appointed prophet, placing him within God’s uninterrupted succession of messengers; its purpose is to remind listeners that prophets are chosen bearers of guidance whose authority and example merit acceptance, and to encourage patience and steadfastness by showing that confronting rejection has been the recurring experience of God's sent guides.

translation: When he said to his people, "Will you not fear (God)?"
interpretation: A sharp prophetic admonition aimed at rousing moral consciousness: the speaker confronts his community’s complacency and calls them to taqwa — a reverent, watchful fear of God that deters injustice and immorality and prompts repentance and obedience to divine guidance, warning that continued heedlessness will lead to consequences.

translation:
أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًا وَتَتْرُكُونَ أَحْسَنَ الْخَالِقِينَ
“Do you call upon Ba‘l and forsake the Best of Creators?”
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who turn for help and devotion to weak, created things or idols (here referenced as Ba‘l) while abandoning the One who is the most perfect Creator. Its point is to expose the irrationality and ingratitude of seeking support from powerless beings and neglecting the Lord whose creative power, sustainment and authority make Him uniquely worthy of trust, worship and invocation.

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.
interpretation: The phrase asserts that God’s lordship is continuous and universal across time: the same Divine Sovereign who was Lord and guide of one’s ancestors remains Lord of the present community. It implies that true religious belonging and duty are rooted in recognizing this enduring, unchanging authority—so worship, allegiance and moral accountability are not innovations but a return to the primordial relationship between humanity and its Creator.

translation: So they denied him; indeed they will surely be brought (present).
interpretation: The verse asserts that those who reject the messenger and the truth will not evade responsibility: their denial will be exposed and they will be assembled and presented before God on the Day of Reckoning to witness the reality they denied and to receive their due judgment.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: It signifies that what distinguishes and saves people before God is inner sincerity (ikhlāṣ): those who truly serve Allah with pure intention and devotion are set apart from others and are exempted from divine rejection or punishment, receiving God's protection and favor rather than being judged by outward show or numbers.

translation: And We left him among those who came after him.
interpretation: God preserved his presence or legacy so that his example, status or its consequences remained with later generations — a deliberate divine leaving of a sign or lesson in the people who followed, that they might recognize, learn from, or be affected by what occurred to him.

translation: Peace be upon the family of Yā­sīn.
interpretation: This is an invocation asking that God’s peace and blessing descend on those associated with “Yā­sīn” (understood in tradition as a name of the Prophet or as the people linked to the surah Yā-Sīn). It expresses reverence and a prayer for divine protection, mercy, and spiritual serenity for that group, acknowledging their honored or sacred status and seeking God’s favor and tranquility for them.

translation: Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The phrase affirms God’s just and generous response to sincere righteousness: Allah does not let genuine good deeds go unrewarded but meets them with fitting, often abundant recompense — which may take the form of inner uplift, protection or provision in this life, forgiveness and elevation of status, and the multiplied, eternal reward in the Hereafter. It teaches that divine reward is measured by sincerity and excellence of intent and action, and that God, in His wisdom, returns good with more than what is outwardly deserved.

translation: Indeed, he is among Our believing servants.
interpretation: The phrase is a divine affirmation that this person is counted among God’s true believers: it denotes God’s recognition and acceptance, implying belonging to the community under His care, assurance of divine support and eventual recompense, and that inner faith — known to God alone — determines one’s standing rather than outward show.

translation: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.
interpretation: The phrase affirms Lūṭ’s prophetic authority and divine commission: he was a genuine Messenger sent by God, not merely a private moralist. By establishing his status, the verse validates his warnings and the legitimacy of the subsequent divine response to his people’s persistent wrongdoing, teaching that God appoints messengers to guide communities and supports them when their message is rejected.

translation: When We delivered him and all his household together.
interpretation: The phrase stresses that salvation is ultimately a gift of God’s will: He can by His mercy and power rescue not only an individual but extend protection to his entire household. It functions as a reminder of divine sovereignty over deliverance—salvation comes by God’s favor and decree, not by human might—and as an encouragement that sincere trust and obedience may be met with comprehensive rescue from calamity.

translation: Except an old woman among those who have passed away.
interpretation: The phrase portrays that of a people destroyed or vanished, only a frail elderly woman remained — a stark image of utter ruin and extinction. It emphasizes how completely a community can be wiped out when it rejects guidance, leaving nothing but a powerless remnant as testimony to its end.

translation: ثم دمرنا الآخرين — Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This phrase teaches that when communities persistently reject guidance and persist in wrongdoing after warnings, God brings decisive punishment upon those remaining or successive groups; it thus emphasizes divine justice and sovereignty, the pattern of warning followed by final accountability, and serves as a warning that persistent collective rebellion has inevitable consequences.

translation: وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ — "And surely you will pass by them in the morning."
interpretation: The phrase affirms the certainty of encountering certain people or a situation at a specific time, teaching that events unfold according to God’s decree; it also warns that mere physical proximity (passing by) does not guarantee recognition or understanding—insight and outcomes occur only when God wills and grants perception.

translation: By the night—will you not understand?
interpretation: The oath “by the night” spotlights the night as a clear, purposeful sign of God’s ordering (rest, concealment, alternation) and is a rhetorical challenge: in light of such manifest signs, people are asked to reflect, use reason, recognize divine wisdom and accountability, and therefore to believe and act rightly.

translation: And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers.
interpretation: The phrase affirms Yunus’s legitimate status as a divinely appointed messenger: his story—marked by hardship, apparent withdrawal, sincere repentance, and deliverance—serves to show that God’s messengers are chosen despite human frailty, that trials do not nullify prophetic office, and that God’s mercy restores and vindicates those whom He commissions, offering believers a model of turning back to God with humility and trust.

translation: When it sailed off with them into the laden ship.
interpretation: This terse description is offered as a sign: the progress and apparent security of a heavily laden ship are not the result of human autonomy but of God’s ordering of wind, sea and means. What people take for safe, self-sustaining transport is actually sustained by Divine power and provision, a reminder to recognize God’s lordship, be grateful, and remember that any worldly security can be altered by His will.

translation: So he took part in it, and thus became among the abased.
interpretation: The phrase warns that by joining in wrongdoing, denial, or mockery one renders oneself complicit and shares its fate: when the falsehood or injustice is exposed, those who participated are counted among the disgraced and refuted. In other words, active participation in evil or rejection of truth results in being rejected, humiliated and held accountable, both morally and before God.

translation: So the fish swallowed him, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: The phrase mu·līm denotes a state of reproach, humiliation and inward remorse; the verse teaches that when a servant departs into error or heedlessness, God may subject him to a humiliating trial that exposes his fault and drives him into sincere self‑reproach, turning him from reliance on his own way back to true repentance and trust in God — trials thus serve as means of spiritual correction and return rather than mere punishment.

translation: But for the fact that he was among those who glorify (Allah).
interpretation: This phrase indicates that the person’s continual glorification and remembrance of God (tasbih) was the decisive reason he was treated differently—spared, exalted, or accepted. It teaches that sincere, habitual praise of Allah shapes one’s spiritual status: such constant devotion draws God’s mercy and protection, marks a believer as distinct, and can avert punishment or loss because the act itself evidences closeness to and trust in God.

translation: to remain in its womb until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: The phrase likens the grave/earth to a womb: those who die are placed into a hidden, formative state under God’s will, preserved and confined until He commands their re-emergence on Resurrection Day. The image emphasizes both human helplessness before God’s timing and His sovereign power to return the dead to life, serving as consolation for believers and a reminder of final accountability.

translation: So We cast him out onto the bare plain, and he was sick.
interpretation: The verse uses the image of someone thrown out onto open, barren ground while ill to convey divine withdrawal of protection and the resulting vulnerability and humiliation. It teaches that turning away from God’s guidance can lead to exposure and helplessness — a reminder of human frailty and that true dignity and security depend on God rather than on worldly support.

translation: And We caused a gourd-plant to grow over him.
interpretation: The gourd represents God’s merciful, immediate provision and protection: in a time of need He brings forth a humble but life-restoring blessing that shelters, nourishes, and visibly transforms hardship into relief — a sign meant to awaken gratitude and trust in Divine care.

translation: And We sent him to one hundred thousand, or more.
interpretation: The phrase highlights the vast scope of the prophetic mission: God’s messenger was sent to a very large number of people, signaling both the universal reach of the call and the heavy responsibility placed upon the prophet. The rounded figure (‘a hundred thousand or more’) serves to stress magnitude rather than provide a literal census, teaching that guidance was offered broadly, requiring perseverance, compassion, and divine support in addressing the needs of a multitude.

translation: So they believed, and We granted them enjoyment for a while.
interpretation: It signifies that when people truly embraced faith, God accepted them and permitted them temporal comforts and ease in this life as a mercy and a test; that enjoyment is deliberately limited (“for a while”) to remind believers that worldly good is transient and their faith’s sincerity and perseverance will be judged by God in the end.

translation: So ask them: “Are the daughters for your Lord, and for them the sons?”
interpretation: A rhetorical rebuke of the pagan practice of assigning familial roles to the divine: the verse exposes the absurdity of claiming God has daughters while humans keep sons for themselves. It condemns this projection of human, gender‑biased preferences onto God, stresses God’s transcendence beyond such human family relations, and undermines the theological and social justification those beliefs gave for worshiping idols or for privileging sons over daughters.

translation: Or did We create the angels as females — and are they (then) witnesses?
interpretation: The verse uses rhetorical irony to refute the pagan claim that God has daughters: it exposes the absurdity of attributing human-like offspring or familial relations to the Divine and of imagining angels as divine female progeny or authoritative witnesses to such a claim. Angels are created servants who carry out God’s command, not divine descendants or independent witnesses, and those who assert otherwise are projecting human categories onto God without any valid testimony.

translation: ألا إنهم من إفكهم ليقولون — Behold, they, out of their own fabrications, indeed say (such things).
interpretation: The verse indicts those who habitually invent and spread falsehoods: their statements are products of their own imagination rather than of truth or divine guidance, revealing moral corruption and warning believers not to accept or be swayed by assertions that originate in such fabricated claims.

translation: “Allah has begotten (a son).” Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse rejects and condemns the claim that Allah has offspring, asserting His absolute oneness and transcendence; attributing human-like begetting to the Divine is false and incompatible with the core monotheistic understanding of God.

translation: He chose (or preferred) daughters over sons.
interpretation: It expresses that a choice or preference was given to daughters instead of sons; interpreted as a remark about a reversed or misguided valuation — an assertion that someone (contextually the one spoken of) favored daughters in a way that runs counter to the expected or proper ordering, thereby highlighting an error or misplaced preference.

translation: What is the matter with you that you judge (thus)?
interpretation: A sharp rebuke of those who pass judgment hastily or unjustly: it confronts people who rule according to whims, faction, or ignorance rather than by sound evidence and divine guidance, urging humility, restraint, and adherence to justice and truth when making decisions.

translation: أفلا تذكرون — Will you not remember (and take heed)?
interpretation: A rhetorical admonition urging the hearers to cease heedlessness and actively recall and reflect on the clear signs or reminders already presented; it calls for an inward response—recognition of God’s truth, moral reckoning, repentance or continued obedience—rather than mere outward hearing.

translation: Or do you have a clear authority?
interpretation: A rhetorical challenge demanding that the addressees produce an explicit, unmistakable proof or legitimate authorization for their position; it implies that unless they can show such a manifest, decisive authority, their claim or rejection lacks foundation and cannot be accepted.

translation:
فَأْتُوا بِكِتَابِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
“Then bring your book, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: A direct, rhetorical challenge to opponents: if they truly possess written authority or evidence for their claims, they should produce it now. The demand exposes the absence of such corroborating scripture and thus calls attention to the weakness or dishonesty of assertions made without verifiable proof.

translation: They set up a kinship between him and Paradise; and indeed Paradise knows that they are surely to be brought (before it).
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who invent or appeal to familial ties, lineage, or false intermediaries as a supposed guarantee of entry to Paradise. Such claims fabricate a spurious connection that people rely on to escape responsibility; but the reality of the Hereafter is not deceived—Paradise (and the final reckoning) knows the truth, and those who trust in these false links will be brought forth and held to account rather than granted the reward they presumed.

translation: Glory be to Allah, far above what they ascribe to Him.
interpretation: This declares Allah’s absolute transcendence and purity from any false descriptions or attributions—He is above being likened to creation, assigned partners, or given improper human-like traits—so one must reject anthropomorphism, idolatry, and ignorant claims about His nature and affirm His unique, incomparable Lordship.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: It refers to those whose faith and worship are purely devoted to God alone—people purified of hypocrisy and selfish motives, whose inner sincerity and steadfast obedience distinguish them and secure for them God’s special favor, protection, and acceptance.

translation: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ
interpretation: A declarative address that places the people and their objects of worship side by side: both are created, powerless, and transient, so their presumed partnership with the One God is futile—those who cling to other deities are warned that neither they nor their idols can ultimately avert judgment or confer true benefit, underscoring the sole sovereignty and worthiness of Allah.

translation: You will not be able to lead him astray by any temptation.
interpretation: ثبات المخاطَب على الحق وعدم قدرة الآخرين على إغرائه أو صرفه عنه بالفتن.

translation: Except for him who is cast into Hell.
interpretation: The phrase draws an exception: all others are exempt from the stated outcome except the person who is overtaken by the Fire. "صال الجحيم" depicts one who is condemned to and dwelling in Hell — someone whose persistent rejection of guidance and sinful course places him beyond mercy and makes him a rightful subject of its torment.

translation: And there is none of us but has an appointed/known station.
interpretation: The verse affirms that every person in the referenced group has a specific, divinely ordained position or fate: God knows and has set each individual’s standing, role, or recompense, so nothing about one's ultimate place is arbitrary but measured and determined within God’s just and wise plan.

translation: And indeed, We are the Purifiers.
interpretation: God asserts that He is the One who sanctifies the righteous: by His mercy and decree He cleanses their spiritual defilements, elevates their moral state, and admits them among the pure in His presence—their true purification and honour come from Him alone.

translation: And indeed, it is We who are the ones who glorify (Him).
interpretation: The phrase asserts that the speaker’s fundamental identity is continual glorification of God: praising and declaring His purity is not an occasional act but the essential, perpetual activity that defines them, emphasizing an intrinsic, unceasing devotion that proceeds from their very nature.

translation: And indeed they would say
interpretation: The phrase functions as an emphatic marker reporting habitual or repeated speech: by using ل before the verb and كان in the imperfect, the Qurʾān highlights that a group persistently and characteristically voiced a particular claim or objection, framing what follows as an entrenched, recurring assertion rather than a one‑time remark.

translation: If only we had a reminder from those who went before us.
interpretation: The phrase reflects an excuse offered by people confronted with a new divine warning: they claim they would heed it only if they had a precedent or admonition from earlier generations. It points to a psychological tendency to demand external, familiar proof or historical precedent as a way to evade responsibility for recognizing present guidance — a form of deflection that ignores that earlier peoples likewise received warnings and that such appeals cannot justify rejection.

translation: But we are the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: The phrase asserts a declared identity and intention: the speakers present themselves as devoted servants whose worship and conduct are motivated solely by sincerity toward Allah. It marks a moral contrast with those who act for show or personal gain, emphasizing inner purity (ikhlāṣ), humble submission, and consistent obedience as the true signs of servanthood rather than outward appearances or rhetoric.

translation: But they disbelieved in it; soon they will know.
interpretation: The phrase warns that rejection of the divine message does not nullify its truth or the coming of God's decree; in due course the deniers will be made to recognize what they denied—whether by clear signs, manifest consequences, or an unavoidable inner conviction—so their prior denial will be overturned and they will face the reality and its accountability.

translation: And indeed, Our word has gone forth beforehand concerning Our servants, the messengers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s decree and purpose are preordained and have been communicated through His chosen servants—the prophets. In other words, what the messengers brought (warnings, promises, and judgments) is not mere human speech but the prior, authoritative word of God whose unfolding is certain: the sending of messengers and the outcomes they proclaimed were part of God’s predetermined plan and will come to pass according to His decree.

translation: Indeed, they are surely those who are granted victory.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the people being spoken of will receive decisive, divinely‑given support: their success is ordained by God and results from His aid rather than merely their own power. It reassures the faithful that perseverance and trust in God will lead to ultimate triumph—whether over enemies, oppression, or spiritual trials—because God makes them victorious.

translation: And indeed, Our hosts are surely victorious over them.
interpretation: It declares that by God’s authority the forces He appoints—whether understood as angels, heavenly hosts, or the agents of His power—will decisively overcome those who oppose or transgress His command; the verse affirms the certainty of divine support and the inevitability of justice, reassuring the faithful that resistance to God’s will is futile and that truth will ultimately prevail by His might.

translation: Then turn away from them for a while.
interpretation: A directive to refrain from continued disputation with stubborn rejecters: withdraw temporarily rather than exhaust yourself in fruitless argument, entrust their guidance and reckoning to God, preserve your dignity and energy, and await the time when God’s judgment or softened hearts will make further engagement meaningful.

translation: And We will make them see, and they will soon see.
interpretation: It promises that God will, at the appointed moment (most clearly manifest on the Day of Judgment), unveil the truth and the consequences of people’s choices so unmistakably that those who denied or turned away will finally perceive what they refused in life; their excuses will be removed and the reality will be plain and inescapable.

translation: Do they, then, seek to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: A rebuke of those who, from malice, impatience, or mockery, demand that God’s punishment come immediately; it exposes their ignorance and arrogance — they cannot accelerate or control God’s decree, and their eager wish for instant retribution only reveals their hostility and will not alter divine timing or justice.

translation: So when it descends upon their precincts, wretched indeed is the morning for those who were warned.
interpretation: The verse warns that when divine retribution strikes the places of the heedless, it will bring utter ruin and despair at the very moment of realization. “Morning” here symbolizes the abrupt, irreversible hour of reckoning when the warned ones — those who received admonition but persisted in denial or negligence — find their hopes overturned and suffer the full consequences of their refusal to heed the warning. It emphasizes both the certainty of punishment for persistent rejection and the suddenness and helplessness of that experience.

translation: وَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ — "And turn away from them for a while."
interpretation: An instruction to refrain from further contention with those whose hearts are closed: withdraw temporarily from fruitless dispute, preserve dignity and patience, continue the mission without being drawn into vain argument, and trust God to guide or deal with them in His time.

translation: وَأَبْصِرْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ — And look; soon they will see.
interpretation: An address to the Prophet to take heed and observe: the present denial and blindness of the rejecters will not remain hidden — in the near future they will be compelled to witness the truth and the consequences of their rejection, when clear signs and divine judgment expose what they refused to acknowledge.

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might; He is free from what they ascribe to Him.
interpretation: The verse declares God’s absolute transcendence: ‘Subhan’ negates any imperfection or likeness, ‘Lord of Might’ affirms His sovereign, inviolable majesty, and ‘above what they describe’ rejects every human-made attribution, partner, or anthropomorphic depiction. It teaches that human language and imagination cannot capture God’s essence, and therefore the descriptions ascribed to Him by those who err are false and unbecoming of His true, transcendent reality.

translation: وَسَلَامٌ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ
interpretation: تحية إلهية وتثبيت لهم؛ تعني أن الله يمنح الأنبياء والرسل سلامًا وأمانًا واعتبارًا لقيامهم بأمانة البلاغ، وتختتم بذلك خصومة الدنيويّين مع انتصار رسالة الحق وضرورة احترام قدْر الرسل والاقتداء بما جاؤوا به.

translation: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that every form of true praise, gratitude, and recognition belongs solely to God; by calling Him "Rabb al-‛Alamin" it emphasizes His absolute dominion, care, and providential governance over all realms (visible and invisible), so the believer is reminded that all blessings, authority, and moral order originate from Him and therefore the proper human response is submission, thankfulness, and reliance on His guidance.

translation:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. ص. والقرآن ذي الذكر
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Ṣād. By the Qur’an, the Reminder.
interpretation: The detached letter ‘Ṣād’ serves to arrest attention and signal the gravity of what follows: God swears by the Qur’an, naming it dhī al-dhikr — intrinsically a living reminder. The oath highlights the Qur’an’s role as a preserved, decisive admonition that awakens hearts, corrects falsehood, and calls people back to God; it is not mere information but a moral and spiritual summons whose truth and consequence demand reflection and response.

translation: بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق
interpretation: The verse indicates that the disbelievers remain entrenched in proud self-sufficiency and a willful breaking away: their arrogance leads them to reject divine guidance and to foster dissension and estrangement from God and from rightly ordered community, so their stance is one of obstinate pride and divisive rupture.

translation:
كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ فَنَادَوْا فَلَا حِينَ مَنَاصٍ
“How many a generation have We destroyed before them; they cried out (for help), but there was no time for deliverance.”
interpretation: The verse warns that many past communities were punished after persisting in rejection and wrongdoing; when calamity finally overtook them they pleaded, but their cries came too late and could not avert the divine decree. It teaches that last‑minute fear and supplication, after persistent denial of guidance, will not necessarily save a people — sincere response and reform before punishment is what averts destruction.

translation: And they were astonished that a warner had come to them from among themselves; and the disbelievers said, “This is a magician, a liar.”
interpretation: The verse highlights a common human response to inconvenient truth: when a caller to guidance arises from their own community, people often refuse to engage with the message and instead attack the messenger’s character—labeling him a sorcerer or liar—to avoid facing blame, loss of status, or change. This reaction reveals pride and moral stubbornness: denying truth by discrediting its bearer rather than honestly weighing the arguments.

translation: Shall I make the gods One God? Indeed, this is a strange thing.
interpretation: The wording conveys the incredulous stance of those who cling to multiple deities: they find the notion of divine unity absurd not because of reason but because of attachment, prejudice, and social habit. By presenting their reaction, the verse exposes a deeper moral and cognitive resistance—people who are bound to plural gods will dismiss monotheism as unbelievable, and that dismissal itself is what the text indicts.

translation:
وَانطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا وَاصْبِرُوا عَلَىٰ آلِهَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ يُرَادُ
"And the chiefs among them departed, saying, ‘Go on and remain firm in your worship of your gods; indeed, this is something intended (a devised matter).’"
interpretation: The verse portrays the leaders’ reaction as defensive and calculating: rather than engage with the truth of the message, they urge the people to cling to familiar idols and dismiss the claimant as a schemer. Their words reveal that rejection is not merely ignorance but a deliberate stance to preserve existing authority, customs, and power structures by discrediting the new claim as a contrivance.

translation: We have not heard of anything like this in the later religion; indeed, this is nothing but a fabrication.
interpretation: الآية تبيّن موقفَ المشركين والمُنكِرين الذين يرفضون رسالةً جديدة فبدلاً من تمحيص دلائلها يصفونها بالاختلاق لأنّها تُخالف موروثهم ومعتقداتهم؛ فهي تظهِر تعصّبهم وجهلهم وعدم استعدادهم لقبول حقّ جديد رغم وضوحه.

translation: Was the Reminder sent down to him from among Us? Nay — they are in doubt about My remembrance; nay, until they taste a punishment.
interpretation: The verse rejects the notion that the revelation originated from some being ‘among us’ and instead diagnoses the real problem: people’s persistent doubt and rejection of God’s reminder. The repeated negations stress that it is not the source of the message that fails but the hearts that refuse to accept it; they will remain unconvinced until they experience the consequences (the punishment) that reveal the truth of what they denied.

translation: Or do they have the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that mercy and all divine bounty are the exclusive, inexhaustible possessions of God; He alone controls and dispenses guidance, forgiveness and provision according to His wisdom. Human beings cannot claim ownership, entitlement, or the right to withhold or bestow God's mercy — any arrogance that pretends such control is false, since only the Almighty Bestower determines who receives His favors.

translation: Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them? Then let them ascend by the means (the causes).
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge showing the impossibility of human (or idol) claims to independent sovereignty: even if someone were to assert ownership of the heavens and earth, the verse invites them to climb the chain of causes to prove it — a demand no created being can meet. “Let them ascend in the causes” exposes that all power is mediated through contingent means and that ultimate control over existence belongs to God alone; those who claim such ownership are thus shown to be powerless and dependent, unable to transcend the very causes they invoke.

translation:
جُنُودٌ — هُنَالِكَ مَاهُزُومٌ مِنَ الأَحْزَابِ
"Troops — there the Confederates were defeated."
interpretation: The phrase indicates that the enemy’s forces, though seeming strong, were routed by God’s decree; its lesson is that apparent worldly power can be overturned by divine will, so believers should trust in God’s support rather than rely solely on numbers or alliances.

translation: قبلهم كُذِّبَتْ أقوامُ نوحٍ وعادٍ وفرعونُ ذو الأوتادِ
interpretation: الآية تذكر بأن أمماً وحكاماً كانوا شديدي القوة والتمكّن ولكنهم مع ذلك رفضوا الهدى فدُبر أمرهم؛ «ذو الأوتاد» يبيّن صفة الاستقرار والصلابة الظاهرة لدى الظالمين، والقصص التاريخية هنا تحذر أن العزة المادية والثبات الظاهر لا يحمِي من محاسبة الله ولا من الهزيمة إذا صاحبها تكبّر ورفض للحق، فالعبرة بالالتزام بالهدى وليس بالمظاهر.

translation: And Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the companions of the thicket—those were the factions.
interpretation: The verse lists communities that were destroyed for rejecting their messengers and labels them al‑Ahzab (the factions), stressing that their defining characteristic was organized, collective opposition to divine guidance: they were groups united in corrupt customs and resistance to the truth, and their fate illustrates that numbers, alliances, or entrenched social cohesion do not protect a people from divine accountability when they persist in wrongdoing.

translation:
إِنَّ كُلَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمْ ٱلْعِقَابُ
"Indeed, those who denied the messengers brought upon themselves deserved punishment."
interpretation: The verse asserts a moral cause-and-effect: persistent rejection of prophetic warnings does not remain morally neutral but leads to divine accountability. It emphasizes that God’s punishment is not arbitrary but a just consequence for communities that persist in denying guidance; the admonition is to recognize prophetic truth and reform, lest one be encompassed by the inevitable consequences of stubborn denial.

translation:
وما ينظر هؤلاء إلا صيحة واحدة ما لها من فواق
"They will perceive nothing but a single cry; there will be no interval in it."
interpretation: The verse teaches the suddenness and irrevocability of the Hour: resurrection comes by one single blast of the trumpet that has no repetition or pause (فواق), so there is no opportunity for delay, escape, or a second chance — all are instantly raised and held accountable.

translation:
وَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا عَجِّلْ لَنَا قِطَّانَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ
“And they will say, ‘Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning.’”
interpretation: The verse portrays the plea of those who prefer immediate, worldly relief or reward over preparing for the final judgment; it exposes their desire to secure their allotted pleasures or respite now rather than to face accountability, showing spiritual short-sightedness and a priority of temporal comforts above repentance and lasting, righteous deeds.

translation: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant David, the possessor of might; indeed he was oft-returning [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse presents David as a model: though endowed with power and authority (“the possessor of might”), his true excellence was constant humility and repeated turning to God (“awwāb”). By linking patience in the face of others’ speech with the example of David, the verse teaches that real strength is accompanied by endurance under provocation and by continual repentance and reliance on God — power without humble return to the Divine is incomplete, and believers should emulate David’s combination of steadfastness and perpetual return to Allah.

translation: Indeed, We made the mountains subject to him; they would glorify (praise) [God] with him at evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God bestowed upon the prophet a miraculous concord between his devotion and the created world: the mountains’ participation in ‘tasbih’ symbolizes both a real, divinely-wrought support for his mission and the deeper truth that sincere prophetic worship brings the cosmic order into harmony with God’s praise. It emphasizes that divine favor can make even the immovable world responsive to spiritual leadership, signifying the truth and weight of the prophet’s call.

translation: And the birds are gathered together; each has an appointed place to return to.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s precise governance of creation: birds assemble and then go back to their ordained dwellings according to God‑given instincts and timing. This orderly pattern shows that every created being has a fixed, God‑assigned course and home, a visible sign of divine wisdom and control that reminds people of the certainty of returning to their Lord and calls them to acknowledge His sovereignty and turn back to Him.

translation: وَشَدَدْنَا مملكته وآتيناه الحكمة وفصل الخطاب — "And We strengthened his kingdom, and granted him wisdom, and perfected/clarified his speech."
