The passage thus condemns clinging to ancestral customs in the face of truth and shows that acceptance of guidance depends on sincere readiness to follow it, not merely on lineage or habit.

translation: So We took vengeance on them; then behold how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: The verse functions as a warning and evidential lesson: by directing attention to the fate of those who denied the truth, it calls people to learn from history — the ruin of persistent rejection demonstrates that rejecting clear guidance has real consequences, and sober reflection on those outcomes should strengthen belief and correct conduct.

translation: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, ‘Indeed, I disown what you worship,’
interpretation: This statement expresses Abraham’s clear and principled repudiation of idol-worship: he publicly severs spiritual allegiance to the objects and customs of his kin because they contradict tawhid (the oneness of God). It illustrates the prophetic duty to stand for truth even against close family, showing that genuine faith may require a decisive moral and social separation from inherited falsehoods and functions as a summons for others to reexamine and abandon those practices.

translation: Except the One who created me — He will surely guide me.
interpretation: The speaker expresses absolute reliance on God as the sole Creator and therefore the true Source of guidance: because He brought the speaker into existence and knows his nature and purpose, He is trusted to lead him along the right way. The phrase conveys firm confidence that divine guidance — in decisions, trials, and the path to ultimate success — will be granted by the Creator rather than by any other power.

translation: And He made it an enduring word among his offspring, that they might return.
interpretation: The verse indicates that God transforms Joseph’s ordeal into a lasting, living legacy within his descendants — not merely a historical tale but a preserved moral and spiritual truth transmitted through the generations so that, by encountering this example, his people may be moved to repentance, reform, and a return to true belief and obedience.

translation: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly prosperity granted to a people and their ancestors is not proof of divine approval but can be a temporary respite or test; when the definitive truth and a clear messenger reach them, that marks the point of obligation and responsibility, so continued rejection thereafter incurs accountability despite prior ease.

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, “This is sorcery, and indeed we are, concerning it, disbelievers.”
interpretation: The verse shows that when clear divine guidance confronts people whose hearts are closed by pride, interest, or fear, they refuse to accept it and instead label it as ‘magic’ to discredit and avoid its demands; the statement reflects a deliberate, defensive rejection of truth motivated by stubbornness and attachment to falsehood rather than by genuine evaluation of the evidence.

translation: And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not revealed to a great man from one of the two cities?"
interpretation: The verse exposes a common arrogance: people demand that divine guidance be endorsed by worldly rank and prestige. By insisting revelation ought to come through a powerful, prominent figure, they reveal that their standard for accepting truth is social status rather than evidence or moral responsibility; the remark therefore criticizes the vain criterion of authority and the refusal to submit to guidance simply because it comes by a humble messenger.

translation: Do they then apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned their livelihood among them in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees so that some may make use of others as servants; and the mercy of your Lord is better than what they amass.
interpretation: The verse admonishes those who act as if they can allocate or claim God’s mercy by equating worldly advantage with divine favor. It explains that God alone dispenses provision and differences of rank in this life as part of a test and social ordering, not as a licence for arrogance or to deny others’ rights. Ultimately, what truly matters and endures is the mercy of the Lord—His forgiveness, guidance and final reward—which surpasses all temporal wealth, status, and what people gather in this world.

translation: And if the people were but one single community, We would surely have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful the roofs of their houses of silver and stairways on them whereby they would ascend.
interpretation: The verse implies that God is perfectly able to grant even the disbelievers conspicuous worldly splendor, but He withholds making such universal, ostentatious prosperity the norm so that moral testing and distinction among people remain meaningful. By not turning the world into a single, uniformly prosperous society for all, divine wisdom preserves the arena for free choice, separates believers from disbelievers, and ensures that true worth is measured by faith and conduct rather than by visible material show.

translation: And for their houses [are] doors, and couches upon which they recline.
interpretation: The verse portrays the dwellings of the righteous in Paradise as deliberately furnished and dignified: the presence of doors signals protected, private, and orderly abodes rather than chaotic or exposed quarters, while the couches on which they recline convey ease, honor, leisurely companionship and permanent comfort. Together these details emphasize that the hereafter’s rewards are not only spiritual but concretely arranged to provide restful dignity, privacy and social delight—an intentional, fitting provision in contrast to worldly hardship and insecurity.

translation: وَزُخْرُفًا ۚ وَإِنَّ كُلَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۚ وَالْآخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
interpretation: الآية تبيّن أن الزينة والمباهج الدنيوية كلها متاع زائل وامتحان، وأن القيمة الحقيقية والثواب الباقي ليست في هذه المظاهر العابرة بل في الآخرة التي أعدّها الله للمتقين؛ وبذلك تدعو إلى توجيه الاهتمام من التلاحق وراء الزخارف إلى بناء التقوى والعمل الصالح لأن ذلك هو طريق نيل الجزاء الدائم عند الرب.

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful — We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes a companion to him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that abandoning regular remembrance of God creates spiritual vulnerability: God permits a satanic influence to attach itself to such a person, not merely as an external tempter but as an intimate, persistent companion that whispers, rationalizes, and strengthens heedlessness. Rather than leaving the soul neutral, turning away from dhikr opens the heart to a steady inner force that hardens it, increases inclination to sin, and perpetuates distance from guidance.

translation: And indeed they turn them away from the way, and they think that they are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse indicts those who, by their behavior, rulings or influence, divert people from God’s straight path while remaining convinced of their own correctness. It highlights the danger of self-deception: outward certainty and confidence do not equal true guidance when practice and principle are opposed to divine instruction. Leaders and communities who mislead others will be held accountable, for sincere belief in one’s rightness cannot justify causing others to stray.

translation: “Until, when he came to Us, he said, ‘Would that there were between me and you the distance of the two easts!’ What an evil companion!”
interpretation: The verse shows the utter despair and vain wish of the wrongdoer at the moment of standing before God — he longs for an impossible, vast separation (“the distance of the two easts”) to escape reckoning. “Evil companion” points to the deceiver who accompanied him in life (the Devil or his own corrupt inclinations): that companion’s guidance proved disastrous, leaving him ruined and alone before divine judgement.

translation: And it will not benefit you today, when you have done wrong, that you are partners in the punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that on the Day of Reckoning any claim to shared status or alliance will not save those who committed injustice; being part of a group, invoking common ties, or arguing that others share the blame will not avert divine punishment. Accountability rests on one’s deeds, and collective association cannot dilute individual responsibility before God.

translation:
أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين
“Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind? And whoever is in manifest error...”
interpretation: The verse uses deafness and blindness as metaphors for spiritual incapacity or wilful refusal to receive guidance. It reminds that the Prophet’s role is to convey the message clearly; he cannot force inner perception or acceptance. True guidance — the opening of hearts and insight — is granted by God, so those entrenched in evident misguidance who close themselves to the signs will not be made to understand despite external proofs. The passage thus emphasizes human responsibility to respond and the limits of the messenger’s power: deliver the truth faithfully, while leaving the granting of guidance to God.

translation: So if We were to take you away, then indeed We would be avengers against them.
interpretation: A reassurance from God to the Prophet that his removal (e.g., by death or departure) would not frustrate divine justice: God Himself will requite and hold accountable those who persecuted or rejected the message. The verse emphasizes that ultimate redress rests with God, who will punish wrongdoers in due measure rather than leaving justice to human hands.

translation: Or shall We show you that which We have threatened them with? Indeed, We are over them All‑Powerful.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical address assuring the Prophet and the community that the threatened punishment for the rejecters is real and that God has full power to bring it about at any time. It underlines that divine forbearance is not inability but a deliberate restraint: God controls the timing and execution of His promise, so the delay of punishment is part of His wisdom and mercy, while its eventual fulfillment is certain because He is wholly capable of enforcing it.

translation: So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: This is a divine exhortation to maintain unwavering commitment to the revelation as the decisive guide for belief and conduct: by clinging to God’s message rather than being swayed by ridicule, pressure, or personal desires, one preserves moral clarity and spiritual integrity—such perseverance is both the proof that one is rightly guided and the means of remaining on the correct path.

translation: And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people; and you will surely be questioned.
interpretation: The verse tells the Prophet that the Qur’an is not mere words but a deliberate admonition directed at him and his community, and it warns that they will be held accountable. “You will surely be questioned” emphasizes personal and communal responsibility: recipients of the message will be asked by God about how they received, conveyed, and acted upon this reminder, so the passage functions both as consolation for the Prophet (that he fulfilled his duty in conveying guidance) and as a solemn warning that acceptance and conduct will be examined on the Day of Recompense.

translation: وَاسْأَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَا أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ الرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ
interpretation: Allah commands to question the messengers sent before Muhammad as a way of exposing the absurdity of assigning divinity to anything besides the Merciful. The verse functions rhetorically: it points out that God never appointed partners or gods to be worshipped, and that the consistent testimony of the prophets rejects the deification of created beings. Its purpose is to undermine polytheistic claims by appealing to the continuous prophetic message that true worship belongs to God alone.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs; he said, “Indeed, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that prophetic authority derives from God’s commissioning and is confirmed by divine signs, so prophets must confront concentrated worldly power with that mandate; legitimacy before God—not political rank—determines truth, obliging the messenger to deliver the warning and guidance to rulers and their circles regardless of resistance.

translation: So when Our signs came to them, behold, they would laugh at them.
interpretation: This verse points to the inner reality behind rejecting revelation: mockery functions as a defensive posture born of pride, attachment to existing interests, and refusal to submit to moral truth. Laughing at the signs is not neutral amusement but a deliberate act that belittles guidance to preserve self‑image and social position; the passage therefore indicts the mocker’s moral blindness and warns that ridicule cannot negate truth nor remove responsibility for one’s rejection.

translation: And We show them no sign except that it is greater than its predecessor; and We seized them with punishment so that perhaps they might return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God presented people with a succession of ever-more compelling signs (each superseding the previous in clarity or force), yet when they persisted in rejection He allowed chastisement to overtake them. That punishment is not presented as mere retribution alone but as a corrective, mercy-laden instrument intended to shock them into recognition and repentance — a stern wake-up designed to bring the obstinate back to the right path. It also warns that continued denial in the face of increasingly clear evidence will lead to decisive consequences.

translation: And they said, “O magician, call upon your Lord for us by what He has promised you; indeed we will be guided.”
interpretation: The verse exposes a conditional, opportunistic response to apparent supernatural power: people demand that the one who manifests extraordinary ability invoke God’s promise as a proof or concession, and only then will they claim to be guided. It highlights insincere acceptance of truth—seeking miracles or favors as bargaining chips rather than approaching guidance with genuine faith and submission to God’s message.

translation:
فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ العَذَابَ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ
"But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke (their covenant)."
interpretation: The verse indicates that when God lifts a chastisement and people are granted relief, some respond with ingratitude and immediately return to violating their covenant with God — abandoning faith, commandments, or promises they had made. It teaches that divine respite can be a test of sincerity, and that mercy should lead to steadfastness and repentance rather than complacency or renewed disobedience; those who 'break' in this way forfeit the trust placed in them and risk the return of divine accountability.

translation: And Pharaoh cried out among his people, "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers run beneath me? Will you not then see?"
interpretation: The verse highlights Pharaoh’s arrogant appeal to visible, material signs—political dominion and control over life‑giving rivers—as proof of his legitimacy and superiority. By flaunting wealth and control of natural resources he seeks to silence doubt and bind his people to him, equating worldly power with rightness. The implied lesson is that external prosperity and authority are not evidence of moral truth or divine approval; pride in material advantage can blind leaders and societies to justice and guidance, making apparent strength a poor criterion for discerning right from wrong.

translation: أم أنا خيرٌ من هذا الذي هو مهينٌ ولا يكاد يبين؟
interpretation: الآية تُظهِر سؤالاً استنكاريّاً ينبع من غطرسة شخص يدّعي أنه أرفع منزلة من الآخر لأن هذا الآخر مُحتقَرٌ في أعين الناس ولا يجيد الكلام أو التعبير؛ تفسيرها أن بعض الناس يرفضون الحق ليس لضعفه بل لأن حاملَه يُعتبر دون مرتبتهم الاجتماعية أو لغته غير فصيحة، فالمقولة تكشف عن حُكمٍ ظالمٍ ومتكبّرٍ يقيس القيمة بالهيبة الظاهرة والبلاغة الخارجية ويرفض التحقق من الحقيقة بذاتها.

translation:
فَلَوْلا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ
"So why was not a bracelet of gold cast upon him, or why did not the angels come to him in company?"
interpretation: The verse exposes the misplaced criterion of people who demand spectacular, worldly proofs—luxury trappings or an angelic entourage—as the basis for belief. Its point is that divine truth is validated by its guidance and moral evidence, not by theatrical displays; God does not manufacture ostentation to force assent, and even if such displays were given the obstinate would still refuse. Thus the passage teaches that genuine faith rests on sincere acceptance of the message, not on external pomp or visible signs.

translation: He belittled (the matter) to his people, so they obeyed him. Indeed they were a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse indicts both a misleading leader and the compliant crowd: a person in authority made the truth seem insignificant or harmless, and his followers surrendered their independent moral judgment and followed him into error. The phrase “a people defiantly disobedient” signals habitual, willful rejection of guidance rather than a one‑time lapse. The lesson: when leaders trivialize duty or divine warning, they corrupt the community, and moral responsibility rests with both those who mislead and those who uncritically follow.

translation: So when they afflicted us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them all.
interpretation: The verse conveys that persistent oppression and rejection of truth do not escape divine justice: when a people persist in harming the righteous and rejecting guidance, God may bring decisive, comprehensive punishment (here symbolized by drowning) that ends their corrupt power and serves both as retribution and as a warning to others; it comforts the oppressed by affirming that ultimate accountability belongs to God.

translation: So We made them predecessors and examples for others.
interpretation: God designates those earlier communities and righteous people as precedents whose faith, conduct, and outcomes serve as normative models: their lives are meant to be examined and imitated in what to emulate (obedience, trust, moral courage) and what to avoid (disobedience, heedlessness), so that later generations derive guidance, legal and moral lessons, and warning from their experiences rather than treating their stories as mere history.

translation: And when the son of Mary set forth an example, behold, your people turned away from it.
interpretation: The verse reproaches the listeners for their reaction to a didactic example given by Jesus: instead of receiving its lesson and acknowledging its implication, they evaded and rejected it. Their turning away shows a moral and spiritual refusal to be guided—using the parable as a pretext to avoid responsibility, twist meaning, or cling to prior positions rather than submit to the truth it intended to reveal.

translation: And they said, “Are our gods better, or is he?” They did not present it to you except as mere disputation; rather, they are a people given to contention.
interpretation: The verse exposes the opponents’ question as a rhetorical tactic, not a sincere inquiry: by comparing the Prophet to their idols they sought only to argue and defend their customs. The phrases “ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا” and “بل هم قوم خصمون” characterize their approach as contentious and hostile, indicating their motive is prideful opposition rather than a genuine search for guidance or truth.

translation: He is nothing but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and whom We made an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: God is emphasizing that the person referred to is a human servant elevated by divine grace to serve as a moral and spiritual exemplar for Bani Isrāʾīl. The point is not to exalt him as divine but to show that by God’s favor his life, character and mission were placed before the community to teach them obedience, trust in God, righteous conduct and the correct response to revelation; his example is intended to guide, reform and expose the responsibility of the people who were given that model.

translation: And if We had willed, We would certainly have made from among you angels on earth to be successors.
interpretation: The verse highlights God’s sovereign power and purposeful choice: He could have created obedient angels to occupy the earth, but instead fashioned humans with free will so that responsibility, moral testing, repentance, and earned reward could take place. In other words, the human capacity for choice, error, and spiritual growth is intentional—integral to God’s plan for stewardship, accountability, and the display of divine justice and mercy.

translation: And indeed it is knowledge of the Hour — so do not doubt it, and follow me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse affirms that what has been conveyed about the Hour (the Last Day) is divinely informed and certain; believers must not entertain skeptical hesitation about this reality but must accept it and live by the prophetic guidance. To “follow” here means to adhere to the Prophet’s message and its moral and religious demands, because that obedience constitutes the straight path — the guiding way that preserves faith, unity, and leads to salvation in the reckoning.

translation: Do not let Satan turn you away; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse warns that Satan’s purpose is to divert people from God’s guidance by tempting, whispering, or sowing discord; he is not a neutral force but an open adversary. The implication for believers is vigilance and active resistance: seek God’s refuge, strengthen faith through remembrance and righteous deeds, hold to Scripture and communal guidance, and correct one another so that Satan’s attempts to lead individuals or communities astray do not succeed.

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs he said, “I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that concerning which you differ; so fear Allah and obey me.”
interpretation: The verse presents Jesus’ role as a divinely sent teacher whose ‘wisdom’ is practical moral and legal guidance that settles disputed issues; his injunction to ‘fear God and obey me’ means submit to God’s will as conveyed through him — obedience to the messenger is obedience to God, and the emphasis is on reforming belief and conduct by following the revealed, clarifying guidance he brought rather than elevating the messenger himself above the One who sent him.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse declares the sole lordship of God shared between the speaker and the audience, and derives from that shared fact a clear command: worship God alone. It teaches that true guidance is rooted in exclusive, sincere submission to God — this single-minded worship defines the “straight path,” shaping belief and action, rejecting idolatry or intermediaries, and directing communal and personal life toward divine guidance and ultimate salvation.

translation: Then the parties differed among themselves; so woe to those who did wrong from the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: The verse warns that division and conflicting loyalties in moments of trial are signs of moral failure: when people split, betray trusts, or abandon what is right, this discord reflects injustice and hypocrisy. The exclamation “woe” signals inevitable and severe divine recompense for those who persist in wrongdoing; the “painful Day” points to the Day of Judgment. Thus the verse functions as both warning and moral guidance: it calls for steadfastness, loyalty to truth and duty, and conscious fear of God’s accountability, because internal disunity coupled with injustice leads ultimately to grave consequences.

translation: Do they await anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
interpretation: The verse condemns the complacency of those who reject guidance or postpone concern for accountability, as if their only expectation is to be overtaken unawares by the Day of Judgment; it warns that divine decree can strike suddenly, so their denial and heedlessness will not avert the Hour—hence the imperative to heed the signs, repent, and prepare by right belief and conduct before it comes.

translation: On that Day, close friends will be enemies one to another, except the God‑fearing.
interpretation: The verse warns that on the Day of Reckoning the ordinary bonds and loyalties formed in this life—friendships based on shared interests, habits, or false assurances—will break down when ultimate truth is unveiled; people will turn away from or condemn those whose deeds condemn them. Only relationships rooted in genuine piety and God‑consciousness (those who feared God and lived righteously) will endure and not become sources of enmity, because such ties are founded on moral truth rather than transient worldly ties.

translation: O servants, there is no fear for you this day, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: A divine reassurance to those addressed that on the Day of Reckoning their anxieties and punishments will be removed: by God’s mercy and the fruition of their faith and deeds they will be delivered from dread and sorrow and admitted into a state of security, peace, and joy rather than fear and grief.

translation: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ
interpretation: تشير إلى أولئك الذين لم يكتفوا بالقبول العقلي لكلام الله بل قاموا بالاستسلام الكامل له — أي أن إيمانهم بآيات الله مصحوب بتسليم القلب والامتثال العملي لأوامره؛ فالإيمان الحق هو اتحاد اليقين بآيات الله مع السلوك الذي يعكس الخضوع له.

translation:
ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون
"Enter Paradise—you and your spouses—rejoicing/filled with gladness."
interpretation: The address promises that those who were faithful and righteous, together with their lawful partners, will be admitted into Paradise and share in its delight; it underscores that spiritual success and divine reward encompass the household and intimate bonds formed in right conduct, so that companionship in faith becomes companionship in the bliss of the hereafter.

translation: They will be served with plates of gold and goblets; therein is whatever the souls desire and what delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse uses earthly images—golden dishes and cups, fulfilment of inner longings and pleasing sights—to convey the honoured, complete and pure reward prepared for the faithful. "يطاف عليهم" conveys attentive service and dignity; "ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين" indicates that both deepest inward desires and outward aesthetic pleasures will be satisfied in a way free from imperfection or loss; and "وأنتم فيها خالدون" stresses that these blessings are permanent. In short, the verse reassures believers that Paradise offers dignified, comprehensive and everlasting joy, described in familiar terms to help human minds grasp an otherworldly reality.

translation: And that is the Paradise which you are made to inherit because of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Garden (Paradise) is granted to people as an inheritance — a rightful, lasting allotment — on account of their deeds. Calling it an inheritance emphasizes that reward in the afterlife is dispensed by God’s just will and is the due consequence of one’s actions, not merely a transient favor; it underlines moral responsibility and the certainty that righteous conduct will lead to an assured, enduring share in the hereafter.

translation: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون — "Therein for you are abundant fruits to eat."
interpretation: The verse points to God’s munificence in providing plentiful, accessible sustenance; it functions as a reminder that the variety and ease of provision are signs of Divine mercy meant to awaken gratitude, responsible stewardship of blessings, and trust that God supplies what people need rather than a guarantee of excessness or heedlessness.

translation: Indeed, the wrongdoers will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding therein forever.
interpretation: The verse asserts that for those who persist in rejection of God and commit grave injustice without repentance, the consequence in the afterlife is an irreversible exile from mercy: the term “خالدون” (abiding forever) emphasizes the permanence of that divine retribution. Its function is both doctrinal—affirming ultimate divine justice—and practical—as a stern warning intended to spur repentance, moral reform, and turning to God before death.

translation: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون — The punishment will not cease for them while they remain in it humiliated and dejected.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the chastisement inflicted on the guilty is neither intermittent nor alleviated for those who deserve it; their persistent wrong and rejection leaves them confined in a condition of humiliation, exhaustion and despair, so the suffering continues without respite as a just consequence of their state.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were themselves the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This affirms God’s perfect justice: any suffering or punishment that befell those people was not an act of Divine oppression but the consequence of their own unjust choices and rejection of guidance. Responsibility for the injustice rests with them, and what they experienced was a just outcome of their actions rather than arbitrary harm from God.

translation: And they will call, “O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us.” He will say, “Indeed, you are to remain.”
interpretation: The verse teaches the finality of divine judgment: once the appointed recompense is realized, appeals to others cannot undo it. It warns that rescue and repentance become futile after the decree is carried out, so responsibility and seeking God’s guidance must be taken beforehand.

translation: We have certainly come to you with the truth, yet most of you are averse to the truth.
interpretation: This verse asserts that divine guidance is presented clearly and authoritatively, but human disposition—shaped by love of worldly gain, entrenched customs, pride, fear of loss, or attachment to falsehood—causes the majority to resist and reject it; the statement explains why prophets meet opposition, relieves the messenger of blame for rejection, and underlines that refusal of the truth is a moral choice for which people will be held accountable.

translation: Or have they resolved upon a matter? Indeed, We are those who will bring it to pass.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human plots, however firmly formed, do not operate outside God's sovereign will; when people 'resolve' something, it ultimately unfolds only by divine decree. God thus makes human schemes serve His purpose—bringing them to completion at the appointed time, whether that completion becomes the schemers' undoing or the realization of a divinely intended outcome.

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secret talks and private counsel? Nay—indeed Our messengers are with them, recording [everything].
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s complete knowledge of even hidden speech and intentions, refuting any notion that secret plots escape Divine hearing; the “messengers” referred to are the recording angels who note private words and deeds, so covert consultations and denials are witnessed and preserved for Divine judgment — a warning to wrongdoers and reassurance that no injustice or concealment will go unnoticed.

translation: قُلْ: إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ فَإِنِّي أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ — Say, ‘If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would indeed be the foremost of the worshippers.’
interpretation: The verse is a categorical denial of the idea that God could have offspring: through a hypothetical conditional the Prophet asserts his complete servitude—even if God had a son he would be the first to worship, not to claim divinity. The statement underlines pure monotheism (tawḥīd), rejects any attribution of kinship or partnership to God, and emphasizes the Prophet’s role as a humble worshipper rather than someone possessing divine status.

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth — the Lord of the Throne — exalted above what they ascribe to Him.
interpretation: The phrase proclaims God’s absolute transcendence and sovereignty: He is the Creator and supreme Lord of all realms (including the exalted Throne) and is completely free from the limited, mistaken, or anthropomorphic attributes that people attribute to Him. It is a corrective and warning — human imagination and idols cannot capture His essence, and true reverence requires accepting only what He has revealed about Himself, rejecting association or likeness, and approaching Him with humility and worship.

translation: So leave them to indulge in vain discourse and idle play until they meet the Day they are promised.
interpretation: The verse teaches restraint: believers should not be consumed by disputation or attempts to force conviction on those who persist in heedlessness. Rather than chasing or quarreling with the mockers, trust that God’s promised Day of Reckoning will reveal the truth and bring justice; meanwhile devote energy to patient preaching, upright conduct, and safeguarding your own faith instead of being dragged into fruitless contention.

translation: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth; and He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms the absolute, singular sovereignty of God over every realm — heaven and earth alike — rejecting any division of divine authority or legitimacy of rival deities. Calling Him “the Wise, the Knowing” explains how that sovereignty is exercised: God’s governance is grounded in perfect knowledge and purpose, so what occurs in both worlds is under His deliberate, wise decree and cannot be attributed to blind chance or competing powers.

translation:
وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون
"Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them; with Him alone is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: The verse asserts God's absolute sovereignty and exclusive knowledge of the final Hour to solemnly orient human life: because dominion and ultimate certainty belong only to God, human claims to lasting control or ultimate knowledge are illusory, and therefore people are called to humility, responsible conduct and constant awareness that all actions lead to a final return and accountability before Him.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Him possess no intercession except he who bears witness to the truth — and they (the people or those invoked) know it.
interpretation: This verse denies any real power of intercession to deities or beings worshipped alongside God: they cannot plead or mediate before God on behalf of others. Intercession is conditional and belongs only to those who themselves testify to the truth — i.e., those who acknowledge God’s oneness and righteousness and do so truthfully — and even then it occurs only by God’s leave. The statement “and they know it” underscores that this limitation is manifest and understood (by the invoked beings and/or by people): false gods lack authority, while true intercession is reserved for sincere, truthful servants acknowledged by God.

translation: And if you were to ask them who created them, they would surely say, ‘Allah.’ So how are they being turned away?
interpretation: The verse criticizes the gap between verbal assent and lived conviction: people will acknowledge, when questioned, that Allah is their Creator, yet in practice they remain led astray by habit, desire, false authorities, or social conformity. The rhetorical question exposes the irrationality of admitting a truth without allowing it to reshape belief and action, warning that mere lip‑acknowledgment is insufficient if the heart and conduct remain diverted.

translation: And it was said to him, “O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.”
interpretation: This phrase expresses the believer’s turning to God in the face of stubborn rejection: a recognition that some people’s hearts are closed and that human effort cannot force faith. It is an appeal to divine wisdom and judgment, entrusting the outcome to God while acknowledging the moral reality that persistent refusal of guidance marks a people as disbelievers and limits what a messenger or believer can achieve.

translation: So pardon them and say, “Peace.” Soon they will know.
interpretation: This instructs the believer to meet hostility with forgiveness and a greeting of peace rather than retaliation, trusting that the truth and consequences will become evident in time; by showing restraint and goodwill one leaves judgment to God and lets the eventual realization of reality speak for itself.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Hāʼ Mīm.
interpretation: The disjoined letters “Hāʼ Mīm” are part of the muqattaʿāt; classical scholars interpret them as a purposeful, divine sign whose full meaning is known only to Allah, intended to arrest attention, attest to the Qurʾān’s miraculous, non‑human origin, and invite deeper reflection on its guidance.

translation: And the Clear (Manifest) Book.
interpretation: It refers to the Scripture as intrinsically clear and self-evident: its language, guidance and signs are made manifest so that truth and error are distinguished, doubts are removed for sincere seekers, and those who turn to it can recognize and follow the straight guidance it presents.

translation: Indeed We revealed it on a blessed night. Indeed, We were ever to warn.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the Qur’an was sent down in a single, divinely appointed “blessed night” (understood as the moment of its decisive transmission), a time charged with mercy and spiritual significance; the purpose of that revelation is primarily to warn humanity—an act of compassionate guidance meant to awaken consciousness, call people away from heedlessness and wrongdoing, and give them a clear, authoritative admonition so they can change course and attain salvation.

translation: In it He distinguishes every wise affair.
interpretation: The phrase means that within the revealed matter (the Book/God’s decree) God, by His perfect wisdom, separates, determines and explains every affair: He clarifies truths and rulings, distinguishes right from wrong, and settles matters with justice and wisdom so that people may recognize guidance and act accordingly.

translation: A decree from Us; indeed, We are the ones who send (messengers).
interpretation: The phrase asserts that what is happening is rooted in God's sovereign will and in His established practice of commissioning messengers; the aim is to remind listeners that the warning or ordinance is divinely authoritative and therefore inevitable and legitimate, not a human fabrication, so resistance or rejection cannot overturn what God has decreed.

translation: A mercy from your Lord; indeed He is the All‑Hearing, All‑Knowing.
interpretation: This declares that the help or blessing mentioned is an act of divine mercy rooted in God’s attentive care: He hears every plea and knows every circumstance, so His mercy is both responsive and perfectly informed—offering reassurance that turning to Him is met with understanding and compassionate response.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them — if you are certain.
interpretation: A declaration of God’s exclusive sovereignty over the entire cosmos coupled with a rhetorical challenge to doubters: if you really claim to be certain otherwise, bring your evidence. The phrase presses listeners to recognize that every realm and all that lies between them are under God’s authority and wise governance, and that denial without sure proof is unreasonable.

translation: There is no deity except Him; He brings life and causes death. He is your Lord and the Lord of your earlier forefathers.
interpretation: The verse affirms exclusive divine sovereignty: God alone controls the fundamental realities of existence—granting life and causing death—so He alone merits obedience and worship. By identifying Him as both 'your Lord' and 'the Lord of your forefathers,' it underscores the uninterrupted, transgenerational authority of God and rejects any claim that lineage, tradition, or multiple gods can override His lordship; it calls people to recognize that their origin, destiny, and ultimate accountability are governed by the one God rather than by ancestral customs or rival deities.

translation: Nay — they are in doubt and are playing about.
interpretation: The phrase corrects any appearance of firm conviction: these people do not possess sincere, serious doubt aimed at seeking truth but rather a frivolous, unserious attitude toward guidance. Their uncertainty manifests as mockery, diversion, and idle disputation, treating weighty matters of faith as a game; as a result they remain spiritually adrift and fail to pursue honest inquiry or reform.

translation: So await the Day when the heaven will bring forth a clear smoke.
interpretation: The verse announces an unmistakable, visible portent sent by God immediately before the Hour: a manifest “smoke” that functions both as a warning to rouse the heedless and as an instrument of testing and judgment. Its clarity (مبين) removes any pretense of ignorance, exposing people’s true states—to be a trial that affirms God’s sovereignty, brings consequences on the obstinate, and distinguishes and purifies the righteous.

translation: يغشى الناس: It will overtake/envelop the people. هذا عذاب أليم: This is a painful (severe) punishment.
interpretation: The verb يغشى conveys sudden, overwhelming coverage — the warning is that a divine torment will come upon people and completely overwhelm them. Calling it "عذاب أليم" stresses the intensity and reality of that suffering: it is a grievous, crushing retribution for persistent rejection or wrongdoing. The formulation underscores both the inevitability and the severity of the consequence, urging listeners to take the warning seriously before they are wholly overtaken and can no longer avert the punishment.

translation: Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers.
interpretation: This plea illustrates that deliverance ultimately depends on God’s mercy combined with a faith that is sincere and transformative: the supplication teaches that turning to God in humility, confessing faith, and seeking forgiveness are the means by which punishment may be lifted, and it warns implicitly that God’s pardon is granted according to genuine belief and repentance rather than mere last‑minute words.

translation: How will they take admonition when there has come to them a clear Messenger?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the people’s failure to heed guidance cannot be excused by ignorance, because a manifest, unmistakable messenger has been sent to them. It implies their rejection is a deliberate moral choice—rooted in stubbornness, arrogance, or self-deception—so the responsibility and accountability for ignoring the reminder rest squarely on them; the clarity of the messenger’s message increases their culpability rather than lessening it.

translation: Then they turned away from him and said, “A teacher, a madman.”
interpretation: When people oppose clear guidance, they often evade its force by leveling personal accusations—portraying the messenger as merely “taught” (part of a plot or trained by others) or as insane—a rhetorical tactic that exposes their refusal to engage with the truth and reveals moral and intellectual resistance rather than any substantive refutation.

translation: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while; indeed, you will return.
interpretation: The verse cautions that any worldly respite from Divine chastisement is temporary and by God’s design: a short postponement that does not cancel eventual accountability. It serves both as a warning that those who presume safety from consequences are mistaken and as a reminder that humans will ultimately return to God to face the outcome of their deeds — the delay may be mercy, a test, or a prelude to final retribution, but it is not permanent forgiveness.

translation: The Day We will seize with the greatest, overwhelming seizure — indeed, We are the Avengers.
interpretation: The phrase underscores the inevitability, totality and finality of God’s intervention at the end: when divine justice is executed, all concealment and opposition will be swept away and no one can avert the consequence. Declaring “We are the Avengers” affirms that God Himself will restore justice and recompense wrongs, serving both as a warning to persistent transgressors and as consolation to the oppressed by assuring that ultimate vindication and accountability belong to God alone.

translation: And certainly We tested before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger.
interpretation: The verse indicates that God’s dealings with nations include deliberate trials in the form of clear, dignified messengers; here the people of Pharaoh were not condemned without warning but were given a gracious prophet and manifest signs so that their acceptance or rejection would be a free moral choice. Calling him رسول كريم stresses the messenger’s honor, mercy and authoritative evidence, and thus responsibility rests on the people who persist in denial despite such clear guidance.

translation: أن يُسَلَّموا إلى عبادِ الله؛ إني لكم رسولٌ أمينٌ
interpretation: الآية تؤكد أن المتكلم — النبي أو المرسل — يطالب بتسليم الحقوق أو الأشخاص إلى عباد الله وحسن معاملتهم، ويشهد على نفسه بالصدق والأمانة في نقل الرسالة؛ أي أن على الناس أن يوفوا بحقوق الآخرين ويطيعوا الأمر الإلهي لأن المبلغ أمين لا يخدعهم، فطاعة ما يدعو إليه مبنية على ثقةٍ بأنه ينقل حكم الله وأمره بأمان.

translation: And do not be arrogant toward Allah. Indeed, I will bring you a clear authority.
interpretation: The speaker rebukes prideful defiance of God and promises to present an unmistakable, decisive proof—whether a manifest sign, miracle, or irrefutable argument—that will expose the emptiness of their pretensions and compel them to recognize divine sovereignty; the verse stresses that human arrogance cannot withstand clear evidence of God’s authority, leaving those who persist in pridefully rejecting it fully accountable.

translation: And I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me.
interpretation: The speaker invokes the common Lord as a shield against the threatened mob violence, placing his trust in God’s protection rather than in human approval. By saying “my Lord and your Lord” he reminds them of a shared divine authority and accountability, appealing to their conscience to refrain from an unjust collective act (stoning) and asserting that his safety and vindication rest ultimately with God.

translation: And if you do not believe me, then withdraw from me.
interpretation: The speaker (the Messenger) asserts a clear boundary: if people reject his message, he will cease engaging with them. It teaches that guidance cannot be compelled and that, when faced with persistent unbelief or hostile denial, the appropriate response is to disengage respectfully rather than continue fruitless dispute or compromise one’s mission.

translation: So he called upon his Lord, “These are indeed a people who are criminals.”
interpretation: The expression signals the speaker’s turning to God in reliance when faced with a community entrenched in persistent wrongdoing; “مجرمون” describes sustained transgression and active injustice (disbelief, oppression, persecution of truth), and the act of calling on the Lord teaches that ultimate judgment and deliverance belong to God rather than to human vengeance, while also expressing the urgency for divine intervention against entrenched corruption.

translation: So slip in among My servants by night; surely you are being followed.
interpretation: The words describe how Satan and his followers operate stealthily at night to whisper and mislead people, but their secretiveness is futile: God’s knowledge and justice track them, and their efforts will be pursued and held to account—an assurance that their deception is temporary and will meet retribution or be thwarted.

translation: And leave the sea in its stillness; indeed, they are an army that will be drowned.
interpretation: The command to “leave the sea at rest” is an assurance that God’s intervention is decisive: believers are invited to cease anxious striving and trust the divine plan, for the fate of oppressive forces is already sealed. It teaches reliance on God’s power to deliver and to enact justice, and that tyrants who pursue wrongdoing will ultimately be overwhelmed by what God ordains.

translation: How many gardens and springs they left behind!
interpretation: The phrase draws attention to the abundant worldly comforts people abandoned — gardens and flowing springs — and teaches that true commitment to God's guidance often requires forsaking material ease; it also reminds us that such worldly possessions are transient and must not be valued above the eternal outcome.

translation: وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ — “and gardens and an honorable station.”
interpretation: The phrase promises that the righteous will receive both tangible, flourishing blessings (gardens as symbols of provision, peace and beauty) and a dignified, noble standing (مقام كريم) — meaning not only material comfort but an elevated, honorable status and nearness to God in the hereafter; the two together show that true reward combines external bounty with spiritual honor.

translation: And a blessing which they were enjoying therein.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the dwellers of the hereafter experience a continuous, effortless blessing and delight in Paradise. The past-tense phrasing conveys certainty and perpetuity: their enjoyment is real, ongoing, and both physical and spiritual. The word “فاكهين” evokes savoring and contentment, indicating not merely possession of favors but heartfelt, sustained pleasure as the true recompense for the righteous.

translation: Thus it was; and We made it an inheritance for other people.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God, by His will and judgment, transfers possession or blessing (often land, security, or leadership) from one community to another. It teaches that worldly tenure is not permanent but contingent on divine wisdom and people’s conduct: when a people persist in wrongdoing or fail to uphold what warranted their favor, God may remove that gift and entrust it to others who are destined to receive it.

translation: Neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them, and they were not granted any respite.
interpretation: The verse stresses the finality and inevitability of divine judgment: when God’s sentence on the wrongdoers came, even the cosmos gave no lament or delay—there was no protest from creation and no postponement of their fate. It teaches that created things cannot avert or postpone God’s decree, so hope for reprieve based on worldly intercession is vain and accountability before God is unavoidable.

translation: And indeed We delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God removed from the Israelite community a degrading, dignity-stripping torment, highlighting divine mercy and power in rescuing a people; it teaches that honor and humiliation are ultimately determined by God’s will and serves as a reminder to trust in His providence rather than in transient worldly supports.

translation:
من فرعون؛ إنه كان عالياً من المسرفين
"From Pharaoh; indeed he was lofty/arrogant among the transgressors."
interpretation: The phrase characterizes Pharaoh’s moral condition: his exalted position produced arrogance and excessive transgression. He is presented as someone who exceeded bounds in pride, oppression and self-indulgence—claiming undue authority and acting unjustly—so that he stands as the model of those whose hubris and extravagance in wrongdoing set them against God’s guidance and lead to ruin.

translation:
وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَـٰهُم بِعِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
"And certainly We selected them by (Our) knowledge over the worlds."
interpretation: The phrase indicates that God, by His perfect and prior knowledge, singled out certain people (e.g., prophets or the rightly guided) and elevated them in rank and responsibility relative to others across creation; their distinction is not accidental but the result of Divine wisdom and foreknowledge, so their guidance, authority, or exemplary status serves as an expression of God’s intentional selection and purpose.

translation: And We gave them signs, in which there was a clear trial.
interpretation: God granted people unmistakable signs — revelations, miracles, provisions or warnings — not merely to inform them but to test their response: by making the truth plain He heightened their responsibility so that those who truly believed and acted rightly would be distinguished from those who persisted in denial, ingratitude, or hypocrisy.

translation: Indeed, these will surely say
interpretation: An emphatic introductory phrase pointing to the predictable speech of certain people (often deniers or hypocrites); it stresses the certainty that they will voice their customary objections or excuses when confronted with a truth, highlighting human stubbornness and the expected pattern of denial.

translation: قَالُوا: «إِنَّهَا إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُبْعَثِينَ» — “They said: ‘This is nothing but our first death, and we will not be resurrected.’”
interpretation: The verse captures the obstinate denial of the disbelievers who dismiss the prospect of a final judgment: by calling what confronts them merely their “first death” they treat death as an ordinary end and refuse to accept that God will raise people again for reckoning. It expresses arrogance, short‑sighted materialism, and a rejection of accountability in the hereafter.

translation: فَأْتُوا بِآبَائِنَا إِن كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ — “Then bring our fathers, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: This is a challenge issuing from people who refuse the prophet’s claim: they demand an impossible, sensational proof — that he produce their deceased ancestors — as the condition for belief. It reveals their obstinate attachment to literal, worldly proof and their evasion of the moral and spiritual reason for the message, asking for miracles instead of sincere reflection and repentance.

translation:
أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم ۚ أهلكناهم ۖ إنهم كانوا مجرمين
“Are they better, or the people of Tubbaʻ and those before them? We destroyed them; indeed they were criminals.”
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly rank, power, or lineage cannot protect against divine justice: past mighty peoples (like Tubbaʻ and those before him) were annihilated because of their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of guidance. It teaches that continued disbelief and injustice lead to inevitable accountability, urging the present listeners to repent and accept the truth to avoid the same fate.

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the cosmos is the outcome of deliberate, wise purpose rather than whim or amusement: every aspect of creation serves ends—to manifest God’s attributes, to provide for life, and to test and educate moral agents—so nothing in existence is meaningless or accidental, and human beings must recognize their responsibilities in light of that ordered, purposeful design.

translation:
ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون
"We did not create the two (them) except in truth; but most of them do not know.",
interpretation: The verse asserts that the paired creation (commonly understood as the heavens and the earth) is not accidental but founded on divine truth and purpose—its order, measure and signs testify to God’s wisdom and intent. Yet most people fail to perceive or acknowledge that purpose, either through heedlessness or willful neglect; the implication is a call to reflect on creation as evidence of God’s sovereignty and to correct the intellectual/spiritual blindness that prevents recognizing and responding to that truth.

translation: Indeed, the Day of Decision is their appointed time — for all of them.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Day of Judgment is a fixed, divinely ordained appointment for every person; on that decisive day all will be gathered together and finally separated for recompense, and no power or excuse in this life can avert, delay, or exempt anyone from that appointed reckoning.

translation: The Day when no protector will avail another at all, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection all human alliances, patrons, kinship ties and worldly supporters will be powerless; no one can intercede effectively or transfer salvation to another. Each person will stand alone before God, judged by their own deeds, and true deliverance comes only through Allah’s decree and mercy rather than through other people.

translation: Except for the one upon whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He — He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that exemption from blame, punishment, or ultimate loss rests solely on God’s mercy; ultimate judgment and pardon are not determined by human action alone but by Allah’s will. It affirms two complementary divine attributes — absolute power (Al-ʿAzīz) and compassionate readiness to forgive (Ar-Raḥīm) — teaching believers to place their hope in God’s mercy while recognizing that mercy is dispensed by One who is fully capable of showing justice and protection.

translation: إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ — Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum.
interpretation: This refers to a tree in Hell whose fruits are the ghastly, repellent food of the wicked; it represents the reversal of God’s blessings into torment — what sinners sought or loved in life is transformed into a bitter, protruding punishment, a concrete manifestation of divine justice and the consequences of persistent evil.

translation: the food of the sinful
interpretation: It denotes sustenance or provisions that are tainted by sin — what a person obtains or consumes through unjust, forbidden, or morally blameworthy means (oppression, deception, illicit gain), emphasizing that such food is spiritually and ethically reprehensible.

translation: Like molten metal boiling in the bellies.
interpretation: The phrase portrays the punishment of the wrongdoers by likening it to searing molten metal churning inside the stomachs: a vivid metaphor for overwhelming, inescapable internal agony that consumes both body and conscience, emphasizing the real, severe and irreversible nature of the recompense that follows rejection of guidance.

translation: like the boiling of molten copper
interpretation: The simile conveys intense, searing agony and a hissing, bubbling tumult: comparing the state described to molten metal emphasizes unbearable heat, corrosive burning and an overwhelming, consuming force — evoking both the physical torment and the chaotic, noise-filled distress of those subjected to it.

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hell.
interpretation: This is a divine command ordering the agents of punishment to apprehend an arrogant denier and consign him to Hell, signifying that those who defiantly reject God's guidance and persist in wrongdoing will have no refuge; it emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice, the absolute authority of God, and the moral consequence that every soul ultimately faces the outcome of its choices.

translation: Then they poured upon his head from the torment of boiling (scalding) water.
interpretation: تصوير لعقوبة شديدة ومهينة للمكذبين: سكب ماء الحميم الحارق فوق الرأس يدل على غرض عقابي شامل يخترق الجسد ويحطم الكرامة، ويعبّر عن جزاء الله العادل لمن أبى الحق وظلم الناس، وتنبيه على واقعية وعنف الجزاء لمن استمرّ في التكذيب والطغيان.

translation: Taste! Indeed, you are the Mighty, the Generous.
interpretation: An ironic rebuke to the proud: the command to “taste” is to undergo the consequence or chastisement, while the appellation “you are the Mighty, the Generous” exposes the addressee’s vaunted self-regard as hollow—his claimed power and honor will not avert the coming penalty.

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to doubt.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rebuke and verdict: the clear sign or proof just given decisively answers the opponents’ earlier suspicions, exposing their doubts as unfounded and leaving them accountable for having rejected what was made plain.

translation: Indeed, the God‑fearing are in a secure (safe, trusted) station.
interpretation: The phrase teaches that those who live in conscious obedience to God attain a protected and honored standing: inwardly they enjoy peace, trustworthiness and freedom from fear and temptation, and ultimately they are placed under God’s protection in the final abode. “Maqām amīn” conveys both divine security from punishment and a status of trust and dignity earned by piety.

translation: In gardens and springs
interpretation: This phrase depicts the promised reward for the righteous: abiding in verdant, tranquil gardens accompanied by ever-flowing springs. The imagery conveys both physical comfort and spiritual peace—gardens as secure, pleasant dwellings and springs as continual, pure sustenance and refreshment—signifying God’s enduring mercy, provision, and the fulfillment of human longing in the afterlife.

translation: They will be clothed in fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), facing one another.
interpretation: The verse signifies that the righteous will be granted dignified, pure and enduring garments as a symbol of divine honour and comfort in Paradise; the luxurious fabrics express the removal of worldly need and shame, while “facing one another” indicates serene mutual companionship and recognition—enjoyment and dignity shared among the blessed without envy or conflict.

translation: Thus We will marry them to companions with beautiful, wide eyes.
interpretation: The phrase promises that the righteous will be given pure, splendid companions in Paradise; ‘hurʾ ʿayn’ conveys both visible beauty (clear, luminous, wide eyes) and moral/spiritual purity. The word ‘kadhālik’ links this gift to the broader catalogue of heavenly blessings, indicating these companions are part of the complete, honorable, and eternal felicity God grants — an assurance of perfect, unblemished companionship and delight rather than a mere temporal or carnal reward.

translation: They will be offered there every kind of fruit, safe and secure.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy complete and uninterrupted provision — every kind of fruit they desire — coupled with perfect security. The word آمنين indicates freedom from fear, harm, anxiety, labor, loss or any change that would spoil their enjoyment; their blessings are permanent, protected, and experienced without any distress or threat.

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death; and He will have saved them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse means that those granted entry into Paradise will not experience dying again after the single death they underwent in this worldly life. “Tasting death” refers to the suffering and cessation that accompany dying, and “the first death” is that one temporal earthly death; thereafter their existence in the Hereafter is permanent and free from further death or the torment of Hell, a manifestation of God’s mercy and protection for the righteous.

translation: A bounty from your Lord — that is the great success.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the highest achievement is not worldly gain but God’s gracious favor: the unearned gift of His guidance, pardon, acceptance and admission to His presence. True triumph consists in receiving that divine bounty — a merciful bestowal beyond human claim — which secures eternal well‑being and closeness to the Lord.

translation:
فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لعلهم يتذكرون
"We have only made it easy in your tongue so that they may remember (take heed)."
interpretation: God is indicating that the revelation was delivered in the Prophet’s own language and in a clear, accessible manner so that people would be able to understand, reflect and be guided. The phrase “we have only made it easy” emphasizes that divine facilitation removes barriers to comprehension but does not compel acceptance; it places moral responsibility on listeners to attend, ponder, and respond.

translation: So wait; indeed, they are awaiting.
interpretation: A divine injunction to the Messenger to practice patient restraint and leave the matter to God: those who oppose him are themselves expectant of what will come (the Hour, judgement, or the outcome of events), and their anticipations or plots cannot hasten or avert God’s decree — the truth and recompense will unfold in their appointed time.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Meem.
interpretation: The Basmala invokes God's mercy as the framework for revelation; the disconnected letters “Ha Meem” (muqaṭṭaʿāt) are a deliberately enigmatic, attention‑drawing sign whose exact import is known only to Allah. They function to underline the Qur’an’s divine origin and miraculous nature: although composed of familiar letters, its meaning and impact cannot be reproduced by human effort, thereby calling listeners to humility, reflection, and recognition of the authority of the message.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: Affirms that the Qur’an is not a human product but divine disclosure whose authority rests on God’s power and whose guidance reflects His perfect wisdom; describing God as al‑‘Azīz signals that His word will stand and cannot be overcome by opponents, while al‑Hakīm indicates that the text’s laws, judgments, and narratives are purposefully ordered and measured to guide human conduct and rectify hearts, so the believer is called to accept and live by it with trust in both its sovereignty and its wise design.

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: الآية تدلّ على أن مظاهر الخلق في السماوات والأرض ليست بلا معنى بل هي دلائل عملية على حكمة وربوبية الله؛ فالمؤمن يتأمل في انتظام الكون وتنوع المخلوقات وآيات القدرة فيها فيزداد يقينًا، يستنبط منها صفات الخالق وهدايته، ويجعلها سببًا للثبات على التوحيد والطاعة والعمل المستنير بالعبرة الإلهية.

translation: And in your creation and in what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for people who are certain.
interpretation: This statement invites contemplative believers to recognize that the constitution of human beings and the diversity, instincts, and interactions of animals are deliberate signs of God’s wisdom, power, and providential care; those who possess true certainty will read the order, balance, and purposive features in living things as evidence of a single Creator, which strengthens faith, engenders gratitude, and calls for responsible, reverent behavior toward creation.

translation: And the alternation of night and day and what Allah has sent down from the sky of provision — by which He revives the earth after its death — and the directing of the winds are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: These natural cycles and provisions are offered as deliberate evidences meant to awaken reflection: they point to a single, wise Sustainer who sustains and renews life and who governs the world’s order. For those who use reason, such signs call for trust in divine providence, humility about human dependence and mortality, and a moral response of gratitude, responsibility, and readiness for accountability.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. So what statement, after Allah and His signs, will they believe?
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quranic revelations are the truthful, authoritative signs from God and poses a rhetorical question to expose the absurdity of rejecting them: if God’s message and clear signs are presented, there is no legitimate alternative claim or story worthy of belief. It rebukes those who persist in denial or demand other proofs, emphasizing the sufficiency and finality of divine guidance and calling people to recognize and submit to what has been made clear by God rather than cling to vain substitutes or obstinacy.

translation: Woe to every persistent, sinful liar.
interpretation: This is a stern moral and eschatological warning: God condemns those who make a habit of falsehood, slander or deceit. Such persistent misuse of speech corrodes trust and justice in society and will meet with severe divine accountability; the verse therefore demands truthfulness, restraint in speech, and awareness that words carry moral consequences.

translation: He hears the signs of Allah being recited to him, then turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them; so give him the tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against deliberate, proud rejection of divine guidance: hearing the Qur’an without humility does not transform the heart—arrogance acts like a barrier that makes one ‘as if not having heard.’ That willful closing of the heart is a moral responsibility that merits stern warning; the passage calls for self-examination, humility, and readiness to let the message change one’s conduct, because persistent repudiation out of pride leads to spiritual ruin and accordingly to a severe recompense.

translation: And when anyone comes to know of any of Our signs, he takes them in mockery. For them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that encountering or understanding divine signs yet responding with ridicule is a deliberate, culpable rejection rather than innocent levity. Mockery of God’s revelations stems from pride, stubbornness, or a willful refusal to submit, and it carries consequence: a degrading, dishonoring punishment that reflects both moral ruin in this life and loss of dignity before God in the Hereafter.

translation: Behind them is Hell; and whatever they earned will not avail them at all, nor will those they took as protectors besides Allah; and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who reject the truth or rely on other than God will find Hell awaiting them on the Day of Reckoning: their accumulated deeds will not save them because salvation depends on true faith and God’s acceptance, and any so‑called allies or protectors besides Allah have no power to intercede or avert the Divine judgment — their trust was vain, and they will suffer a mighty punishment.

translation: This is guidance. As for those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the revealed message functions as clear guidance toward God and right living; rejecting God’s signs is not a neutral act but a willful turning away that brings consequence. The term rujz (a scourge or retribution) qualified as alīmun (painful) signals both moral and existential loss: persistent denial severs a person from the light and safeguards that guidance provides and therefore leads to humiliation, inner ruin and — where God wills — manifest affliction or chastisement. The warning is meant to provoke humility, reflection and repentance, showing that divine justice follows deliberate, obstinate rejection of truth.

translation: Allah is He who has made the sea subservient to you so that ships may sail through it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse asserts God’s sovereignty and providence: by subduing the sea He has enabled human mobility, commerce and access to resources that would otherwise be inaccessible. These material and practical blessings are portrayed as deliberate divine favors meant to be recognized; the proper response is gratitude, which implies acknowledging God as the ultimate source, using His gifts responsibly, and letting that recognition shape conduct and faith rather than mere exploitation or ingratitude.

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—entirely from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse means that God, by His providence and power, has made the forces, resources and regularities of the heavens and the earth available to human life; this arrangement is a sign pointing to His sovereignty and wisdom and is meant to prompt thoughtful people to respond with gratitude, humility and ethical stewardship—using creation responsibly while recognizing that all ability and provision come from God.

translation:
قُل لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اغفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْمًا بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
Say to those who have believed: ‘Forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.’
interpretation: The verse instructs believers to exercise forgiveness and restraint toward people who deny or do not anticipate God’s decisive days (punishment or accountability). Rather than seeking personal revenge or trying to deliver divine justice themselves, believers should pardon such persons and leave ultimate recompense to God, trusting that He will judge and reward or punish each people according to their deeds; forgiveness thus embodies moral self-restraint and reliance on divine justice.

translation: Whoever does a righteous deed, it is for the good of his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it; then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse affirms individual moral responsibility and spiritual causality: actions primarily affect the doer—good deeds build and benefit one’s inner self while wrongful deeds ultimately harm the one who commits them—so every person must live with awareness that they will finally return to God for just recompense, which grounds ethical choice and accountability.

translation: And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and the judgment and the prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them above the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God bestowed on that people a sequence of divine favors—revealed guidance, discerning authority (hukm), prophets, and lawful blessings—and by this grace elevated them relative to other nations. This elevation (faḍl) should be understood as a bestowed privilege and trust, carrying moral and covenantal obligations rather than implying an innate, perpetual superiority; the favor is conditional on faithfulness and can be revoked if the responsibilities are neglected. In short, divine gifts confer both honor and accountability, granted by God’s wisdom to guide communities toward righteousness.

translation: And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter; yet they only differed after knowledge had come to them, out of mutual enmity. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God had already provided unmistakable evidence and guidance, but people chose to abandon consensus and truth because of pride, jealousy, and partisan hostility. Their disputes were therefore not born of uncertainty but of corrupt motives that overrode the evidence. The warning is twofold: human quarrels that arise from selfish enmity do not alter divine truth, and on the Day of Judgment God alone will settle those contested matters and hold each party accountable for following passion instead of evidence.

translation: Then We set you (O Prophet) upon a determined legislation in the matter; so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.
interpretation: God is commanding adherence to the divinely revealed law and guidance given for how affairs are to be conducted; believers (and the Prophet as its exemplar) must follow that prescribed way and resist being led astray by fleeting desires, popular opinions, or uninformed impulses of those lacking true knowledge, because following such whims departs from God’s guidance and undermines justice and right conduct.

translation: They will never avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies to one another, but Allah is the Protector of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse teaches that no human power, relationship or alliance can ultimately protect anyone from God’s will or judgment. Those who commit injustice may defend and support one another for a time, creating a sense of security, but such mutual backing cannot prevail against divine authority. True and enduring protection belongs to those who cultivate God-consciousness (taqwa); Allah is their guardian, helper and disposer of affairs. The passage therefore comforts the steadfast and warns against relying on the apparent strength of oppressors, urging trust in God and perseverance in righteousness.

translation: These are clear insights/signs for the people, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain.
interpretation: The phrase distinguishes between the Qur’an’s outward evidential role and its inward, transformative effect: as “basaʾir” it offers clear proofs and light available to all who look, inviting reflection and discernment; but its full power as “huda wa rahma” is realized by those who approach it with yaqīn — settled, heartfelt certainty (not mere verbal assent). For such people the words become guidance that corrects understanding, heals the heart, and draws down mercy, whereas without that inner conviction the same clear signs may be seen yet leave one unchanged.

translation: Or do those who have committed evil deeds think that We will make them equal to those who believed and did righteous deeds — (in) their life and their death? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who, through arrogance or self-deception, assume that their evil conduct will be treated as if it were equivalent to true faith accompanied by righteous action. It affirms that God’s moral order distinguishes between faith‑and‑good‑deeds and persistent wrongdoing; the phrase “their life and their death” stresses that this distinction applies both to one’s worldly condition and to the final outcome.
