Those who make such a claim are severely mistaken in their judgment and misunderstand the basis of divine recompense.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse affirms that creation is purposeful and founded on divine truth, and that God’s governance is just: every person will inevitably be held accountable and receive a fair, proportionate recompense for their deeds, with no one being treated unjustly.

translation: Have you seen the one who takes his desire as his god? Then Allah has let him go astray out of knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and has placed over his sight a veil. So who can guide him after Allah? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: The verse warns that when a person elevates their own whims into the ultimate standard—making desires the authority in place of God—they gradually close themselves off to truth. That persistent preference for caprice over revelation results in a divine withdrawal: the person’s receptivity to guidance is impaired (symbolized by a seal on hearing and heart and a veil over sight), so they no longer perceive or accept the truth. The rhetorical question underscores the futility of seeking guidance from others once one has willfully rejected God’s guidance; it is thus both a diagnosis of spiritual hardening and a warning to preserve humility and submission so one’s faculties remain open to guidance.

translation: And they say, “There is nothing but our worldly life; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.” And they have no knowledge of that; they do nothing but conjecture.
interpretation: The verse rebukes a materialistic stance that reduces existence to only this life and excuses God’s role by blaming impersonal “time.” Such assertions—denying resurrection and divine sovereignty—are grounded in ignorance and mere speculation; the Qur’an here warns that attributing life and death to chance or time is an unfounded claim that obscures responsibility before God and leads to moral and spiritual error.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is that they say, “Bring back our forefathers, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse exposes a common evasive tactic: faced with unmistakable revelation, people deflect responsibility by demanding an impossible spectacle — the return of their ancestors — as a condition for belief. This demand is not a genuine proof but a stalling device that shifts the burden and seeks a miracle irrelevant to the moral and rational evidence already presented; it also ignores that those same forebears had rejected truth, so invoking them only highlights the speakers’ unwillingness to accept guidance rather than a legitimate objection.

translation: قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
interpretation: الآية تهدف إلى مواجهة الشكّ في البعث بالتأكيد على قدرة الله المطلقة على إحياء الناس وإماته، وعلى حتمية الجمع يوم القيامة؛ وتدعو إلى وقفة ضميرية ومسؤولية أخلاقية، لأن الاعتراف بهذه الحقيقة ينبغي أن يوقظ الإنسان من غفلته ويقوده إلى حسابٍ لافعالِه، بينما الواقع أن كثيرين يبقون جاهلين أو مقصرين في استيعاب ما يترتب على هذه الحقيقة.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day when the Hour is established, that Day the falsifiers will surely be losers.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s absolute and exclusive sovereignty over all existence—nothing in the heavens or the earth escapes His authority or ultimate rule. It then points forward to the inevitable coming of the Hour (the Day of Judgment), when all pretensions and deceptions are exposed. “Al-mubṭilūn” (the falsifiers) refers to those whose claims, beliefs, or deeds are vain because they are based on falsehood—whether by denying or distorting divine truth, committing shirk, practicing hypocrisy, or rendering their worship insincere so that their actions are nullified. On that Day their worldly status, gains, or arguments will avail them nothing; their works will be invalidated and they will suffer true loss. The statement is both a theological affirmation of God’s control and an ethical warning: only sincere, truthful submission to God secures lasting benefit, while falsehood and insincerity lead to final ruin.

translation: And you will see every nation prostrate (or kneeling). Each nation will be called to its record — “Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.”
interpretation: This verse portrays the Day of Reckoning when all peoples stand helpless before God and are summoned to the specific record that contains their deeds and responsibilities. The image of being jathiya (kneeling/prostrate) expresses total subjection and inability to avert what is coming. That each nation is called to its own book emphasizes communal and individual accountability: peoples will be judged by the guidance and obligations given to them and will receive exact recompense — neither loss nor injustice. The scene intends to warn, to affirm divine justice, and to remind listeners that deeds are preserved and will be fairly accounted for on the appointed day.

translation: This is Our Record that will speak about you in truth. Indeed, We used to transcribe what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns that there exists a divine register of deeds which will itself bear truthful testimony against people on the Day of Reckoning. It affirms that nothing done by anyone is lost or hidden—actions have been continuously recorded (by God or His appointed recorders) and will be presented as objective evidence; the reminder is meant to deter wrongdoing and to stress inevitable accountability before God’s just judgment.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the manifest success.
interpretation: The verse teaches that genuine faith must be accompanied by moral action, and that the true goal of a believer is entry into God’s mercy: not merely reward for deeds in a transactional sense, but being enveloped by divine compassion and forgiveness. Calling this outcome the “manifest success” stresses that ultimate salvation — eternal well‑being and dignity before God — is clear, unequivocal, and incomparably superior to transient worldly gains.

translation: And as for those who disbelieved—were not My signs recited to you? But you became arrogant and were a people of criminals.
interpretation: The verse reproaches people who, despite repeatedly hearing God’s signs (the revelations and clear evidence), refused to submit out of pride. Their rejection was not due to lack of exposure but to arrogance, and that stubborn pride led them to persist in transgression and injustice; being called “a people of criminals” signifies moral guilt for violating God’s limits and harming others rather than mere legal criminality.

translation: And when it is said, “Indeed the promise of Allah is true and there is no doubt about the Hour,” you say, “We do not know what the Hour is; we only suppose (conjecture), and we are not certain.”
interpretation: The verse describes a stance of willful doubt: people verbally concede Allah’s promise yet dismiss the Resurrection as mere conjecture. Saying “we only suppose” is not innocent ignorance but a defensive posture that reduces a clear divine truth to personal opinion, allowing them to evade moral responsibility. The passage therefore criticizes an attitude that replaces conviction with flimsy speculation and shows that lack of certainty about the Hour is a self‑chosen denial, not a valid theological position.

translation: And the evils of what they had done became apparent to them, and what they were mocking encompassed them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when the hidden harm of sinful actions is finally revealed—especially at the moment of divine reckoning—those who once ridiculed warnings and signs will be overtaken by the very consequences they made light of; their mockery will turn to helpless regret as the true nature and effects of their deeds are laid bare and surround them.

translation:
وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنسَاكُمْ كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَٰذَا ۚ وَمَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ ۚ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ
“And it will be said, ‘Today We will abandon you as you abandoned the meeting of this your Day; your abode is the Fire, and you will have no helpers.’”
interpretation: The verse conveys that on the Day of Reckoning God will enact a fitting response to those who denied or were heedless of the Resurrection: they will be ‘forgotten’ not in the sense of Divine ignorance (God is All‑Knowing) but as a withdrawal of Divine mercy, protection and favor, mirroring the way they neglected the meeting with their Lord. Their final dwelling becomes Hell, and none of their worldly allies, idols, or claimed intercessors will be able to aid them. The passage thus stresses moral accountability and that the consequences people experience correspond to the stance they took toward truth and the afterlife.

translation: That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you; so today they will not come out of it, nor will they be granted a reprieve.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the final, irrevocable punishment of certain people: by treating Allah’s revelations as a joke and being misled by the fleeting attractions of worldly life, they have forfeited any hope of release or postponement on the Day of Reckoning. “They will not come out of it” points to confinement in the appointed punishment, and “nor will they be granted a reprieve” stresses that no excuse, negotiation, or delay will be accepted then — a warning to take divine guidance seriously and not be seduced by temporal comforts.

translation: So to Allah belongs all praise — Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The phrase affirms that every form of praise and gratitude is due exclusively to God because He alone is the sovereign Creator, Sustainer and Governor of all realms. By naming Him Lord of the heavens, the earth and all worlds it denies any rival or divided sovereignty, grounds trust and submission in His comprehensive providence, and summons believers to respond with gratitude, reliance and moral responsibility before the One who rules and sustains all existence.

translation: To Him belongs greatness in the heavens and the earth; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse asserts that ultimate majesty and sovereignty belong solely to God: His authority pervades every realm of existence, leaving no place exempt from His dominion. Describing Him as al‑ʿAzīz (the Mighty/Invincible) affirms that His power is absolute and cannot be overcome, while al‑Hakīm (the Wise) affirms that His will and decrees are guided by perfect wisdom and purpose. Together these attributes teach that divine rule is neither arbitrary nor weak—God’s might is rightly exercised with insight and justice—so the proper human response is to abandon pride, recognize our relative position, trust in God’s judgments, and align our actions with the wisdom manifest in His commands.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā, Mīm.
interpretation: The disconnected letters Ḥā and Mīm act as a divine sign pointing to the miracle of the Qur’an: though composed of ordinary Arabic letters, its meaning, eloquence and transformative power cannot be produced by human effort. By presenting these bare letters God both draws attention and issues a tacit challenge to human language, thus testifying to the Qur’an’s divine origin and inviting reflection on realities that transcend the mere alphabetic signs.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All‑Wise.
interpretation: This declares that the scripture’s origin is God’s sovereign will and is infused with His attributes of power and wisdom; therefore the Book’s commands, prohibitions, narratives and judgments are not human opinions but purposeful, authoritative guidance — designed with divine wisdom to order human life and backed by God’s invincible power, calling for trust in its truth and compliance with its guidance.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth, and for an appointed term; yet those who disbelieve turn away from that with which they were warned.
interpretation: The verse affirms that creation is purposeful and governed by God’s truthful design and a fixed term (ajal), signifying order, meaning, and eventual accountability. It contrasts this reality with the stance of disbelievers who, despite clear signs and warnings, consciously avert themselves from accepting the truth—showing that evidence of divine authority is presented, but moral responsibility remains with each person to heed it rather than turning away.

translation:
قُلْ «أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ؟ أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ؟ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ؟ أَوْ أَرْسَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهِيدًا؟ أَتَرُونَكُمْ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمْ شَهِيدًا؟» — «أِيُّهَا النَّاسُ مَنِ الَّذِي يَرْعَاكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ؟»» (rendered to mirror the Arabic wording)

Say: “Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this or a trace of knowledge, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse is a polemical demand for evidence addressed to those who worship other than God: it forces the claimants to produce tangible proof that their deities possess real creative power, authority in the heavens, or an earlier revealed scripture or verifiable knowledge. By shifting the burden of proof onto those making the extraordinary claim, the verse exposes the impotence and invented nature of idols and false gods and underscores the principle that truth claims require demonstrable evidence — a proof the idolaters cannot provide, thereby vindicating the claim of divine sovereignty and the legitimacy of true revelation.

translation: And who is more astray than one who calls upon besides Allah someone who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are heedless of their invocation?
interpretation: The verse condemns the spiritual error of placing trust and seeking support from powerless beings or idols: doing so reveals both misplaced dependence and a kind of spiritual blindness. True guidance and response belong to God alone, so expecting help from entities that cannot hear, act, or be held accountable is fundamentally misguided and diverts a person from the path of sincere reliance on Allah.

translation: And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them; and in their worship they were disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Gathering those whom people once trusted or worshipped (idols, false deities or false objects of devotion) will prove hostile and of no help to their worshippers. The worship these people offered was in reality disbelief—misdirected, associating partners or rejecting true guidance—so it will not avail them, and what they had relied upon will turn against them.

translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, “This is obvious magic.”
interpretation: The verse highlights a moral-psychological explanation for rejection: people may dismiss even clear, persuasive evidence by labeling it ‘magic’ to avoid the consequences of accepting it. Rather than honestly weighing the signs, the disbelievers resort to delegitimizing the source and protecting their pride, interests, or worldview; this demonstrates inward resistance and intellectual dishonesty, showing that the refusal is rooted not in lack of proof but in a willful closing of the heart and mind.

translation: Or do they say, “He invented it”? Say, “If I had invented it, then you would have no power to protect me from Allah at all; He knows best what you ascribe. He is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse responds to accusations that the Prophet fabricated the revelation by pointing to the ultimate arbitrariness of human claims when faced with God's knowledge and judgment. It affirms that accusations cannot alter divine reality or confer protection, for God alone knows inner motives and is the decisive Witness between claimant and accused. At the same time, invoking God as “the Forgiving, the Merciful” balances warning and mercy: those who falsely accuse will be held to account by One who fully knows, yet the door to repentance and divine pardon remains open. The passage thus both vindicates the messenger’s integrity and reminds the community that truth and moral responsibility rest ultimately before God, not with human slander or defense.

translation: Say, “I am not something new among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The speaker affirms his limited human status and his sole dependence on divine revelation: he is not an invented or novel messenger, he does not possess knowledge of the unseen or of future outcomes, and his responsibility is simply to convey what God reveals. His role is that of a clear warner — to communicate the message faithfully without claiming control over its acceptance or over events — leaving judgment and ultimate consequences to God. This statement emphasizes prophetic humility, the authority of revelation as the basis for guidance, and the principle that acceptance or rejection and their outcomes rest with the people and with God alone.

translation: Say, “Then have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, while a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes, and you are arrogant — indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse confronts stubborn rejection by showing that denial of divine guidance, even when corroborated by an external, credible witness, is rooted in pride and injustice; such arrogance closes the heart to guidance, so persistent obstinacy in rejecting truth makes one spiritually misguided and beyond God’s guidance until one abandons that oppressive stance.

translation: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه ۚ وإذ لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم
interpretation: الآية تكشف عن أسلوب رفض الحق لدى المكذبين: بدلاً من محاججة بالدليل، يلطخون النيات ويرمون المؤمنين بالسبق أو التحالف لتقليل قيمة الرسالة، ثم إذا لم تهدِهم يؤكدون أنها مجرد افتراء قديم. المقصود أن الرفض نابع من تحيّز وحسد وعناد لا من نقص في البراهين، والآية تبيّن أن مثل هذه الحجج ليست رداً موضوعياً بل أساليب تصفية حسابات ومعارضة مسبقة.

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy. And this is a book confirming (what came) before it, [delivered] in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who transgress and as glad tidings for the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s guidance is continuous: the Torah given to Moses functioned as a moral guide and mercy, and the Qur’an affirms and clarifies that same divine message for its immediate audience by being revealed in Arabic. Its purpose is twofold—sternly to admonish those who persist in wrongdoing and injustice, and reassuringly to promise reward and hope to those who cultivate righteousness—thus balancing God’s justice and mercy and stressing accountability and encouragement within a single, coherent revelation.

translation: Indeed, those who have said, “Our Lord is Allah,” then remained steadfast — upon them is no fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: The verse promises spiritual security to those whose profession of tawḥid (“Our Lord is Allah”) is joined by istiqamah — steady faith and upright conduct. It does not mean that such people will be exempt from tests, but that by sincere belief and persistent obedience they are safeguarded from ultimate loss: they need not fear final punishment or anxiety about their fate, nor suffer lasting regret or hopeless grief. The assurance points to inner peace, trust in God’s justice and mercy, and victory in the eternal reckoning for those who maintain rectitude.

translation: أُولَـئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
interpretation: الآية تصف فئة مؤمنة أتمت الأعمال الصالحة فكان جزاؤها عند الله معاشاً أبديّاً في الجنة؛ «خلدين فيها» تؤكد دوام النعيم بلا زوال، و«جزاء بما كانوا يعملون» تبيّن أن هذا النعيم نتيجة عادلة لأفعالهم في الحياة — هو ثواب إلهي مقرون بمحكمة الحساب والجزاء وفق ما عملوا.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning [together] are thirty months, until when he reaches maturity and reaches forty years he says, 'My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteous deeds pleasing to You, and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed I have repented to You, and indeed I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse teaches that showing kindness to one’s parents is a divine command grounded in recognition of the burdens parents—especially the mother—bear in bringing a child into the world and raising them. By noting the long period of dependency (the carrying and weaning) the text highlights continual parental sacrifice and the child’s owed debt of respect and care. The depiction of a person at full maturity (here marked by forty) turning to Allah models spiritual awakening: gratitude is not merely feeling but a capacity one asks Allah to grant, and it must be expressed through righteous deeds that please Him. The supplication to make one’s offspring righteous links personal reform with responsibility for future generations. Finally, the concluding repentance and declaration of submission show that true maturity combines gratefulness, active righteousness, concern for one’s lineage, sincere turning back to Allah, and wholehearted acceptance of His guidance.

translation: Those are the ones of whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds; they will be among the companions of Paradise — the true promise that they were promised.
interpretation: The verse conveys that Divine judgment favors the sincere excellence of believers: God, in His justice and mercy, gives weight to their best, most earnest actions and pardons lesser failings, admitting them into Paradise as the fulfillment of His truthful promise. It emphasizes that wholehearted intention and striving for good, coupled with reliance on God’s mercy, determine ultimate success rather than a strict ledger of faults alone.

translation: And [as for] the one who said to his parents, “Aren’t you going to dissuade me so that I will not be brought forth while generations before me have passed away?” — while they were invoking Allah for help, saying, “Woe to you; have you believed? Indeed, the promise of Allah is true” — he said, “This is nothing but tales of the former peoples.”
interpretation: The verse indicts the spiritual malady of prideful denial: some people, though confronted with clear warning and even the heartfelt appeals of those closest to them, choose to dismiss divine truth as mere ancient stories. Their rejection is not born of honest doubt but of impatience, arrogance, and self-justifying rationalization; it severs filial responsibility and moral accountability and marks the heart’s blindness that precedes ruin.

translation: Those are the ones concerning whom the word has been fulfilled among peoples who passed away before them — of jinn and of mankind — indeed they were losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that divine judgment is consistent and inevitable: those who persist in denial and rebellious wrongdoing repeat the errors of past communities and thereby incur true loss — a comprehensive failure that strips them of guidance, success and reward in this life and in the hereafter.

translation: For each are ranks according to what they did; and He will repay them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse affirms divine justice expressed as proportional accountability: people are assigned differing ranks or stations — in this life and especially in the hereafter — that correspond to the quality and quantity of their actions. God’s recompense is exact and fair, so every deed, however small, will be taken into account and rewarded or requited appropriately; no one will be denied what is due nor subjected to injustice. The phrase thus both comforts the believer that no good effort is wasted and warns that moral responsibility carries real consequences, encouraging earnest pursuit of righteousness and care in conduct.

translation: And the Day when those who disbelieved are presented to the Fire [it will be said], “Did you expend your good things in the life of this world and enjoy them? So today you will be recompensed with humiliating punishment for what you used to be arrogant about on the earth without right and for what you used to transgress.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that temporary worldly enjoyment and the use of God’s blessings as mere pleasures — especially when coupled with pride, injustice and habitual disobedience — will not avert accountability at resurrection. It links the chastisement in the Hereafter directly to a moral cause: those who lived arrogantly and exceeded bounds while reveling in earthly goods will receive a degrading, humiliating punishment; the passage thus warns against treating worldly gains as an end in themselves and against arrogance and transgression, calling people to humility, justice and preparedness for final judgment.

translation: And remember the brother of ʿĀd when he warned his people in al‑Aḥqāf — and warners had already gone before him and after him — [saying], “Do not worship anyone but Allāh; indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.”
interpretation: The verse presents the prophet’s compassionate urgency: he stands within a continuous chain of messengers and, seeing his people entrenched in false worship, pleads for exclusive devotion to God out of fear of catastrophic recompense. It teaches that prophetic warning is both a moral responsibility and an act of mercy, and that persistent rejection of clear guidance — despite previous and subsequent warnings — brings about severe consequences, whether immediate communal destruction or the decisive punishment of the Last Day. The passage therefore calls listeners to heed the recurring message of monotheism to avert ruin and to submit to God before it is too late.

translation: قالوا: «أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُفْسِدَنَا عَن آلِهَتِنَا؟ فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِن كُنتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ»
interpretation: الآية تكشف عن أسلوب رفض الناس للتوجيه الأخلاقي: بدل أن يواجهوا الحجة أو يغيّروا سلوكهم، يتهمون الناصح بأنه مسبب للفتنة ويطلبون برهانًا خارقًا وفوريًا كشرط للاعتراف. هذا طلب للاعتراض والمماطلة — وسيلة لتفادي المسؤولية الأخلاقية والدعوة إلى دليل خارق بدل الانتباه إلى الأدلة العملية والأثر المعنوي للرسالة.

translation: He said, “Knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I was sent with; but I see you a people who know not.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes prophetic humility and the theology of revelation: ultimate knowledge of the unseen belongs solely to God, while the prophet’s role is to faithfully communicate what he receives, not to claim independent access to hidden truths. By calling his listeners “a people who know not,” the speaker reproves their willful ignorance and rejection of guidance, urging them to abandon arrogance and accept the conveyed message.

translation: So when they saw it approaching their valleys, they said, “This is a cloud that will bring us rain.” Rather, it was that which you were eager for — a wind in which is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that people can mistake impending divine retribution for a hoped‑for blessing when it comes in a familiar guise; their eagerness for an outcome (here, relief or gain) can blind them to its true nature, so that what they hastened after becomes the instrument of their own destruction — a reminder that desires pursued outside of God’s guidance may bring ruin rather than benefit.

translation: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, so nothing was seen of them except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the guilty people.
interpretation: The verse conveys that God’s sovereign will can bring about swift and total punishment for persistent wrongdoing; the survival of mere dwellings functions not primarily as an accidental remnant but as a didactic sign—an intended testimony left for others to witness and reflect upon. In this way divine recompense is both just and instructive: the visible ruins admonish future generations to recognize God’s authority, the consequences of transgression, and the inevitability of accountability for those who persist in crime and corruption.

translation: And indeed We made them secure in what We had made you secure in, and We gave them hearing and sight and hearts; but their hearing and their sight and their hearts did not avail them at all, for they were rejecting the signs of Allah; and what they used to ridicule overtook them.
interpretation: God reminds that past communities were granted the same worldly stability and the same faculties of hearing, sight and understanding as others, yet those very gifts did not save them because they obstinately rejected God’s signs. The point is moral and practical: senses and intellect are means, not guarantees — they benefit only when used to recognize and submit to truth. Comfort, power, or natural talents cannot avert the consequences of persistent denial and ridicule of divine guidance; those who scorn the message will ultimately be overtaken by the very outcome they mocked.

translation: And certainly We destroyed the towns around you and set forth the signs so that they might return.
interpretation: The verse means that when communities persisted in denial and wrongdoing, God brought destruction upon neighboring towns as a manifest evidence of His warning. By “setting forth the signs” He made the consequences and lessons clear and visible, not merely to punish but to prompt reflection and repentance; the punitive events are thus presented as deliberate, didactic warnings intended to turn people back to obedience before it is too late.

translation: If only those whom they took as deities besides Allah would help them! — No; rather those (false gods) have turned away from them. That is their lie and what they used to invent.
interpretation: The verse rejects the idea that anything created can truly support or intercede for people: the beings or things set up as gods besides Allah are powerless and in fact abandon those who depend on them. The belief that such intermediaries can bring help or nearness is a falsehood and fabrication; the passage therefore exposes the futility of putting trust in idols or created things and redirects reliance to God alone.

translation: And when We directed to you a party of the jinn who listened to the Qur'ān; and when they attended it, they said, “Be silent.” And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners.
interpretation: The verse signifies that the Qurʾān’s truth and authority transcend human bounds: its message compels attentive, reverent reception and elicits immediate conviction, and those who truly encounter it acquire a duty to convey and warn their communities. It also affirms that jinn are morally accountable beings who can recognize revelation, be transformed by it, and become transmitters of guidance—underscoring the universality of prophetic responsibility and the transformative power of God’s speech.

translation: قالوا: "يا قومنا، إنا سمعنا كتابًا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقًا لما بين يديه يهدي إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم."
interpretation: الآية تعبّر عن مبدأ محوري في الوحي: أن الكتب التي تنزل بعد كتاب موسى ليست قطعًا منفصلة بل تؤكد جوهر الرسالة الإلهية السابقة وتعمل كمعيار يهدِي للحق ويبين السبيل المستقيم. القول هنا يبرز أن قبول الوحي اللاحق واعترافه بما سبقه يعيد الناس إلى وحدة العقيدة والأخلاق التي أرادها الله، وأن الرفض أو التحيّز لقراءات جزئية من الكتب القديمة يبعد عن هذا المعيار. بالتالي الرسالة المدعاة هي دعوة إلى الاستجابة لما يقرّ الحق ويصلح المسار، سواء في جانب الإيمان بتوحيد الله وتعاليمه أو في جانب السلوك العملي الذي ينسجم مع الطريق المستقيم.

translation: O my people, respond to the call of Allah and believe in Him; He will forgive you your sins and save you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This address presents God’s summons as a turning point: accepting it through sincere faith and return transforms one’s standing before God. The verse emphasizes that divine mercy is not merely abstract but effective — genuine acceptance leads to reconciliation (removal of past guilt) and deliverance from impending retribution — so the exhortation is simultaneously an invitation to restorative mercy and a sober warning that such mercy requires an active, heartfelt response.

translation: And whoever does not answer the Caller of Allah — then there is none who can avert [Him] on the earth, nor do they have any protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s summons—refusing guidance, obedience, or accountability—means one has no real defender or rescuer in this world apart from Allah; no human power can avert His decree. Such a stance severs the sole source of true protection and guidance, leaving the person plainly misguided and exposed to the consequences of their turning away.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah — He who created the heavens and the earth and was not hindered in their creation — is able to give life to the dead? Yes indeed; He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse confronts those who deny resurrection by pointing to the clear, effortless power God displayed in creating and sustaining the vast cosmos: if God could bring the heavens and earth into being without impediment, then restoring life to the dead is well within His capacity. It affirms God’s absolute omnipotence and rebukes disbelief that judges the impossible for the Creator who controls all things.

translation: And on the Day those who disbelieved are presented to the Fire — “Is this not the truth?” — they will say, “Yes, by our Lord.” He will say, “Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment of accountability when the reality of divine judgment becomes undeniable to those who rejected the message. Their belated admission of the truth does not avert the consequence because faith requires sincere, timely acceptance rather than forced acknowledgement after the fact. The passage emphasizes God’s justice: persistent denial of clear guidance brings an experiential and fitting consequence (ذُوقُوا العذاب), demonstrating that moral responsibility and choices in this life determine one’s outcome on the Day of Recompense.

translation: So be patient, as were the resolute among the messengers, and do not be impatient for them. It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised, they had remained no longer than an hour of a day. [This is] a proclamation — so who will perish except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: The verse counsels the Prophet to adopt the calm, enduring patience of the great, steadfast messengers and not to try to force God’s judgment. It teaches that divine justice may be delayed in human perception but will arrive suddenly and decisively — what seems long in worldly terms will be compressed into an instant on the Day of Reckoning — and therefore the proper stance is confident, restrained endurance rather than impatience or vindictiveness. The word “بلاغ” underlines that this is a clear, final warning: ultimately only those who persist in wilful disobedience and moral corruption will be destroyed.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Those who disbelieve and prevent (others) from the way of Allah — their deeds have been rendered vain.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent rejection of faith coupled with actively obstructing others’ guidance corrupts the moral value of a person’s actions: God causes their deeds to go astray so that outward works, despite appearances, fail to bring reward or spiritual benefit. Actively turning people away from the path of Allah thus becomes a decisive factor that nullifies one's deeds and leads to ultimate loss.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad — it is the truth from their Lord — He will erase from them their misdeeds and set right their condition.
interpretation: The verse conveys that when faith is genuine (including acceptance of the revelation brought by the Prophet) and is lived out in righteous action, God’s response is restorative: He removes the burden of past wrongs and brings inner and outward repair. “Kafara” implies not merely legal pardon but the wiping away or covering of moral stains, while “aṣlaḥa balahum” indicates a real reformation of hearts and life circumstances. Thus faith-plus-deeds trigger divine mercy that both purifies the person and redirects their affairs toward spiritual and practical well‑being.

translation: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus Allah presents examples to the people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the fundamental difference between communities lies in what they choose to follow: adherence to falsehood (driven by desires, misleading authorities, or corrupt reasoning) leads away from reality, while acceptance of the truth that comes from God leads toward genuine guidance. Allah’s use of parables and examples is a deliberate pedagogical method: by comparing and illustrating, He makes the unseen moral and spiritual consequences of those choices perceptible, invites reflection, and clarifies for people why their paths produce differing outcomes.

translation: “So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike the necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds; then either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] — until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the ordinance]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered this] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah — never will He let their deeds be lost.”
interpretation: This verse provides a wartime ruling and its moral framework: it commands decisive force against hostile combatants in the specific context of battle, followed by restraint and regulated treatment of prisoners (binding and then either release as an act of mercy or exchange/payment) until hostilities end. The passage also explains that God did not immediately annihilate opponents in order to leave human beings responsible for the test of conduct and faith toward one another, and it reassures believers that those who fall fighting for God’s cause are not forgotten — their deeds will be preserved. In short, the verse balances legitimate use of force in armed conflict with limits, procedures, and a higher moral purpose (trial, accountability, and care for the fallen).

translation: He will guide them and set their hearts aright.
interpretation: The phrase indicates that divine guidance does not merely give correct beliefs or outward rules, but effects an inward transformation: God illuminates their understanding, removes doubt and hypocrisy, straightens their intentions, and heals their spiritual condition so that both their inner life and consequent actions become rightly ordered.

translation: And He will admit them into Paradise and make it known to them.
interpretation: It means that God will not only grant the righteous entrance into Paradise but will unveil to them its true reality and blessings — the gardens, delights, companions, and the nearness to Him — so that they fully recognize, experience, and are satisfied with the reward prepared for them, leaving no doubt about the justice and generosity of their Lord.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.
interpretation: The promise here is that when believers actively uphold God’s way—through sincere faith, obedience, moral courage, enjoining right and striving against injustice—God responds with real assistance: victory, protection, and a settled resolve. “Supporting Allah” does not mean aiding God’s omnipotence but committing to His guidance and cause; in return God steadies their position, strengthens their resolve and stabilizes their community in the face of trials.

translation: And as for those who disbelieve—woe unto them, and He has led their deeds astray.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent rejection of God’s guidance brings ruin: by turning away from truth, disbelievers render their actions ineffective or misdirected so that those deeds neither attain divine approval nor lead to genuine good; instead of benefiting them, their works become a source of further loss and misguidance, exemplifying the spiritual consequence of unbelief in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He nullified their deeds.
interpretation: Because they rejected and harbored aversion toward Allah’s revelation, the sincerity and guidance that make actions acceptable before God were removed; consequently, Allah rendered their outward deeds void of reward. In other words, turning away from divine guidance and acting from hostility to it causes actions to lose their spiritual validity and benefit.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them; and for the disbelievers is the like of that.
interpretation: The verse is a call to sober reflection: by urging people to 'travel through the earth' and look at the ruined outcomes of earlier nations, it presents historical destruction as a clear, empirical sign of the moral law that persistent rejection of God's guidance and habitual corruption brings ruin. Its purpose is not mere historical notice but moral warning—those who emulate the disbelief and wrongdoing of former peoples risk the same divine consequences unless they repent, reform, and heed the guidance conveyed by the messengers.

translation:
ذلك بأن الله مولى الذين آمنوا وأن الكافرين لا مولى لهم
"That is because Allah is the Protector (Wali) of those who believe, and the disbelievers have no protector (wali) of their own."
interpretation: The verse affirms that true guardianship and ultimate support belong to God: believers who submit to Him receive His guidance, protection and sustaining authority that secures them spiritually and—in the decisive sense—against misguidance and loss. By contrast, those who reject faith lack that transcendent, reliable patron; any worldly allies they claim cannot substitute for divine protection nor avert the moral and existential consequences of turning away from God. The practical implication is that allegiance, trust and dependence must be placed first in Allah, for He is the lasting guardian whose support determines ultimate success.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow; and those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as the cattle eat, and the Fire will be their abode.
interpretation: The verse teaches that apparent worldly ease and consumption, when disconnected from faith and moral responsibility, is a degrading, temporary condition—likened to the unreflective eating of cattle—and ultimately leads to ruin, whereas true, enduring dignity and reward belong to those whose belief is realized through righteous action; thus the passage emphasizes divine justice and warns that fleeting pleasures can be deceptive unless paired with moral accountability.

translation: And how many a town, stronger than your town — the one that expelled you — We destroyed them; they had no helper.
interpretation: The verse teaches that temporal power and social dominance cannot shield a people from divine accountability: communities that opposed God's messengers and persisted in wrongdoing, even when stronger than the Prophet’s persecutors, were ultimately overthrown by God and found no one to defend them. It both comforts the oppressed believer by reminding them that present hardship does not determine the final outcome and warns the arrogant that worldly strength is not a safeguard against moral failure and divine judgment.

translation:
أَفَمَنْ كَانَ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ
“Is one who stands on clear proof from his Lord like one for whom his evil deed has been made attractive and who followed their desires?”
interpretation: The verse draws a decisive distinction between two spiritual states: those who receive unmistakable guidance from God and act upon it, and those whose sins are cosmetically disguised so that they pursue their passions. It teaches that genuine conviction rooted in divine evidence cannot be equated with self‑deception—when wrongdoing is beautified and people follow their desires they are being led away from guidance and toward ruin, whereas the one on clear proof is rightly guided and accountable in a different, far more hopeful way.

translation: مثلُ الجَنّةِ التي وُعِدَ المتقونَ: فيها أنهارٌ من ماءٍ غير آسنٍ، وأنهارٌ من لبنٍ لم يَتَغَيَّر طعمه، وأنهارٌ من خَمْرٍ لِذًّةٌ للشاربينَ، وأنهارٌ من عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى، ولهم فيها من كلِّ الثمراتِ ومغفرةٌ من ربِّهم. أَفَمَثَلُ مَنْ هو خالدٌ في النارِ وسُقوا ماءً حَميمًا فَقطَعَ أمعاءهم؟
interpretation: الآية تُرسي مبدأً أخلاقيًا وتربويًا: الجزاء الإلهي يَنعكس صِفَةً على صِفَةِ صاحبه. نعيمُ المتقين موصوفٌ بصفاءٍ وديمومةٍ ووفرةٍ روحية ومادية—ماءٌ غير معكّر، لبنٌ لا يتغير طعمه، خمرٌ لذةً بلا فساد، عسلٌ مُصفّى، وثمراتٌ متنوعة، مع عطيةٍ أعظم هي مغفرةُ الربّ—دلالة أن المكافأة الإلهية ليست مجرد ملذات حسّية بل كمالٌ ونقاءٌ يملأ القلب والروح. مقابل ذلك، التشبيهُ بالنارِ وماءٍ حارٍّ يقطع الأمعاء يُظهر أن العقاب ليس مجرد ألمٍ مؤقت بل تدميرُ الحياة والإنسانية. المقارنةُ الرهيبةُ تعمل كتحذيرٍ فعال: الاختيار الأخلاقي له نتائج جوهرية لا تُقاس بمظاهر الدنيا، والابتعاد عن التقوى يؤدي إلى خسارةٍ شاملة، بينما التقوى تُحصّل للإنسان صفاءً ودوامًا ومغفرةً من الله.

translation: وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى إِذَا خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِندِكَ قَالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ مَاذَا قَالَ آنِفًا ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ
interpretation: الآية تصف نوعًا من الناس يظهر سمعًا ظاهريًا للحق ولكنه لا يستقبله بقلبه؛ حين يخرج من مجلس الوعظ أو المواجهة يتظاهر بالجهل أو يسأل العلماء عن الكلام كطريقة للتملص أو للسخرية بدلاً من قبول النصيحة. ختم الله على قلوبهم هنا ليس مجرد عقوبة عرضية بل نتيجة تراكمية لاختيارهم أهواءهم وانتقاصهم من قيم الحق، فصاروا مقفلين على فهم الهدى وغير قادرين على التلقي لأنه لم تعد لهم إرادة صادقة للاتباع.

translation: And those who were guided — He increased them in guidance, and bestowed upon them their piety (taqwa).
interpretation: Sincere acceptance of God’s guidance is not static: God deepens that guidance and implants taqwa — a sustained God‑consciousness and reverent self-restraint — which becomes the believer’s inner safeguard. This bestowed piety refines intention, governs behavior, protects from relapse into error, and makes the initial guidance firm and growing rather than fleeting.

translation:
فهل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة ۖ فقد جاء أشراطها ۚ فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم
"Do they then await anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come. So how will they be when their reminders come to them?"
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who profess to merely await the Final Hour as if it will arrive unexpectedly, while they ignore the clear signs that have already appeared. It points out the self‑contradiction and warning: having seen the portents, their continued heedlessness leaves them without excuse, and when the decisive reminders (the final summons, judgment and admonitions) actually reach them they will be powerless, shocked and unable to benefit from warning or repentance.

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah; and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and the believing women. And Allah knows your coming and your going and your resting places.
interpretation: Affirming the oneness of God is presented as the foundation that should move a person to sincere repentance and to intercede with forgiveness on behalf of the whole believing community; this inward turning is not merely private because God is fully aware of all our movements, changes of state, and ultimate situations — so recognition of tawḥīd must be lived out in humble self-accountability, communal care, and constant seeking of God’s mercy, since nothing of our inner or outer life is hidden from Him.

translation: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ «لَوْلَا نُزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ» ۖ فَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ سُورَةٌ مُّحْكَمَةٌ وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا الْقِتَالُ، تَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ نَظْرَ الْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ؛ فَوَيْلٌ لَهُمْ
interpretation: الآية توبخ أولئك الذين يطلبون آياتٍ أو سوراً تيسر لهم الدين فتُظهر رغبتهم في السهولة، ثم هم عند مواجهة الأحكام العملية المرهِقة ـ خاصة القتال أو الجهاد حين يُذكر ـ يَنبُهُ خوفهم وضعفهم وحب النفس. «مرض في القلوب» وصفٌ لضعف الإيمان أو نَفَحِ النفاق الذي يجعل القلب يتهيب أداء الواجب، ونظرتهم للمُرسَل كمن يكاد يُغشى عليه دلالة على تملص وارتباكٍ بل خِذلان. المقصود تذكير بأن الإيمان الحقيقي يقاس بالثبات عند الامتحان والالتزام بأمر الله مهما كان مشقّاً، وأن مجرد التنديد بطلب التسهيل يكشف عن خلل باطني سيؤدي إلى سوء الجزاء والمآل.

translation: طاعةٌ وقولٌ معروفٌ. فإذا عزمَ الأمرُ فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرًا لهم.
interpretation: الآية تحذر من الاكتفاء بالمظهر — طاعة ظاهرة وكلام لطيف — دون صدق وإخلاص عند لحظة الحسم. عندما يتطلب الأمر قرارًا جريئًا أو التزامًا حقيقيًا، يفشل من يكتفون بالظاهر لأنهم لم يكونوا صادقين مع الله في نواياهم وعهودهم؛ ولو صدقوا الله بقلوبهم وأفعالهم لكان نتيجة ذلك خيرًا لهم. الرسالة الأساسية أن الإيمان الحقيقي يظهر في الصدق والعمل الحاسم لا في المواقف الشكلية أو الأقوال الخفيفة.

translation: Did you think — then, if you were to turn away — that you would spread corruption on the earth and cut off your ties of kinship?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who imagine that rejecting God’s guidance or abandoning the Prophet frees them from moral responsibility; instead it warns that such turning away inevitably produces moral and social decay—injustice, disorder and the breaking of family bonds. It teaches that faith and submission are safeguards against selfishness and communal harm, and that severing kinship and spreading corruption are the visible consequences of abandoning divine guidance.

translation:
أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَهُمْ وَأَعْمَىٰ أَبْصَارَهُمْ
"Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed; so He has made them deaf and deprived them of sight."
interpretation: The verse conveys that through persistent rejection, hypocrisy, and deliberate turning away from guidance, God withdraws His mercy and seals their receptivity: their inner faculties to perceive and accept truth are rendered 'deaf' and 'blind.' This is both a divinely sanctioned consequence and a form of punishment—making them incapable of receiving guidance and thus preventing further harm from their obstinacy.

translation:
أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها
"Will they not then reflect on the Qur'an? Or are there locks upon their hearts?"
interpretation: The phrase challenges spiritual dullness: understanding the Qur'an requires sincere, contemplative attention, yet many cannot receive its guidance because their inner faculties are blocked. These “locks” symbolize moral and spiritual obstacles — pride, persistent sin, heedlessness, preoccupation with worldly concerns, or a hardened disposition from repeated rejection — which prevent insight and soften the heart’s responsiveness. The passage implies both an account of why guidance is missed and a call to remove those barriers through humility, repentance, and genuine reflection so the Qur’an’s meanings can be apprehended.

translation: Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them — Satan suggested to them and gave them false hopes.
interpretation: The verse explains that when people abandon the truth after it was made manifest to them, their turning away is not merely personal whim but the result of satanic deception: Satan insinuates doubts, entices with comforting suggestions, and grants illusory respite or promises so they postpone repentance and persist in error, ultimately leading them away from guidance and toward loss.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah had sent down, “We will obey you in some matters.” And Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: The verse indicts hypocritical behavior: some people placate opponents of God’s revelation by promising outward compliance in certain matters while concealing their true loyalties and intentions. It warns that such pretenses—agreeing publicly to those who reject divine guidance to gain favor or avoid conflict—do not escape God’s knowledge, for He is aware of the hidden motives and inner conspiracies behind their words.

translation:
فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم
"So what will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?"
interpretation: The verse depicts the moment of death for those who persisted in denial and wrongdoing: the angels, executing divine judgment, seize them in a manner that strips them of dignity and hope — striking faces and backs as a vivid image of humiliation, helplessness, and the decisive removal of mercy. It conveys that their worldly obstinacy and rejection of truth culminate in an irreversible, shameful end when they stand powerless before God's will.

translation: ذلك لأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه، فأحبط أعمالهم.
interpretation: المعنى أن اتباع ما يثير سخط الله ووجود موقف معاد لمراده ورضاه يؤدي إلى بطلان الأعمال أمام الميزان الإلهي؛ أي أن الأعمال الخارجية لا تُقبل ولا تُثمر ثوابًا عندما يكون القلوب متجهة إلى ما يغضب الله ويرفضون ما يطلب رضاه، فينقض الله تلك الأعمال ويُحرِم فاعليها من قبولها.

translation:
أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ أَنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغَانَهُمْ
"Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring forth their rancour?"
interpretation: Those who harbour an inner sickness — hypocrisy, malice, envy or hatred toward the truth and the believers — are deluded if they imagine God will leave that hidden. Allah will either expose their rancour and hold them to account or purge and reform their hearts; He does not let the inward corruption remain concealed.

translation: And if We had willed, We would have shown them to you, and then you would have known them by their marks; and you would have known them by the manner of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: The verse points to God’s sovereign choice about what to reveal and what to conceal: He could make people’s inner states manifest by outward signs or speech, yet He often withholds such exposure for wisdoms — to preserve tests, prevent harm, and regulate divine guidance. The practical lesson is restraint: since true knowledge of hearts and deeds belongs to God alone, believers should not rely on appearances to pass final judgement but remain humble, avoid rash accusations, and trust God’s timing and justice.

translation: And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and those who are patient; and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God puts the community through trials so that true dispositions and commitments are revealed: those who genuinely struggle in His way (through effort, sacrifice and steady commitment) and those who endure with patience. The phrase “we will test your affairs/أخباركم” indicates that inner states, intentions and real conduct become exposed under pressure. Such testing serves to purify and distinguish the sincere from the pretenders, to establish who merits reward and responsibility, and to strengthen and correct the community by bringing hidden realities to light.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and obstruct the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them — they will not harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deliberate rejection and active obstruction of God’s guidance, especially after the truth has been made clear, cannot diminish God’s sovereignty or alter His plan; rather it is self‑destructive: such opposition nullifies the moral and spiritual worth of the opponents’ deeds. Emphasis on “after guidance became clear” makes their culpability greater — their actions are not merely mistaken but willfully contrary — and the consequence is that their hostility only harms themselves, leaving God unaffected while their efforts and claims are rendered void.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not render your deeds void.
interpretation: The verse enjoins that true faith is lived through submission to God’s commands and to the Prophet who conveys them; obedience to the Messenger is not optional but part of obedience to Allah. The warning “do not render your deeds void” means that outward acts of worship and goodness can be nullified by inner defects or contrary conduct—hypocrisy, ostentation, deliberate disobedience, abandoning what the Prophet taught, or reverting to disbelief—so believers must couple righteous actions with sincere faith, conformity to prophetic guidance, and moral consistency for those deeds to be accepted and retain their spiritual value.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder others from the way of Allah, then die while they are disbelievers—Allah will not forgive them.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent rejection of God combined with the active obstruction of people’s guidance is a grave moral crime: if one dies entrenched in that state without sincere repentance, the door to divine forgiveness is closed. It stresses both personal accountability (the sin of disbelief) and the aggravated culpability of causing others to stray, and serves as a stern admonition to abandon hostility to the truth and to seek repentance before death.

translation:
فلا تَهِنوا وَتَدْعُوا إِلَى السَّلْمِ وَأَنتُمْ الْأَعْلَوْنَ ۗ وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ وَلَنْ يُلْقِيَ بِأَعْمَالِكُمْ
“So do not grow weak and call for peace while you are the superior; Allah is with you and He will not let your deeds be in vain.”
interpretation: The verse admonishes believers against losing courage or seeking a premature truce when they hold the advantage; it calls for steadfastness in pursuing what is just and in the mission entrusted to them, assuring that God’s support accompanies them and that their sacrifices and righteous efforts will be preserved and rewarded rather than wasted.

translation:
إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو ۚ وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم
"The life of this world is only play and amusement. If you believe and are conscious of Allah, He will grant you your rewards and will not demand your wealth from you."
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly existence is fleeting and largely superficial; what carries eternal weight is sincere faith (īmān) and God‑consciousness (taqwā). God’s reckoning focuses on inner fidelity and righteous conduct rather than the size of one’s possessions, so the true recompense is given for belief and piety—not for wealth. Practically, this frees the believer from equating material success with divine favor and from despair in poverty: trust in God and cultivate righteousness, for He will grant the real reward without charging you for what you own.

translation: If they ask you for it, you hold back, being stingy, and your resentments come forth.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who, when requested to give of what they possess (typically for charity, support of the community, or the cause of God), respond with avarice and reluctance; their stinginess is not hidden but appears in their expressions and attitudes. This outward reluctance reveals an inner lack of sincere faith and generosity—character traits that the Qur’an condemns and warns will draw God’s disapproval.

translation: Here you are — you are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah — yet among you some are stingy; and whoever is stingy, he is stingy only against his own soul; and Allah is free of need, while you are needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with a people other than you, and they will not be like you.
interpretation: The verse exhorts the community to give for Allah’s cause and condemns miserliness as spiritually self-damaging: withholding wealth from what Allah has commanded does not harm God, who is self-sufficient, but harms the individual and the communal trust that sustains the believers. It also contains a sober warning about collective responsibility—if a community refuses its obligations, God can and will raise others who will fulfill them, so the threat of replacement should spur sincere giving, solidarity, and obedience rather than comfort in hoarding or complacency.

translation:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, We have granted you a clear (manifest) victory.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet that what appears outwardly as a limited or compromised outcome (historically linked to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah) is by God's design a decisive, visible opening that advances the mission of Islam. The “clear victory” means Allah transforms events—even those that seem like setbacks—into means of strengthening the community, validating the Prophet’s authority, opening hearts to the faith, and facilitating future triumphs; it therefore calls for trust in divine wisdom and patience when immediate results seem ambiguous.

translation: That Allah may forgive you your past and future sins, complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a divine reassurance that God’s mercy toward the Prophet (and by extension the faithful) is comprehensive: sins are pardoned not only for what has already occurred but broadly in the course of the mission, and God’s benevolence will be brought to its full effect. The ‘completion of favor’ points to the vindication and establishment of the prophetic mission (turning apparent setbacks into eventual success), while guidance to a ‘straight path’ means ongoing, steadfast direction to uphold truth and moral order. Together the elements teach that Allah’s plan unites forgiveness, the fruition of divine support, and continued guidance so that the community may be restored, strengthened, and led rightly despite trials.

translation: And Allah will grant you a mighty victory.
interpretation: A promise that God will bestow decisive, powerful support that vindicates and elevates the Prophet and the believing community; “نصر عزيز” denotes not merely a temporary aid but an honorable, overpowering help that overturns weakness into strength, secures the truth, and confers lasting prestige—granted in connection with faithfulness, perseverance, and reliance on God.

translation: He is the One who sent down tranquility (sakinah) into the hearts of the believers so that they might increase in faith with their faith. To Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God can and does impart a real inner calm and assurance to believers—sakinah—which functions to strengthen and deepen their faith especially in moments of trial or decision. That reassurance is not merely psychological but is grounded in divine support: God alone commands the ‘hosts’ of heaven and earth (angels, forces, and means under His authority), and because He is fully knowing and perfectly wise, the reassurance and the outcomes that follow are purposeful and ultimately serve the believers’ spiritual welfare and the fulfillment of God’s wise plan.

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally; and He will forgive them their sins. And that is, in the sight of Allah, the great attainment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true faith leads to God's ultimate mercy and reward: forgiveness of sins and an everlasting, bountiful residence symbolized by gardens with flowing rivers. By naming both men and women it emphasizes the equal promise to all sincere believers; by stressing eternal residence and calling this “the great attainment,” it reframes success as spiritual salvation and divine favor rather than transient worldly gain, making God’s pardon and admission to Paradise the supreme objective of a believer’s life.

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women — those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil. Upon them is a doom of evil; and the wrath of Allah is upon them, and He has cursed them and prepared for them Hell — and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: The verse teaches that both external disbelief (associating partners with God) and internal corruption (hypocrisy and ill opinion of God) render one liable to divine wrath and punishment; it stresses that true faith requires sincere inner conviction and a correct understanding of God, and that moral and spiritual accountability covers intentions as well as outward actions, with Hell presented as the just consequence for persistent denial and malice toward the truth.

translation: To Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Ever Exalted in Might, All‑Wise.
interpretation: The phrase declares God’s absolute sovereignty: every regiment and force — whether angels, celestial and earthly powers, the laws of nature, or the ranks of believers and armies — exist and act under His authority. Nothing operates independently of His will, and events that appear as power, triumph, trial, or disorder occur within a framework governed by His might and wisdom. This reassures the faithful that ultimate control rests with One who is invincible and acts with purpose, and it warns those who oppose truth that they stand against a sovereign and wise Lord whose decrees are both powerful and just.

translation: Indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse defines the Prophet’s office: as a witness he testifies to the truth of God’s revelation and stands as living proof of its reality and consequences; as a bringer of good tidings he communicates the promise of God’s mercy and reward to those who follow guidance; and as a warner he alerts people to the moral and eschatological consequences of rejecting that guidance — together these roles establish his mission to testify to the covenant between God and humanity, summon people to righteous conduct, and make clear both the hope and the warning inherent in God’s message.

translation: So that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and assist him, and revere him, and glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse sets out the inward and outward signs of true submission: genuine faith in God and His Messenger must be lived out by actively supporting and defending the prophetic mission, showing proper respect and honour to the Prophet’s station, and by continual remembrance and praise of God day and night; together these attitudes and actions bind the community to its faith and to one another.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge does so only to his own loss; and whoever fulfills what he has promised Allah — He will grant him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that giving allegiance to the Prophet is fundamentally a covenant with God: such pledges are made under divine authority and witness (the image of "the hand of Allah over their hands" conveys God’s sovereignty, protection, and oversight). Therefore breaking that covenant harms the one who breaks it — it is a self-destructive rupture of trust and of one’s relation to God and the community — while faithfully keeping one’s commitment is a morally and spiritually weighty act that God rewards greatly. In short, loyalty to the Prophet is inseparable from fidelity to God, carrying both accountability and the promise of divine recompense.

translation:
سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا ۚ يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم ۚ قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا ۚ بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

Translation: Those of the Bedouins who were left behind will say to you, “Our wealth and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us.” They utter with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, “Then who can give you from Allah anything if He intends for you harm, or give you any harm if He intends for you good?” Rather, Allah is, concerning what you do, Aware.
interpretation: The verse reproves those who offer excuses and insincere pleas: lip-service requests for forgiveness cannot undo the consequences of negligence or alter what Allah has decreed. It stresses that benefit and harm ultimately depend on God’s will, not on last‑minute verbal appeals, and reminds that God knows both outward words and inward realities—sincere repentance and responsible conduct, not hollow excuses, are what matter before Him.

translation: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا
interpretation: الآية تُوجه توبةً وذماً لمن جعل في قلوبهم الحسد والخبث ففرحوا وطمأنوا أنفسهم بأن رسول الله والمؤمنين لن يعودوا إلى أهاليهم؛ تكشف أن سرور المرء بهلاك الآخرين واحتضان الظنون السيئة ليس مجرد خطأ فكري بل علامة فساد أخلاقي يؤدي إلى الهلاك الأخلاقي والاجتماعي، وتحذر أن مثل هذا السلوك يفضي إلى كونهم قوماً بورا—مدمرين وخاسرين في مقام الحقوق والفضيلة.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger—then indeed We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: The verse functions as a solemn theological and moral warning: persistent, culpable rejection of God and His Messenger is met by a predetermined, just response from God. By saying the punishment is “prepared,” the wording stresses both God’s sovereignty and the certainty of consequences for deliberate denial after clear guidance; at the same time the formulation presumes moral responsibility—faith requires sincere acceptance and submission—so the passage underscores divine justice and the gravity of rejecting the truth while leaving open the possibility of mercy for those who turn back.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse proclaims God’s absolute sovereignty over all creation and teaches that mercy and punishment flow from His sole, wise discretion. It both consoles and warns: believers are invited to hope in God’s vast capacity to forgive by turning in sincere repentance, while also remaining humble and mindful of accountability because divine justice is real. Thus the passage balances trust in God’s mercy with an ethical demand for responsibility and righteousness.

translation: Those who were left behind will say when you set out for the spoils to take them, “Let us be with you; we will follow you.” They desire to change the words of Allah. Say, “You will not follow us”; thus did Allah say before. Then they will say, “Rather, you envy us.” Nay, they understood nothing except a little.
interpretation: The verse condemns the hypocrites who stayed behind from the fighting: at the prospect of gain they feign willingness to join only to obtain spoils and to revise divine rulings to suit themselves. Their proposal is insincere—an attempt to ‘change the words of Allah’ for personal advantage—and when exposed they resort to accusing the faithful of envy. The passage exposes their moral and intellectual poverty and teaches that true submission to God cannot be manufactured opportunistically nor excused by false accusations.

translation: Say to the Bedouins who remained behind, “You will be called against a people of great strength; you will fight them or they will submit. If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away, as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.”
interpretation: The verse admonishes those who repeatedly shirk communal duty: God warns that a grave test (here framed as facing a formidable people) will require courage and solidarity, and that true faith is proved by readiness to share the burdens and risks of the community. Willing participation in what is required brings a promised divine reward; persistent avoidance, especially in a pattern like before, exposes moral failure and invites severe consequence. Thus the passage stresses responsibility, sincerity of belief demonstrated through action, and the communal obligation to stand together in trials.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick; and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away — He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that legal obligation and moral blame are measured by one’s capacity: genuine physical incapacity and illness remove the burden of certain duties, for God’s law is merciful and proportionate to ability. At the same time it affirms the moral principle that sincere obedience to God and His Messenger leads to the supreme reward (Paradise), whereas deliberate rejection or turning away from guidance brings divine chastisement; thus responsibility follows capability, and ultimate accountability depends on one’s response to God’s guidance.

translation: Indeed Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree; He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.
interpretation: When people make a sincere, tested commitment to God and His cause—especially under pressure—what matters most is the state of their hearts, which God alone knows. From that inner sincerity He grants divine reassurance (sakīnah) that steadies and strengthens them, and He brings about outcome and relief that may at first seem delayed but is in truth an imminent and fitting victory; thus sincere intention in trial elicits God’s approval, inner peace, and eventual success.

translation: And they took many spoils; and Allah was Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the material gains taken were not accidental but unfolded under God’s sovereign power and wise decree: apparent victories or acquisitions occur by Allah’s permission and serve purposes known to Him. Describing Allah as ‘Azīz’ and ‘Hakīm’ reassures that He enforces His will and arranges outcomes with perfect wisdom, so worldly gains are ultimately subject to His authority and the wise ends He intends.

translation: Allah promised you abundant spoils that you would take; so He hastened this [victory] for you and restrained the hands of people from you, and [this was] so that it might be a sign for the believers and that He might guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s granting of gains—understood both as tangible spoils and as victory, honor, and stability—was effected by His will: He hastened the outcome and checked the hands of opponents. This divine facilitation is intended not merely as a worldly reward but as a manifest sign to strengthen believers’ faith and to turn the experience of success into a moral and communal guidance that leads them onto the straight, God‑guided way.

translation: And others you were not able to [bring about]; Allah has encompassed them. And Allah is, over all things, All‑Powerful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human agency is limited: there are affairs and outcomes beyond our control, but God’s knowledge, authority and power embrace those matters. Rather than despairing or presuming mastery where we have none, believers are called to recognize divine sovereignty, rely on God’s wisdom and justice, and submit to His decree because He is fully capable of managing what we cannot.

translation: And if those who disbelieve were to fight you, they would surely turn their backs; then they would find neither a guardian nor a helper.
interpretation: The verse reassures the community that apparent threats from opponents are ultimately hollow: when genuinely tested, foes who lack faith and divine support will not stand firm but will flee, and no human alliance can substitute for God’s protection. Its purpose is to teach believers to rely on God rather than fear mere numbers or bluster, since true success in confrontation depends on divine backing and those without it will find no real protector or helper.

translation: ذلك هو سنن الله التي كانت من قبل؛ ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلًا.
interpretation: الآية تؤكد أن أسلوب الله في تدبير الأمور والتعامل مع الناس ثابت لا يتبدل: هناك نظام إلهي من جزاءٍ ومكافأة واختبار وبلاء يتكرر عبر التاريخ، وما حلّ بالأمم السابقة عندما أعرضت عن الحق وضاقت ذرعًا بالفساد ليس استثناءً بل تطبيق لهذا القانون الإلهي الثابت، فلا يقدر أحد أن يغيّر قضائه، وعلى الناس أن يتصرفوا على ضوء هذه الثباتية — بالامتثال لله والاعتماد على عدله وعدم توقع تبدّل في سننه.

translation: And He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had made you victorious over them. And Allah is, concerning what you do, All‑Seeing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God intervened to halt mutual violence at the moment of triumph so that victory would not become an occasion for vengeance; this restraint is an expression of divine wisdom and mercy that opens the way for reconciliation and magnanimity rather than revenge, while reminding the believers that Allah continually observes their actions and intentions and will hold them accountable.

translation: They are those who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and turned back the sacrificial animals so that they did not reach their place. And if it had not been for believing men and believing women — whom you did not know — so that you might not trample them and thereby be touched by ignorance, Allah would have admitted into His mercy whom He willed.
